News.title: Hundreds evacuated from UK holiday park in dead of night and major incident declared as fire crews tackle wildfire
News.content:
BLAZE TERROR Hundreds evacuated from UK holiday park in dead of night and major incident declared as fire crews tackle wildfire

HUNDREDS of holidaymakers were evacuated in the middle of the night as a wildfire raced towards a popular seaside resort.

A major incident was declared at Dunwich Heath in Suffolk and 90 firefighters were called to tackle the blaze.



The fire broke out just after 5.30pm yesterday evening and has been spreading rapidly southwest towards Sizewell B nuclear power station.

Crews successfully evacuated Coastguard Cottages, Mount Pleasant Farm and Cliff House Holiday Park and around 200 caravans at the holiday park in the dead of night.



The 14 crews are now working to protect the buildings and 70 firefighters remain at the scene this morning.

It comes as families flock to the Suffolk coast for the summer holidays.

Locals have been urged to avoid the area and keep their windows and doors closed as the wind sends billows of smoke into the sky.

Have you been affected by this? Contact araminta.plumptre@thesun.co.uk

Suffolk Fire and Rescue said the inferno is now a major incident “due to the size and complexity”.



Station manager Dan Davis added that the blaze was a “large-scale, wind-driven forestry fire”.

The nature reserve and several of the holiday lets are owned by the National Trust.

The charity is said to be assisting fire crews from Leiston, Reydon, Halesworth, Beccles, Ipswich East, Ipswich Princes Street, Lowestoft South, Lowestoft North, Stradbroke, Wrentham, Bungay, Saxmundham, Haverhill, Orford, Stowmarket, Felixstowe and Woodbridge.

Firefighters deployed specialist equipment including drones, Unimogs and quadbikes.

The wildfire is close to the RSPB Minsmere nature reserve and heading towards St James’ Church.



The fire around 2.5miles from Sizewell B but is not thought to be a threat to the nuclear power station currently.

Anyone displaced has been told to attend Westleton Village Hall at 08:00am for further updates.

Just hours before the forest fire broke out, Suffolk joined half the country by officially declaring a drought.

The areas are East Anglia, Hertfordshire and the whole of London, Thames Valley, Hampshire and the Isle of Wight, Devon and Cornwall, the West Midlands, and Wessex – covering Dorset, Somerset, Wiltshire and Gloucestershire.

The blaze is one of several major wildfires being tackled across the UK.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Separately, in Scotland, crews said they were making “significant progress” tackling a wildfire in the Cairngorms that broke out two weeks ago.

A number of homes in the remote region were evacuated as plumes of smoke billowed into the sky, and vast swathes of trees, heather and grasslands have been left charred and blackened.

News.title: Nato scrambles fighter jets after ‘Russian missile hits Poland’ as children among 8 dead in Ukraine strikes
News.content:
NATO scrambled fighter jets after a suspected Russian missile crossed into Polish airspace.

The incident came during a deadly overnight assault from Vladimir Putin – which saw two girls, aged five and 12, among eight killed in Ukraine.



Smoke was seen rising from Poland’s Lublin region where a 33ft-wide crater was reportedly found after air raid sirens sounded across the area.

Polish operational command said an “unidentified object” crashed in its territory after multiple missiles were spotted flying close to the border.



One, feared to be a Kh-101 missile launched from a Russian bomber, entered Polish airspace at around 3.30am.

Residents of Targowisko reported a loud explosion as the missile crashed and burned in a field.



Poland’s operational command said in a statement: “At 3.29am, the closest approach was made by one of the objects.

“At 3.40am, an unidentified object was detected in Polish airspace moving westward. An F-16 fighter jet was dispatched to the area to identify and intercept it.



“At 3.46am, before a clear identification could be made, the object disappeared from radar detection.

“To verify and ultimately confirm the radar’s technical indications, an Mi-24 helicopter was dispatched to the area of the last detection.

“The helicopter crew located the probable crash site of the object in an undeveloped area near the town of Tarnawa-Kolonia in the Lublin Voivodeship.”

The crash site sits four miles from Otrocz, which is around 56 miles from the Ukrainian border.

Polish defence minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz said: “Clarification is now underway as to what kind of object fell near the locality of Tarnawa-Kolonia.”



It comes as Ukraine faced another night of drone and missile attacks at the hands of Russia.



President Volodymyr Zelensky had warned Russia was preparing for a “massive attack”.

Two girls, aged five and 12, were among six killed in a village near the central Ukrainian city of Kryvyi Rih.

A ballistic missile is said to have hit a home and sparked a fire, a local official said.

Eight others were injured, including two children.

Zelensky said: “A Russian missile strike in Radushne, Dnipropetrovsk region, killed parents and three children.



“Two more children were rescued alive from the rubble. A regular residential building was completely destroyed by a ballistic missile.

“Dozens of ordinary homes, civilian businesses, and infrastructure facilities have been destroyed and damaged.

“This attack involved more than 70 missiles, and a significant number of them were ballistic. More than 280 attack drones were also used.”

In the capital Kyiv, one person died as multiple blazes broke out in three buildings, according to mayor Vitali Klitschko.

The mayor of Poltava also said one person has died after a Nova Poshta postal terminal had been attacked.



Several other cities were also reported as being under attack by relentless Russian bombing.

It comes as Putin is reportedly set to mobilise half a million men for his war in Ukraine – as the tyrant vows to be “bolder” despite suffering huge losses.

Zelensky said Putin is planning to mobilise the 500,000 troops after legislative elections scheduled for September.

The move is said to be in response to Kyiv’s recent attacks on Russia’s economy.

Ukraine has been putting its foot on Moscow’s neck with a series of strikes crippling the regime’s biggest e-commerce platform.



The devastating strikes on warehouses owned by Wildberries – the country’s biggest online marketplace – have shattered Russian morale.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Over the last few days, Ukraine has destroyed or damaged a series of complexes belonging to the largest e-commerce site in Russia.

And the drone onslaught has thrown Russian daily life into chaos – wiping out local businesses overnight and suffocating small-scale trade.

News.title: Man, 59, arrested after ‘two women sexually assaulted’ at iconic UK festival headlined by Snow Patrol and Red Rum Club
News.content:
FESTIVAL 'ATTACK' Man, 59, arrested after ‘two women sexually assaulted’ at iconic UK festival headlined by Snow Patrol and Red Rum Club

A MAN has been arrested after two women were allegedly sexually assaulted at a popular music festival.

A man reportedly touched the two women inappropriately at On the Waterfront music festival held at the Pier Head in Liverpool.

The flagship festival hosts 40,000 attendees and this year’s headliners included Snow Patrol, Red Rum Club and Paul Weller.

The incidents took place between 9.30pm and 10pm on Thursday 18 June and a 59-year-old man was arrested at the scene.





He has since been released on bail as police make further enquiries.

Merseyside Police have urged the two victims and any other witnesses to come forward.

Detective Inspector Jemma Berry said: “Although our officers made an arrest at the event we are continuing with our enquiries into the incident, and I would appeal to anyone with information to come forward.

“As such, we are appealing for the two victims of the sexual assault to please contact us as a matter of urgency.

“In addition as it was a busy event with thousands of people attending the music festival, we also ask for people who witnessed the incident to please also contact us.

“I would like to reassure the public that incidents such as this are rare, and we are taking this incident extremely seriously.”

Anyone with information can contact the force on social media, through its website or be calling 101 with reference 26000487162.

Anonymous reporting is also available using the charity Crimestoppers.



On the Waterfront is said to be a “flagship music event” which has “quickly become a staple in Liverpool’s cultural calendar,” according to the festival’s website.

Previous headliners include Sting, CHIC, Basement Jaxx and Nile Rogers.

News.title: Boy, 12 plummets to his death from roof after climbing barn with friends
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

TRAGIC FALL Boy, 12 plummets to his death from roof after climbing barn with friends

A 12-YEAR-OLD boy has died after he climbed onto the roof of a barn with friends and fell off.

Jaxon Robert Hubery was raced to hospital with serious injuries after he fell from the building near Bishop Auckland on July 24.

He was treated at Royal Victoria Infirmary in Newcastle but despite best efforts he died on Tuesday.

Durham Police said it is working with the Health and Safety Executive to establish the circumstances of Jaxon’s fall.





A spokesperson for the force said: “His family would like to thank those who have given them love and support throughout the last few days.

“They are also urging other parents to keep their children away from the area.

“Police are working alongside the Health and Safety Executive to establish the circumstances surrounding the incident.“

A spokesperson for North East Ambulance Service previously said: “We were called to a person injured at an address in Woodhouses Bishop Auckland at 2.35pm on July 24.



“We dispatched an ambulance crew, a clinical team leader, a rapid response paramedic and requested support from Great North Air Ambulance Service.

“One patient was taken to hospital by road for further treatment.”

News.title: US launches ‘heavy wave’ of strikes in ‘powerful response’ to Tehran’s surprise attack American troops
News.content:
THE US has completed a “heavy wave” of strikes against Iran in a “powerful response” to the regime’s surprise attack.

Iran’s bloodthirsty Islamic Guards infuriated Donald Trump by unleashing a surprise volley of ballistic missiles at US bases in the Gulf on Tuesday.



The US president retaliated with a bombardment on the embattled regime after pausing tit-for-tat strikes last week to revitalise peace talks.

Announcing the onslaught, US Central Command (Centcom) said they “successfully completed a heavy wave of strikes against Iran in response to yesterday’s attempted missile attacks on US forces”.



Washington struck “dozens” of Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) targets, “including military command centers, missile and drone facilities, coastal surveillance and defense sites, and maritime capabilities”.

The strikes aimed to “further diminish threats posed by Iran and its proxies to American forces, commercial shipping, and neighboring Gulf countries”, Centcom said.



Three people including a child were reportedly killed in attacks on the island of Qeshm – Tehran’s key oil export hub, according to state media.

Explosions were also reported in Khuzestan province to the northwest.



The latest round of attacks came after a few days of peace over the weekend where both sides agreed to restart talks.

But Tehran then launched a wave of strikes at Jordan on Tuesday targeting US forces – breaking the short-lived peace.

The IRGC said its force targeted the US air base and Centcom’s regional headquarters in Jordan with several ballistic missiles.



After reviewing video of Iran’s unsuccessful Tuesday attacks, Trump fumed: “We’ll be hitting them hard.”

“They’re going to get a beating”, he told Fox News on Wednesday.

He also vowed to “beat the f**ing s**t” out of the regime in response to the attacks.

US forces had just minutes to shoot down the incoming missiles overnight, Trump said, with all successfully intercepted.



But renewed violence from both sides now risks a return to full-blown war.

“Resistance will continue” as long as the US military’s “unlawful and malicious” acts against “our interests” persist, the IRGC warned on Wednesday.

American missiles, drones and fighter jets zeroed in on key Iranian port cities in the second phase of the war as they attempt to wrestle back control of the Strait of Hormuz.

The IRGC reignited the conflict by firing at ships in the key trade route on July 7, a few weeks after agreeing a fragile ceasefire by signing a memorandum of understanding (MOU).

The US president threatened on Monday he would get back to “very strong military action” if negotiations fell through.



On Wednesday Trump confirmed negotiations are ongoing despite the new tit-for-tat strikes.

“We’re going to let them keep talking,” he said.

Asked how long he was willing to give Tehran to finalise a peace deal, Trump said: “Not much time.”

He said: “Either it goes fast or not at all.”

Earlier this month in Jordan, two US service members were killed in a missile and drone barrage.



The deadly assaults caused Trump to intensify his two week-long blitz of the regime.

Trump’s decision to row back on planned strikes was caused by a diminished stockpile of Patriot antimissile interceptors, according to the New York Times.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

It comes after the US and Saudi Arabia launched joint strikes on Iran-backed militant groups in Iraq on Tuesday.

American and Saudi fighter jets took out terrorist logistics and weapons sites during the operation.

News.title: Putin charges billionaire ‘supersperm’ donor with aiding terrorism – as ‘Russian Elon Musk’ gives tyrant the finger
News.content:
TELEGRAM boss Pavel Durov faces life behind bars after Russia slapped the billionaire with a terrorism charge – before his app hit back with a savage middle-finger picture.

The 41-year-old tycoon has been placed on an international wanted list as Vladimir Putin’s regime turns the screws on his hugely popular messaging platform.



Russian security services accuse Telegram of allowing channels and bots allegedly used by Ukrainian intelligence agencies, terrorists and extremist groups to plot “acts of sabotage and terrorism, mass murder, and cyberfraud” inside Russia.

Moscow claims the alleged failures have already resulted in “numerous human casualties”.



But Telegram appeared to deliver a brutal two-fingered response after the warrant was issued, sharing a picture of Durov giving the middle finger.

The extraordinary clash comes as Russia wages a relentless crackdown on the encrypted app, which has become a vital communications tool on both sides of the war in Ukraine.

Ukrainian security services have also been accused of using a popular dating chatbot on Telegram to lure Russians into “sabotage and terrorist activities”.

Russian authorities claim 46 users aged between 12 and 22 have been detained across the country since July 2025 in connection with the alleged activity.

Durov has long been a thorn in the Kremlin’s side after refusing to bend to demands for access to users’ data.

The Russian-born billionaire founded VKontakte – a Facebook-inspired social network – with his brother Nikolai in 2006.



The platform quickly became Russia’s biggest social network before Durov spectacularly fell out with authorities over demands to censor content and hand over information.

During the anti-Putin protests of 2011 and 2012, Russian authorities demanded personal data belonging to protest organisers and the closure of opposition groups on VK.

But Durov refused.

Then, in 2014, he was pressured again over his refusal to block a VK group supporting Ukraine’s Euromaidan protests and hand Ukrainian users’ data to the FSB.

He was forced out of VK and soon fled Russia, declaring the country “incompatible with internet business at the moment.”



Durov went on to build Telegram into a global messaging giant, with more than a billion monthly active users and a fierce reputation for privacy.

But the billionaire’s turbulent relationship with authorities followed him west.

He was arrested in Paris in 2024 after arriving from Azerbaijan with his girlfriend Yulia Vavilova, then 24, amid a French investigation into Telegram.



French authorities alleged the app’s lack of moderation, limited cooperation with law enforcement and features including disposable numbers and cryptocurrency made it an accomplice to drug trafficking, paedophilia and fraud.

Durov blasted the investigation as “completely absurd”.

He said: “Just because criminals use our messaging service among many others doesn’t make those who run it criminals.”

He added: “Telegram staff can’t see or read user messages.

“That’s why we’ve never revealed a single private message.”



Durov has also insisted that Telegram only reviews limited metadata, such as an IP address or phone number, when a court flags a user ID in a criminal case.

Now Russia has dramatically escalated the war against him by putting the billionaire on its wanted list and threatening him with life imprisonment if convicted.

The Kremlin has already restricted Telegram access and slapped the company with around $1.26billion in fines since January over allegedly banned content.



Putin’s regime has also launched a sweeping internet clampdown.

Authorities have blocked or restricted major platforms, while tightening the grip on online communications.

Facebook, Instagram and X have been banned, while Signal and Viber have been blocked and WhatsApp restricted.

The explosive Russian case comes after Durov revealed another astonishing threat hanging over his fortune.

The billionaire has drawn up a new will splitting his £17billion fortune equally between his alleged 106 children.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Durov says the children – whether conceived naturally or through sperm donation – will not get their hands on his fortune for 30 years.

He told Le Point magazine: “I want them to live like normal people, to build their lives on their own, to learn to trust themselves, to be able to create – not to be dependent on a bank account.”

News.title: Chilling moment police raid funeral home & find bags of human ashes on floor as officers uncover 30 decomposing bodies
News.content:
THIS is the grim moment cops raided a funeral home and uncovered decomposing bodies, bags of human ashes and grieving families’ items dumped on the floor.

Police bodycam footage shows officers picking through cluttered rooms at Legacy Independent Funeral Directors in Hull, East Yorkshire, after concerns were raised about corpses being kept for years.



The video captures the moment cops discovered what prosecutors later described as a “horror scene”.

More than 100 bags and boxes of ashes can be seen stacked up, with families’ belongings strewn across floors and worktops.



One officer shines her torch into dimly lit side rooms packed with rubbish.

“It’s strange, innit?” she remarks, and at one point an officer says: “There’s, like, urns… where you go pick up…”

Boxes of ashes were piled against walls and in the workshop where Bush made coffins from cheap wood.

Officers uncovered more than 30 decomposing bodies that funeral director Robert Bush falsely claimed had been cremated.



The bodies were found inside a cold storage room at the Hull funeral home after police were called to the Hessle Road site in March 2024.

Images released by cops reveal motorbikes and classic cars that prosecutors say Bush bought using money taken from devastated customers.

Police also released footage showing Bush arguing with detectives after he was arrested for a second time.

He had first been arrested at Heathrow Airport after officers discovered dozens of decomposing bodies inside his funeral home.

Bush complained to officers: “I don’t understand. I’ve been arrested off a plane at gunpoint. It’s like I’m Che Guevara or something.



“I’m not that complicated. I’ve said so many times, ‘Let me help you, I’ll come in and talk to you.’

“I know I’m not good at accounting, me handwriting’s bad and all that, and I’m sure there’s times when you’ve looked at things and gone, ‘I don’t know what that means’.”

During police interviews, detectives challenged Bush over why “25 or so bodies” had never been cremated when they should have been.



Bush replied: “The debt started to accrue. The level of cash flow problems that I was having… It presented an opportunity that I did not have to maybe do it immediately.

“If I held on to the bodies for a little bit and back-filled another one and catch up. But I didn’t catch up.”

The full scale of the horror has emerged during Bush’s sentencing hearing at Hull Crown Court – where more than 80 victims or their relatives described how their lives were shattered.

The court heard he spent more than £42,000 on holidays while defrauding scores of grieving families.

Bush also splashed out £9,000 on camping in 2022.



That same year, he failed to cremate Jasmine Beverley’s unborn baby, Sunny Beverley-Conlin, leaving the baby’s body in a paper bag on the floor of the funeral home.

Financial records showed that between 2017 and 2024, Bush spent £21,000 on motorcycle racing and £17,400 on home improvements.

Prosecutors said he pocketed customers’ money for funeral plans he was not authorised to provide before handing some families the wrong ashes.



His spending spree included £6,400 on three Centre Parcs trips, £3,800 on a holiday to Italy and £3,000 on the Arizona break he was enjoying with his daughter when the scandal was uncovered.

Almost £10,000 of retail spending included £1,000 at Boodles jewellers and £3,385 in restaurants, the court heard.

Prosecutor Steven Ball said almost £1.49million was transferred from Legacy Funeral Directors’ business accounts into Bush’s personal bank account between March 2017 and April 2024.

Jurors heard more than £3million passed through Bush’s and the firm’s accounts during that period, but the turnover reported to Companies House and HMRC did not reflect the true figures.

The court was told the shocking discovery happened by chance while Bush was holidaying in Arizona.



Bush had asked Gary Pickering and Steve Emmerson, directors of Evergreen Funeral Directors, to recover a body for him while he was away.

Legacy worker Patrick Moore helped the pair before revealing Bush had warned him “not to bring anyone back to Legacy or help put a body into the fridge area”.

Mr Moore then told the funeral directors: “You two don’t know the half of it, bodies have been there for years.”



Alarmed by the claim, Mr Emmerson later rang Mr Moore and asked how many bodies were inside the premises.

After counting them, Mr Moore estimated there were 29 bodies, describing the scene as something from a “horror scene”.

Police were called to the Hessle Road funeral home in March 2024 and discovered 35 bodies along with more than 100 sets of ashes.

Bush since admitted 30 counts of preventing a lawful and decent burial, theft from 12 charities and 30 counts of fraud by false representation relating to bodies found at the premises.

He also pleaded guilty to four fraud offences involving unborn babies, after falsely telling grieving mothers ashes he handed over were “the remains of their unborn”.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Bush further admitted fraud involving the ashes of 57 people between 2017 and 2024, along with a charge of fraudulent trading linked to funeral plans sold between 2012 and 2024.

He is due to be sentenced at Hull Crown Court later this week.

News.title: How to save exhausted bumble bees and four other ways to help creatures in your garden suffering in the heatwave
News.content:
BEE KIND How to save exhausted bumble bees and four other ways to help creatures in your garden suffering in the heatwave

WHILE we battle through heatwaves by jumping into paddling pools and stocking up on ice lollies, the country’s wildlife has no such luxury.

As our gardens bake, experts warn that birds, hedgehogs and other wildlife are being left exhausted, dehydrated and struggling to find food.



The RSPCA says that rescue centres are “fit to bursting” and it is facing a growing hedgehog crisis after seeing a sharp rise in admissions so far this summer.

In June alone, shortly after the first heatwave of 2026 hit, more than 315 hedgehogs were treated at the charity’s four wildlife centres – that is up 56 per cent from the same month last year.



Experts say making a few simple changes in your garden can provide a vital lifeline to Britain’s wildlife. From leaving out fresh water to resisting the urge to mow every inch of lawn, we reveal how you can help.

SPOT THE WARNING SIGNS: If you see a hedgehog out and about during the day, you may think it’s really cute — but it could actually be a cry for help.



Rebecca Machin, scientific and policy officer at RSPCA Wildlife, says: “People need to be aware of the warning signs that animals might be in danger.

“If you see hedgehogs out in the day, that is unusual in itself but if they are staggering, they may need help. It’s the same if you see a bird panting.”

Rebecca reveals there are lots of things people can do to give wild animals a helping hand.

“If a bee is exhausted and can’t move, you can help by putting them back on to a flower,” she explains.



“Or, if you see small frogs emerging from a pond on to concrete, there is a risk of them sticking, so usher them back in.”

FOOD FOR THOUGHT: Just like humans, animals get thirsty in hot weather but sustenance is often harder to come by.

Forget fancy feeders, though — you might already have the perfect wildlife treat sitting in your cupboard.

After one of the driest summers on record, many animals are struggling to dig worms — their primary source of food — out of the hard soil.



But pet food makes an excellent substitute.

Rebecca says: “Regular wet cat or dog food can be great for badgers and hedgehogs, but make sure you leave it out at night so the neighbors’ pets don’t steal it.”

DOWN TOOLS: Leaving your lawnmower in the shed could be the key to helping wildlife this summer.

Beccy Speight, chief executive of the RSPB, says: “From birds taking refuge in hedges and dense shrubs, to longer grass giving butterflies and insects shelter from the heat, overgrown areas in the garden can provide respite.



Letting the lawn grow a little longer or allowing leaf piles to build up will also provide invertebrates and amphibians with cool, damp areas.”

Experts also recommend creating some shady areas with pebbles or logs in the corner of your garden.

DRINK IT IN: As temperatures soar, we won’t be the only ones searching for the nearest watering hole this summer.

Birds, hedgehogs, bees and butterflies all need access to fresh water to stay hydrated.

Beccy says: “Providing clean water for drinking and bathing all year round is one of the simplest ways to help garden wildlife.



“During the summer, it’s even more of a lifeline, especially with the heatwaves and the likelihood of more dry weather ahead.”

It is not as simple as sticking a bowl of water out in the garden, though.

Beccy explains: “People are being encouraged to provide clean water in a bird bath, pond or shallow dish.

“Adding a few stones around the edge can help butterflies and insects perch safely while drinking, while also making it easier for species such as hedgehogs, frogs and toads to access the water.

“However, hygiene is essential.



“Bird baths should be emptied and refilled daily and cleaned and disinfected every week to help prevent disease spreading between birds.”

DON’T SPARK TROUBLE: Experts warn that many animals’ natural habitats are in danger this summer after months of no significant rain.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Zoe Quiroz Cullen, head of climate and international policy at The Wildlife Trusts, says: “With many of our landscapes already dry, there is a real risk of wildfire across the UK.

“Remember to clear away all your rubbish, leave your barbecue at home in favour of packing a picnic, and carefully discard any cigarette butts to avoid starting an accidental fire.”

News.title: France wildfires live: Emergency response chief says 'all of Europe' could be engulfed
News.content:
Wildfires have ravaged large parts of Spain and France and the head of the EU's Emergency Response Co-ordination Centre has warned that other countries could be next

France wildfires live: Emergency response chief says 'all of Europe' could be engulfed

Europe's emergency response chief has warned that the continent could be engulfed if wildfires continue.

Maria Zuber, head of the EU's Emergency Response Co-ordination Centre, said wildfires could engulf "all of Europe" within days. Her warning comes as wildfires ravage France, Spain, Greece and Portugal.

"The next risk, it's already moving to Greece and also Central Europe," she told reporters yesterday. "Greece for the moment was spared, and now we see that it will go to Greece."

"Italy will face risk at the beginning of August, and we will need to see what will happen with the Iberian Peninsula, because if (it is) there as well, we will have all Europe on fire."

It comes as three firefighters lost their lives while tackling wildfires in Greece as high winds have seen blazes spread across Crete and mainland Greece after days of devastation elsewhere on the continent.

News.title: Neurologist issues warning about common 'deadly' food you've probably got in the cupboard
News.content:
Neurologist issues warning about common 'deadly' food you've probably got in the cupboard

A brain health expert has named the everyday item lurking in millions of kitchen cupboards that he refuses to go near — and the reason why could save your life.

View 3 Images The popular food is bought by many every week (Image: Laurence Berger via Getty Images)

Most of us don't give a second thought to the tins and cans stacked in our kitchen cupboards. They're convenient, long-lasting and always there. But according to one neurologist, a damaged can could be harbouring one of the most lethal toxins known to man — and you'd have no way of knowing until it was too late.

‌



Dr Baibing Chen, a double-board certified neurologist widely known on social media as Dr Bing, has made it his mission to translate complex brain science into everyday advice. With a medical degree from Shanghai Jiao Tong University, a residency at the University of Mississippi, and fellowships at both Emory University and the University of Mississippi, he is well placed to know what poses a genuine risk to the human brain.

‌



In a video shared on TikTok and Instagram, Dr Bing revealed three foods he would never personally eat as a neurologist. One of them — damaged tinned or canned food — shocked many of his followers, and the reason is alarming.

‌



View 3 Images Tin cans that are heavily dented or damaged can be very dangerous (Image: Getty)

What makes a damaged tin so dangerous?

A minor scuff from a supermarket shelf is one thing, but Dr Bing warns that certain types of damage are a serious red flag.

He said: "If a can is bulging, cracked or severely dented, that's a red flag for botulinum contamination.

‌



"This bacteria produces botulinum toxin, which is one of the most potent toxins that we know. And just a small amount can block acetylcholine release at the neuromuscular junction, meaning your brain can't tell your muscles to move."

In plain terms, the toxin essentially cuts off communication between the brain and the muscles with devastating consequences.

What makes botulinum toxin especially terrifying is that it offers no warning. It is completely tasteless and odourless, meaning contaminated food looks, smells and tastes entirely normal. By the time symptoms begin to emerge, the toxin has already taken hold.

‌



Even cooking the food offers little reassurance. Dr Bing warned that heating contaminated food before eating it may not be enough to destroy the toxin, so the standard assumption that "cooking kills bacteria" does not necessarily apply here.

The health consequences can be severe. Dr Bing warned that botulinum toxin exposure can lead to flaccid paralysis, blurred vision, respiratory failure, and even death if the patient is not treated promptly with an antitoxin.

View 3 Images Many of us will buy this food weekly (Image: Getty)

‌



What is botulism and how does it develop?

Botulism is a rare but potentially fatal illness caused by the toxin produced by the bacterium Clostridium botulinum. The Food Standards Agency (FSA) explains that foodborne botulism occurs when a person consumes food that already contains the toxin - most commonly because the food has not been properly canned, preserved or cooked during the manufacturing process.

The bacterium thrives in low-oxygen environments, which is why improperly sealed or damaged cans create such ideal conditions for it to flourish. A bulging can, for instance, is often a sign that gas has built up inside as a result of bacterial activity — a clear signal that something has gone dangerously wrong.

Should you be worried about cans from UK supermarkets?

The good news is that the UK has some of the strictest food hygiene standards in the world. The FSA says that the risk of contracting foodborne botulism from food purchased in this country is considered 'low', thanks to rigorous production and safety controls applied throughout the supply chain.

‌



That said, the FSA fully supports the advice Dr Bing has been sharing with his online following. It stresses that consumers should avoid eating food from any can that is bulging, heavily rusted or deeply dented – regardless of where it was purchased, including major supermarkets.

The agency also advises that if you have any doubt about whether food has been correctly preserved or packaged, if you are unsure about the use-by date, or if the product has not been stored properly, you should not eat it. Instead, dispose of it safely in the bin.

What else does Dr Bing avoid for his brain health?

Also in the video, Dr Bing says he avoids eating reef fish, like groupers and barracuda, because they can also carry a neurotoxin that can cause tingling in the body, dizziness and recurring nightmares. It can also lead to chronic neuropathies.

Article continues below

He also tries to avoid eating undercooked pork, especially from unregulated sources. This can sometimes cause a kind of tapeworm that is one of the leading causes of acquired epilepsy in the world.

News.title: Police launch murder investigation after bodies of five babies found in boxes in flat
News.content:
Police launch murder investigation after bodies of five babies found in boxes in flat

French detectives have opened a murder inquiry after the remains of five babies were found inside an apartment in the town of Orange

View 3 Images The entrance of an appartment in Orange, southern France (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

A police investigation is under way in southern France after the remains of five infants were discovered inside a family apartment following the birth of another baby.

‌



The investigation began after a 32-year-old man reportedly found what appeared to be human remains while searching the home he shared with his partner in Orange. The discovery came shortly after she had given birth at home before being taken to hospital.

‌



Prosecutors have since confirmed that officers recovered the skeletal remains of four infants along with the decomposing body of a fifth newborn from the couple's flat in the historic centre of the town. An investigation has been opened into the "murder of a minor under the age of 15", while forensic examinations continue.

‌



The Carpentras public prosecutor's office said the woman's partner became concerned after learning, at a very late stage, that she had once again been pregnant and had given birth at home before later being admitted to hospital. Prosecutors said he had been "disturbed by the discovery, once again very late in the pregnancy, that his companion had given birth at home the day before being taken to the hospital."

He then searched the apartment and found "what appeared to be human remains", reports the Irish Mirror.

After notifying Orange hospital, medical staff alerted prosecutors, prompting a police search of the property on Monday evening. A forensic pathologist's initial assessment concluded that the remains recovered included the skeletons of four infants and the decomposing body of a fifth baby.

‌



View 3 Images The French police seals affixed to the door of an appartment in Orange (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

An autopsy has been ordered on the newborn's body, while specialists will carry out anthropological examinations on the skeletal remains as investigators work to establish the circumstances surrounding the deaths.

Initial reports said the woman had recently given birth to a healthy baby after previously denying she was pregnant. Prosecutors have also confirmed that the latest birth followed another pregnancy that was not discovered until a very late stage.

‌



The 32-year-old mother remained in hospital after giving birth and was not immediately questioned by police. However, on Wednesday, 29 July, prosecutors confirmed she had been taken into police custody. Responsibility for the investigation has also been transferred to the Avignon prosecutor's office.

Her partner, who is also 32, voluntarily spoke to investigators during the early stages of the inquiry. Prosecutors said he told officers he had been "completely unaware of his partner's pregnancies."

He has since been released without charge.

‌



The couple also have two children, aged eight and nine. Child Welfare Services has been asked to carry out an urgent assessment of the family's circumstances, while the healthy baby boy born on Sunday has been placed in temporary care pending a hearing before a juvenile court judge.

View 3 Images The French police seals affixed to the door of an appartment in Orange, southern France (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

The family lived on the second floor of an old building close to Orange's ancient Roman theatre. By Tuesday morning, police seals bearing the words "murder of a minor under the age of 15" had been placed on the apartment door.

‌



Neighbours said they were stunned by the investigation. Florent Jean, who lives nearby, described the family as "charming people" who had moved into the building around two years ago.

Recalling the emergency response on Sunday, he said: "I thought to myself: Is she pregnant? That's impossible. She was so thin."

He added that the woman "would pick the children up from school at lunchtime for a meal", while her partner "would go to work in the morning and come back in the evening, just normal people, really."

Article continues below

Investigators are continuing to establish exactly what happened to the five infants. Prosecutors have indicated that although the current legal classification is the "murder of a minor under the age of 15", the offence under investigation could change as further forensic evidence is examined.

The case has inevitably drawn comparisons with previous infanticide investigations in France. In the country's most notorious case, Dominique Cottrez was convicted of killing eight newborn babies whose bodies were discovered in 2010. She was sentenced to nine years in prison in 2015 after the court accepted that her judgement had been impaired.

News.title: 'Taliban tortured my dad and threatened to take my sister after MoD data breach'
News.content:
'Taliban tortured my dad and threatened to take my sister after MoD data breach'

An interpreter who worked for the British Army in Helmand Province, Afghanistan, in 2012 has told of his trauma after names were leaked amid a Ministry of Defence breach

View 4 Images Afghans who worked with UK forces spent years fearing for their lives following data breach (Image: Getty Images)

A former Afghan interpreter who worked for the British Army has told how his father was tortured after their names were leaked in a Ministry of Defence blunder.

‌



He said the Taliban raided his parents' home and threatened to take one of his sisters if he didn’t send them money from the UK.

‌



The interpreter, who asked not to be named as he still has relatives in Afghanistan, worked for the Army in Helmand Province in 2012. He said: “I worked for them (the British Army) because I hoped they would help the Afghan government improve my country.”

‌



After British forces officially ended combat operations in 2014, the interpreter stayed in his home country to be close to his parents and seven sisters.

Iran issues chilling warning to Ukraine after attack on ship on Caspian Sea READ MORE :

US announces third service member killed in two days as Iran bombardment continues READ MORE :

View 4 Images British soldiers were part of the Helmand Task Force (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

But he explained: “In 2021 the situation was getting worse. The Taliban was capturing province after province. I knew I couldn’t live in that country anymore. I was receiving threats.”

‌



He applied and was accepted for resettlement in the UK with his wife, but before they could leave the Afghan government collapsed on August 15.

With the Taliban at the gates of Kabul he had to wait at the airport until he managed to board a flight out on August 24 - leaving his family behind.

Once in the UK he applied for his family to be able to join him, receiving confirmation at the end of 2022. By then, there had already been the data breach - accidentally releasing the names of 18,000 people, putting them at risk from the Taliban.

‌



View 4 Images British forces were mentoring the Afghan National Army (Image: Getty Images)

He said: “I do not know if the Taliban had my data or not, but they know who my family was. Our house was looted and searched by the Taliban many times.

“My father was arrested and tortured for two weeks. They were asking for money. They wanted me to send money or they would take one of my sisters. For my father, a 65-year-old man, it was not easy.”

‌



His parents and three of his sisters were eventually resettled in the UK in May 2024. Another sister had already been allowed into the country with her husband who also worked with the Army. His three other sisters have remained in Afghanistan with their husbands.

He said: “They are here now, but it cost three years of depression and trauma. It has affected my mother very badly. They were calling me saying ‘why are you not doing anything?’ All I could say was ‘I’m trying, it’s not in my control’.”

The interpreter said he still knows of people who helped the British forces and other agencies who remain in Afghanistan, adding: “I know of one person who worked in anti-corruption who has arrived here, he was a judge. But I know of another who is still in Afghanistan.”

‌



He also said he knew of Afghan special forces soldiers - known as the “Triples” - who fought alongside the British military who hadn’t been allowed to resettle in the UK.

View 4 Images British forces on operations in Afghanistan (Image: Philip Coburn/Daily Mirror)

The interpreter spoke out as the cross-party defence committee released a damning report into the data breach. Chairman Tan Dhesi said: “This inquiry began with a data breach, but became about the real lives affected by delay, secrecy and flawed decision-making.

‌



"The government must now explain how it will protect eligible Afghans who cannot safely, lawfully or affordably reach a third country for UK entry-clearance checks.”

Sara de Jong, co-founder of the Sulha Alliance, which offers help for former interpreters and their families in the UK, said: “I welcome the Report’s critical assessment of the Government's actions and its recognition of the human costs for Afghans affected by the data breach.

“These human costs, from physical threats to psychological harm, are more significant than the Government initially accepted, as I know from daily contact with affected Afghans and from our survey research among 231 Afghans affected by the data breach, conducted with the NGO Refugee Legal Support.”

Article continues below

Sara, also Professor of Politics at the University of York, who contributed to the select committee’s investigation, added: “We are currently in contact with several desperate Afghan interpreters and Triples who are still at risk and abandoned in Afghanistan, because they don’t have the financial means to self-move.

“So we are grateful that the Committee has demanded that the Government explains how it will protect eligible Afghans who cannot safely, lawfully or affordably reach a neighbouring country for their UK visa processing. Almost 5 years since the withdrawal in August 2021, it is time to finally finish this mission of bringing those who stood by the British Army to safety.”

News.title: 'I was healthy then diagnosis 10 days after birth blindsided me'
News.content:
'I was healthy then diagnosis 10 days after birth blindsided me'

Rebecca Robinson said it had robbed her of time with her newborn daughter

View 4 Images Rebecca during treatment (Image: PA Real Life)

A first-time mother whose tiredness and bleeding gums were thought to be “common pregnancy symptoms” has said she felt “completely blindsided” when she was given a shock diagnosis 10 days after giving birth.

‌



Rebecca Robinson, 33, a product manager who lives in Leeds with her husband James, experienced fatigue during pregnancy in 2024, but when a blood test flagged low iron at 28 weeks, her midwife was not concerned. When her gums started bleeding in the final weeks of pregnancy, Rebecca said her dentist told her it was perfectly normal and nobody had any suspicions that there was anything seriously wrong.

‌



However, just 10 days after giving birth, Rebecca was told she had acute myeloid leukaemia (AML) – a fast-growing type of blood cancer – and she needed to start treatment within two days, leaving her in “complete shock”. She said she was “robbed” of time with her newborn while undergoing treatment for six months, but now, two years in remission, she is finally able to be “a normal mum”.

‌



“I felt hugely guilty for Annabel because that’s not the life that I wanted her to have,” Rebecca said. “I wanted to be able to go to baby classes with her and just have the maternity leave away from work, and my reality was completely different. I just felt robbed… but luckily, I got into remission after the first round (of chemotherapy) and I’ve stayed in remission ever since.”

View 4 Images Rebecca said she was ‘robbed’ of time with her newborn while undergoing treatment (Image: PA Real Life)

Rebecca explained that she was “completely healthy” prior to her cancer diagnosis. She said she “never went to the doctors”, but at 28 weeks pregnant, she had a routine blood test which flagged low iron levels.

‌



“It’s super common in pregnancy, so I was put on iron tablets. I didn’t think anything of it at all,” she said.

Rebecca experienced fatigue as well but, given this was her first pregnancy, she assumed it was simply “pregnancy tiredness”. She was able to continue working up until 38 weeks, but at 40 weeks, she started experiencing bleeding gums and noticed a “little lump on (her) gum”.

According to the NHS, many pregnant women get a condition called pregnancy gingivitis, where the gums become swollen, red and tender, and they may bleed when brushing or flossing. While Rebecca knew this was a “common pregnancy symptom”, she decided to visit the dentist “to get it checked out”.

‌



“The dentist said: ‘Oh, it’s just an infection, but there’s no point in giving you antibiotics because you’re 40 weeks pregnant. Of course, your gums are going to be bleeding’,” she said.

On April 26, 2024, during labour, Rebecca said she requested an epidural – an injection in the back to help relieve pain – and doctors took blood samples, which revealed her platelets were low. Just hours after delivery, Rebecca developed a high temperature and was kept in hospital for eight days, where she had blood tests every day to monitor her levels.

She said: “It wasn’t until I had my blood test during labour that doctors said: ‘No, something crazy is happening’.”

‌



While doctors did not think Rebecca had sepsis or a retained placenta, when part or all of the placenta and membranes are left in the womb after childbirth, she said they wanted to “test (her) for everything”. After her temperature returned to a normal level and remained there for 24 hours, she was discharged from hospital and was told to monitor her symptoms and return in six weeks for repeated blood tests.

View 4 Images Rebecca with her husband before her diagnosis (Image: PA Real Life)

However, two days later – 10 days after giving birth – she was called back into hospital for a bone marrow biopsy and was told to bring an overnight bag. While cuddling her newborn baby on May 7, she was given the news that she had AML – and she felt “completely blindsided”.

‌



“They took me into a room and said: ‘You’ve got leukaemia. We’re going to do a biopsy today to work out exactly what’s what, but you’ll be in for six weeks and you’ll have to stop breastfeeding because the chemo will make your milk toxic’,” she explained. “It all just felt very out of the blue.”

According to the charity Leukaemia Care, leukaemia and other blood cancers can cause vague symptoms. Some of the more common symptoms can include feeling exhausted, bruising easily, unusual bleeding such as nosebleeds or bleeding gums, infections, fever and joint or bone pain. Initially, Rebecca said she was “in denial” about her diagnosis, but after some time to process it, she felt grateful that doctors had “found it during labour”.

Looking back on her bleeding gums, she said: “I could have gone to 1,000 dentists and probably not one of them would have thought (it was) leukaemia because I was so heavily pregnant and it’s such a common pregnancy symptom.”

‌



Rebecca started chemotherapy two days after her diagnosis and said the treatment meant she could not breastfeed, attend baby classes or spend quality time with her daughter during her first six months of life.

“It just felt so unfair,” she said. “You’ve spent nine months psyching yourself up for this experience and then it was just completely taken away.”

Rebecca said she reached remission after the first round of chemotherapy, but she continued to have three more rounds, ending in November 2024, and she did not require a stem cell transplant. She now has biopsies every three months, with two more left on her current treatment plan, and she feels extremely “lucky” to be alive.

‌



She “loves being a mum” and is enjoying “making up all the time that (she) lost” with Annabel. Rebecca said her cancer journey has taught her that “everything is temporary” and that “anything can change”, and she is urging others to get any unusual symptoms checked and to advocate for themselves.

View 4 Images Rebecca before her diagnosis (Image: PA Real Life)

“Now I’m near the end, I keep thinking: ‘Oh my God, I can’t believe that actually happened to me and I actually survived it’,” she said.

‌



“It was unlucky that my gene mutated, but it was lucky that the treatment worked, and I know that it is just chance. It’s just a game of chance and I’ve just won on this occasion.”

She added: “To anyone diagnosed, just know that it’s all temporary and you can make a full recovery. That is the story I wish that I would have seen two years ago when I was lying in bed with a newborn. I wish I could have just found a story like mine and thought: ‘That’s going to be me’.”

Colin Dyer, chief executive of Leukaemia Care, said: “Rebecca’s story is a powerful reminder that leukaemia can strike at any stage of life – even during pregnancy. Every symptom she experienced had a perfectly innocent explanation, and that is exactly what makes this disease so difficult to catch. We are so grateful to Rebecca for sharing her experience and helping to show others that if something doesn’t feel right, it is always worth asking for a blood test.”

Article continues below

To find out more about Leukaemia Care’s ‘Spot Leukaemia’ campaign, visit leukaemiacare.org.uk/get-involved/spot-leukaemia

News.title: Voting opens in biggest ever by-election to replace Andy Burnham as Greater Manchester Mayor
News.content:
Voting opens in biggest ever by-election to replace Andy Burnham as Greater Manchester Mayor

Bev Craig insisted Greater Manchester's 'best days are still ahead of us' as polling stations opened at 7am on Thursday in the mayoral contest triggered by Andy Burnham's Westminster comeback

View 2 Images Voting has opened in the Greater Manchester mayoral by-election (Image: Peter Byrne/PA Wire)

Labour's candidate to succeed Andy Burnham as Mayor of Greater Manchester in the country’s biggest ever by-election has promised voters she won’t let them down.

‌



Bev Craig insisted the region’s “best days are still ahead of us” as polling stations opened at 7am on Thursday in the mayoral contest that was triggered last month.

‌



But as the party fights Reform UK, she added: “Only if we keep moving forward together, face up to our biggest challenges, and make life better for everyone. That's why, today, I am asking for you to choose hope and vote Labour.”

‌



Speaking on the eve of the vote, Ms Craig, who has led Manchester City Council since 2021, said: “With such a big by-election, all indications are that it could be close. That’s why it’s more important than ever that you get out and vote. Today – I hope that you will put your trust in me, and vote Labour. I promise I will not let you down.”

Around two million people are eligible to vote in the contest today — making it the biggest by-election the country has ever seen.

The DIY SOS star turned Reform Manchester mayor hopeful who wants Green voters to house rapists READ MORE :

View 2 Images Labour's candidate for Greater Manchester Mayor, Bev Craig, has promised not to let voters down (Image: Getty Images)

‌



It was triggered after Mr Burnham resigned from the role of Greater Manchester Mayor last month following his victory in the Makerfield parliamentary by-election, paving the way for his bid for Downing Street.

Nigel Farage’s Reform UK had been hoping to cause a major political upset in Greater Manchester - a Labour heartland - and were expected to pour resources into the region. They picked Sian Astley, who has been on DIY SOS and led the party’s group on Manchester City Council, to fight for the party.

But Reform chief Mr Farage’s attention has been diverted to his own Clacton by-election where he is facing comedy candidates including Count Binface after political rivals accused him of a political stunt and announced they were boycotting the contest. And according to the most recent polling Ms Craig looks set for a comfortable victory - despite a reduced share of the vote.

‌



Labour overtakes Reform in two major polls while Nigel Farage argues with a bin READ MORE :

Ahead of polling stations opening on Thursday, the new PM Mr Burnham also urged voters to back Ms Craig, who he said will make sure “every town, every borough” shares in the region’s success.

He said: “After years working alongside Bev Craig, I have no doubt that she will work every single day to build on the progress we’ve all made together.”

“Bev will focus on putting more money in your pocket, giving families more breathing space on the cost of living, and making sure young people across every borough have the opportunities they need to thrive.

Article continues below

“Bev will do this by working in lockstep with every community across our city region so we can shape our future together. She is the only candidate who will make sure every town, every borough, and every person shares in Greater Manchester’s success. Together, for our future, vote Bev Craig today to be our next Mayor of Greater Manchester.”

Voting in the contest will close at 10pm with the result expected to be announced on Friday afternoon.

News.title: Father-to-be plunges to his death during freak accident while rock climbing
News.content:
Father-to-be plunges to his death during freak accident while rock climbing

Andy Paul Ferrarone, 33, was climbing in in California when he slipped on a rocky slope, plummeting about 20ft and suffering severe head trauma. He sadly died three days later as a result of his injuries

View 3 Images Andy Paul Ferrarone, 33, with his wife Nina, Ferrarone (Image: GoFundMe)

A father-to-be has tragically died during a freak accident while rock climbing in California.

‌



Andy Paul Ferrarone, 33, was climbing near Castle Rock in Big Bear on July 12 when tragedy struck. At around 5.25pm local time he slipped on a rocky slope, plummeting about 20ft and suffering severe head trauma, police said.

‌



San Bernardino County Sheriff's Aviation Unit raced to the scene and started CPR before he was air lifted to Loma Linda University Medical Center. He spent days on life support before he sadly died on July 15.

‌



View 3 Images Ferrarone was an avid adventurer with passions that stretched far beyond rock climbing, including snowboarding, tennis, photography, sailing, and art. (Image: GoFundMe)

Teenage girl fights for life after joyride in allegedly stolen car ends in Langwarrin crash READ MORE :

He is survived by his wife, Nina, who is nine weeks pregnant.

A GoFundMe page has been set up in order to raise funds for Nina during this difficult time. A message ont he fundraising page reads: "Nina is 8 weeks pregnant, and while she bravely committed to keep the baby, she now faces the challenge of preparing for parenthood alone.

‌



"As a flight attendant, Nina took time off work when she learned she was expecting, and now she must navigate rent, a mountain of medical bills, and the costs of welcoming a child without Andy by her side.

View 3 Images The soon-to-be father was raised in Philadelphia and became 'an accomplished and widely respected software engineer,' according to his obituary. (Image: GoFundMe)

"Donations will help Nina cover Andy’s life support medical bills, pay rent, and purchase essential baby supplies and necessities for her first year of motherhood. Your support will give Nina a chance to keep the home she and Andy made in San Diego, and ease the financial burden left in the wake of Andy’s passing.

Article continues below

"Andy and Nina were known for their warmth and outgoing spirit, and the love they shared touched everyone around them. By helping Nina, you honor Andy’s memory and ensure his legacy lives on through their baby."

So far just over $58,000 has been raised via the fundraising page.

You can donate to the GoFundMe page by clicking here.

News.title: Cooler conditions on the way for parts of UK - but still no rain for drought-hit areas
News.content:
Cooler conditions and some rain are on the way for parts of UK on Thursday into the weekend, as a cold front moves into the UK.

However, with more than half of England and parts of Wales officially in drought, the coming days are unlikely to bring any rain to the driest areas of the country.

The latest UK heatwave peaked on Wednesday with temperatures soaring to 35.2C at Writtle in Essex. It was the hottest day for more than two weeks, when 35.2C was also recorded in Cotton in the Elms, Derbyshire, on 10 July.

It did not reach the highs experienced last month, when a new UK June temperature record of 38C was set at Lingwood in Norfolk on the 26th, which was also the hottest day of the year so far.

Last month's record was provisionally reported as 37.7C but the Met Office announced on Wednesday a new figure of 38.0C following a verification process.

It comes after drought was declared across more than half of England on Wednesday as hot, dry weather takes its toll on the country's water supplies.

The Environment Agency (EA) announcement covered much of central, eastern and southern England, and was a public sign that further restrictions on water use might follow.

It added that the impacts are already being felt, including low river flows, early harvests and high risk of wildfires. More than 20 million people are already under hosepipe bans.

North Wales and the Upper Severn river basin entered drought conditions last week, Natural Resources Wales said.

Scotland does not declare drought but monitors "water scarcity". Some parts of eastern Scotland are in the most extreme category of "significant scarcity", according to the Scottish Environment Protection Agency.

Northern Ireland is not currently in drought.

News.title: How the UK's extreme heat is shifting the conversation about air-con
News.content:
Against him stand those who think Britain's hostility to cooling has curdled into a type of masochism.

David Lawrence, of the Centre for British Progress think tank, puts it plainly: we don't tell people to insulate their homes in winter and then skip the radiators. So why insist shade and shutters are enough in summer?

He points out that air conditioning is standard now in offices, hotels and shops, "but we don't expect it for schools and hospitals - which is kind of odd, because those are places where millions of people are every day", and where heat measurably dents concentration, learning and health.

This dispute over the pros and cons of the technology is becoming political.

Some London councils, following a planning "cooling hierarchy", say lowâenergy ways of keeping homes cool should be prioritised over air conditioning and in a small number of cases have ordered property owners to remove them; the Conservative front bench calls it "dark ages" miserabilism; other MPs and political commentators demand an "air-con revolution".

Since April, in England and Wales the Boiler Upgrade Scheme has offered Â£2,500 towards a reversible air-air heat pump: a machine that warms a home in winter and cools it in summer. It is, in all but name, Britain's first air-conditioning subsidy - but it is badged as a heat pump, and only worth a third of the Â£7,500 for a heating-only model.

Such has been the silence around this grant, that in its first month only around 45 households claimed it. By comparison, the numbers claiming a heating-only model ran into the thousands.

In Scotland homeowners can also get a Â£7,500 grant for a heat pump via its Home Energy scheme - but for air-air versions that could offer cooling there is no funding at all. And in Northern Ireland there is no universal heat pump grant offered for households.

Under the terms of the England and Wales scheme, some people cannot apply at all. It is closed to social housing and newbuilds - which many argue shuts out the very people most exposed.

Take Woolwich, in south-east London, where a resident called Keisha says her top-floor flat reaches 43C in a heatwave.

She calls the building "inhumane"; she and around twenty neighbours in Canada Court and Clifton Lodge are taking their landlord, the housing association PA Housing, to court over homes they say are unfit to live in.

News.title: Homes and caravan park evacuated due to major heath fire in Suffolk
News.content:
The fire service said it had been working to protect properties including Coastguard Cottages, Mount Pleasant Farm and Cliff House Holiday Park, but all had been evacuated overnight.

Up to 200 caravans are being prepared for evacuation, but the exact number of people affected is not known.

The fire comes as the UK Health Security Agency has issued an amber heat-health alert for the East Midlands, the East, South East and London.

The Environment Agency (EA) announced on Wednesday that the East of England, including Suffolk, was part of an area in England where drought was declared.

Droughts bring with them a high risk of wildfires, the EA warned.

Much of the area is a nature reserve owned by the National Trust, which said it was assisting firefighters.

The area is also close to the RSPB Minsmere nature reserve.

Both National Trust Dunwich Heath and the nature reserve have been closed.

It asked people to avoid Westleton Heath, Mount Pleasant, Westleton Walks and the main bridleway from the entrance road towards Dunwich.

The fire service said crews are using equipment including off-road vehicles, drones and quad bikes.

"Members of the public are advised to avoid the area and keep roads clear for emergency vehicles," it said.
