Sports.title: England fans lead calls for 3 Lions to boycott World Cup as fury grows at Fifa plan & emergency UEFA meeting planned
Sports.content:
FANS are calling on England to boycott the World Cup amid fury at Fifa’s plot to sell off the tournament.

If stakes in the event are flogged as planned it would allow Fifa president Gianni Infantino and his US pals to funnel millions from the sport.



Furious fans say the move is all about greed and that Infantino “must be stopped”.

Europe’s governing body Uefa is set to hold emergency talks as its 55-strong bloc considers a tough response, which could lead to a mass boycott.



England’s FA is leading the opposition, saying its leaders are “deeply concerned about the lack of process” in the plot by world football chiefs Fifa to create a private company to run its competitions.

Three Lions fans were fleeced by Infantino’s obscene ticket prices as the team reached the semi-final at this summer’s tournament.

They have urged the FA to call his bluff after he issued an ultimatum to all Fifa member associations.

He has offered a one-off £30million payment to each of the 211 Fifa nations — provided they sign up to his new deal within 53 days.

He intends to create a tournament organisation called Fifa Forward Enterprise and is believed to be planning for the World Cup to be every two years instead of four.

England fan Simon Harris, 67, a retired finance worker from Bridgnorth, Shrops, who followed Harry Kane, Jude Bellingham and co in the US, said: “This would be the end of the World Cup.



“Fifa is destroying football by selling the soul of the game for money. Uefa should take its countries out of Fifa and boycott the next World Cup. That’s the only way to make Fifa see sense.

“This is all about Fifa and Infantino making more money.”

American business associates of Infantino’s US President pal Donald Trump are understood to have been secretly consulted about the change.

They include an investment firm called Thrive run by Joshua Kushner, the brother of Mr Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner.



Fan Simon added: “Trump’s family links to the organisation which would run the World Cup just tops it off. Infantino must be stopped.”

Steve Hartshorne, 68, a retired pharmacist from Walsall, West Mids, who has not missed an England game for 14 years, said: “Infantino needs to be removed.

“He thinks he’s untouchable — Uefa need to stand up to him. The FA should set up their own organisation to run football properly.

“Having the World Cup every two years with 64 teams would be absolutely ridiculous. It’s special because it’s every four years.”



Manchester City supporter Mike Andrews, 60, a nursery manager from Newquay, Cornwall, who also followed England in the US, said: “Fifa are taking the World Cup away from fans by allowing a corporate entity to run it to make even more money. It’s all about Fifa’s greed.”

New PM Andy Burnham has also blasted the proposals. Ex-FA and Man City chairman David Bernstein said England must withdraw from the World Cup if Infantino’s proposals go through.

He added: “The whole thing is dreadful. It feels like cronyism, nepotism. It stinks, frankly.”

An FA spokesman said: “We were completely unaware of this proposal and have no substantive details.



Fifa's World Cup sell-off plan Fifa would set up a firm for the “operational delivery of Fifa tournaments” called Fifa Forward Enterprise, which will effectively control the men’s and women’s World Cups and Club World Cup

Fifa would then own the majority share in the company — but investors could purchase 20 to 30 per cent which could amount to billions of dollars

Each of Fifa’s 211 member associations would also be given a stake worth approximately £15m which they could keep or sell

Infantino would then be in line to run the company after he steps down as head of Fifa

One proposed investor is Joshua Kushner — a younger brother of Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner

“Based on the limited information, we are deeply concerned about the lack of process and governance to get to this point.

“When the proposal is shared in the full and transparent way now promised by Fifa, we will comment further.”

Uefa accused Fifa of using football “to enrich themselves and their friends”.

A Uefa insider told The Sun: “There is a great deal of anger about this plan. The future of the game is at stake.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

But the hoped-for show of European unity faltered as Czech Republic FA chief David Trunda said he can see the “positive impact” of the plans proposed by Infantino, 56, from Switzerland.



Fifa’s American bloc Concacaf and the Asian Football Confederation have both expressed disappointment that they were not consulted on the plans.

Sports.title: Non-league football club swap pitch for boxing ring as Noel Gallagher’s ex-security guard puts them through their paces
Sports.content:
SOLIHULL MOORS have made a stunning change to their pre-season football routine by swapping the pitch for a boxing ring.

Players for the non-league club ditched their football boots for boxing gloves just over a week before their season in the National League is due to kick off as they visited McCracken’s Boxing Gym.



Owned by Oscar McCracken, the renowned gym located in Tyseley, Birmingham, hosted Chris Millington’s team for a special intensive boxing and conditioning session.

The link up was made possible by MAN Commercial Protection CEO Iain McCallister, who was named Solihull Moors Foundation Chairman in June.



McCallister is a former boxer and entrepreneur whose company has offered protection to stars including Noel Gallagher, Mike Tyson, Tyson Fury, Ricky Hatton and even the King and Queen.

But the latest venture undertaken by MAN saw the fifth-tier stars breaking a sweat in the gym instead of the pitch at Damson Park.



McCallister said of the partnership: “Boxing has always been a passion of mine, so being able to connect Solihull Moors FC with McCracken’s to create this experience was something I was delighted to make happen.

“The lads embraced every challenge from the first bell to the final round.

“It was brilliant to see them step outside their comfort zone and experience the discipline, resilience and focus that boxing demands.

“Seeing an idea become a reality through collaboration is a great example of how organisations in Solihull and Birmingham can work together.”



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Crucially Millington, 50, was pleased with the session and said: “I remember mentioning to Iain that I wanted the lads to experience a proper boxing gym and a proper conditioning session during pre-season.

“That was six months ago, and it was fantastic to see it all come together.

“It simply wouldn’t have happened without Iain bringing everyone together.

“Special thanks to Oscar McCracken and everyone at the gym for their commitment to the session.

“It was fantastic, and I can’t speak highly enough of the work Oscar and his team are doing.”



The Moors start their season with an away trip to Harrogate Town on August 8, before a first home game against Boston United the following week.

Sports.title: Love rat footballer Jermain Defoe locks lips with new flame and cheekily fans her chest on cosy lunch date
Sports.content:
FORMER England ace Jermain Defoe was snapped getting intimate with a new woman during a cosy Mayfair lunch date.

The footballer, 43, who had his managerial contract with Woking FC terminated last week after just four months in the role, enjoyed a series of snogs with new partner Nadine Rider – and was caught getting handsy with her at the table.



Jermain dressed for the hot weather in beige chinos and a white t-shirt with a short-sleeved green and white striped shirt over the top, while his female companion matched in a light beige ensemble.

Seated at exclusive restaurant 74 Drake, the shaded pair seemed somewhat distracted at dinner though, as they locked lips several times.



And in one risque moment, the Premier League legend was seen smirking and pulling Nadine’s top open to fan her chest amid their steamy exchange.

Jermain’s new romance comes after his relationship with recruiter Farran Tomlin, 11 years his junior, quietly ended.





The former age gap couple appeared smitten during a break to Turkey last summer at five-star resort Lujo Hotel Bodrum.

The pair posed alongside Turkish singer Dilek Sert Erdogan, who later shared the photo to Instagram captioning it: “The amazing Jermain Defoe and his lovely wife Farran came to see our show.

“Even after I got off stage, they were still there…”

Jermain has a chequered romantic history, with the star caught kissing wedding planner Paige Mallabourn-Edmondson at a hotel in Lancashire back in 2023 – days after appearing on a red carpet with his influencer girlfriend Alisha LeMay.

Jermain previously left his wife Donna Tierney for Alisha after less than a year of marriage.



Sources claim his new flame Nadine is understood to be of a similar age to Jermain and mum to an adult son.

Last week, Jermain and football club Woking ‘mutually agreed’ to part ways, four months after he was given his first managerial role.

In a statement released on social media, Defoe said: “Following recent discussions, I can confirm that I have mutually agreed to leave my position as manager of Woking.

“Unfortunately, circumstances have ultimately made it impossible for me to continue in the position.

“I am extremely proud of the work undertaken during my time at the club and genuinely felt that we were building something special.



“I would like to thank Todd Johnson for giving me the opportunity to manage the club.

“I am incredibly grateful to the supporters and, most importantly, the players, who I am genuinely gutted for.

“The group is a fantastic one and I wish the squad every success for the season ahead.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Really disappointed the journey has ended so soon, but I leave with great pride in what Paul Bracewell, Karl Halabi and I were building at the club.

“My time at Woking has been an eye-opening managerial experience and one that will undoubtedly make me stronger for the next challenge in my career.”

Sports.title: Transfer news LIVE: Liverpool talks planned, Vinicius Jr Arsenal latest, Bruno Guimaraes admission
Sports.content:
Vinicius Junior has been linked with a sensational move to Arsenal this summer.

The latest transfer news from Arsenal, Manchester United, Liverpool and more as they look to improve their teams ahead of the Premier League season

Welcome to Mirror Football's transfer news live blog on Thursday, July 30th.

The summer transfer window will slam shut in just over a month's time with business strarting to ramp up in preparation for the new campaign. Morgan Rogers, Sandro Tonali and Elliot Anderson have all moved clubs is mega-money deals, in excess of the £100m mark, and that could be just the beginning.

Arsenal remain keen on signing Real Madrid star Vinicius Junior, whose future at Real Madrid is unclear heading into the final 12 months of his contract, and the Gunners are willing to move for the Brazilian if the opportunity arises.

Mikel Arteta's side are prepared to offer the 26-year-old star the biggest deal in the club's history, but also have their eye on improving other areas of the pitch. They remain keen on signing Newcastle United captain Bruno Guimaraes, and there is ample drama on that front with the Magpies' denying any talk of negotations between the two clubs.

Elsewhere, Liverpool are reportedly planning on holding talks with Paris-Saint Germain in an attempt to sign French international Bradley Barcola. Andoni Iraola's side are in the hunt for a successort for Mohamed Salah and have made the PSG star their number one transfer target.

Manchester United remain hopeful of adding another midfielder to their ranks ahead of their return to the Champions League, having already signed Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans. There's also the small matter of Marcus Rashford's future at the club needing resolved.

Follow all of the transfer news, rumours and updates below:

Sports.title: Dream Liverpool attack for 2026/27 as £125million man starts and Barcola replaces Salah
Sports.content:
Dream Liverpool attack for 2026/27 as £125million man starts and Barcola replaces Salah

Liverpool still have a way to go before Andoni Iraola gets his wish in the summer transfer window

View 4 Images Bradley Barcola is a crucial target for Liverpool (Image: Chris Brunskill/Fantasista/Getty Images)

Andoni Iraola’s search for Mohamed Salah’s successor continues, but Liverpool may have just received a huge boost in their pursuit of top target Bradley Barcola. The Reds' right-wing position is yet to be filled with Liverpool's season-opener against Newcastle less than a month away.

‌



The Reds boss had targeted RB Leipzig star Yan Diomande with Liverpool's offer of £85million swiftly rejected by the Bundesliga side. Attention then turned towards Barcola, 23, who had played second fiddle to Khvicha Kvaratskhelia for parts of last season at Paris Saint-Germain.

‌



The Frenchman has been an important player for the Champions League winners in the past two campaigns but has reportedly rejected a contract renewal with the Ligue 1 champions. In the midst of his uncertain future, news broke this week that Barcola had clinched a verbal agreement to join the Reds.

‌



However, landing the highly sought-after Frenchman will carry a massive financial burden, with PSG setting his asking price at £140million. The Reds are reluctant to meet that figure, which would smash the club's transfer record, and are hoping to negotiate a compromise with the French champions.

L'Equipe has reported that the two clubs are currently in talks over a possible deal for Barcola. Predominantly a left-winger, Barcola is also adept on the right flank, with Liverpool not expected to pursue another wide player should they land the Frenchman.

Liverpool chief provides FSG investment update after Jeff Bezos talks READ MORE :

Jurgen Klopp given strict instruction about managing Germany days after making quit threat READ MORE :

The forward has featured on the right side 37 times throughout his career, chipping in with seven goals and 15 assists. That leaves the left-wing berth as a three-way contest between Cody Gakpo, Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz.

‌



Gakpo may hold the edge over the two youngsters in terms of experience, but is considered less suited to Iraola's high-pressing system. A starting berth for Liverpool this coming season might arrive too early for the 17-year-old Ngumoha.

View 4 Images The Frenchman has reportedly declined a new deal at PSG (Image: FRANCK FIFE, AFP via Getty Images)

Given his exceptional talent, the Reds will be carefully monitoring his workload to avoid placing excessive physical demands on him. That could pave the way for Munoz - who arrived at the club in a £34m transfer last month - to establish himself as a regular for the Premier League outfit, following his World Cup success with Spain this summer.

‌



Both players will be anticipated to carry some of the goalscoring burden, as befits the modern-day winger's role. Nevertheless, the bulk of that responsibility will rest with Alexander Isak. The Swede endured a disappointing maiden season with merely four goals in 22 appearances across all competitions.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

View 4 Images Victor Munoz has had a dream summer with Spain (Image: Marvin Ibo Guengoer - GES Sportfoto, Getty Images)

‌



Fitness concerns and injuries disrupted his campaign, but after featuring - and finding the net - at the World Cup, the 26-year-old will be prepared to demonstrate the form that convinced the Reds to invest £125m in his signature last year.

It's a sharp contrast to the heavily interrupted summer Isak experienced this time last year. And he'll effectively be like a fresh signing for Iraola as a consequence.

View 4 Images Alexander Isak will lead the line for Liverpool with Hugo Ekitike injured (Image: Getty Images)

Article continues below

Isak's quality of finishing and capacity to combine with his team-mates, particularly Florian Wirtz, provides the Reds with a distinctive presence up front and one that could establish them as a serious challenger for the biggest honours.

Liverpool's attacking options still raise plenty of unanswered questions at this stage. However, should Iraola succeed in assembling his ideal frontline at Anfield, the rest of the league will undoubtedly be put on notice.

Sports.title: 'I cried after leaving Real Madrid for Arsenal – I wanted new contract but my agent messed up'
Sports.content:
'I cried after leaving Real Madrid for Arsenal – I wanted new contract but my agent messed up'

A former Arsenal star recalled his experience of joining the Gunners from Real Madrid

View 3 Images A former Arsenal star reflected on what led to him signing for the Gunners (Image: Mike Hewitt/Getty Images)

Mesut Ozil became an Arsenal icon but the midfielder never planned to leave Real Madrid. The Germany international joined the Gunners in a marquee £43.5million deal on deadline day in 2013 but Ozil later admitted to crying as he left the Spanish capital.

‌



Arsenal are interested in making another statement signing from Los Blancos this summer as the club explore a move for Vinicius Junior. The Brazil international has entered the final year of his Real Madrid deal, prompting speculation over his future, and contract discussions are what ultimately led Ozil to the Emirates Stadium.

‌



The attacking midfielder had signed for the Spanish giants after starring for Germany at the 2010 World Cup. In 159 appearances, Ozil scored 27 goals and provided 80 assists. However, Real were prepared to cash in on him after his father and agent clashed with club president Florentino Perez, a decision that moved Ozil to tears.

‌



“It was bad. I was very sad when I left Madrid,” Ozil recalled to Marca in 2023. “I had a great time for three years at Real Madrid and in this city. I was truly happy. But things happened.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

“Suddenly, at the beginning of that season, I wasn't getting many minutes of playing time anymore, and there was a conflict between Mr Florentino Perez and my father and agent.

‌



Liverpool given free run at Bradley Barcola as Arsenal make transfer decision READ MORE :

Thierry Henry slammed Jose Mourinho for treatment of Vinicius Jr as Arsenal move arises READ MORE :

“We had to find a new club. It was hard for me. The moment the plane took off and flew away, tears streamed down my face. That was the moment I realised it was over.”

Asked if he would go back and change his decision to leave, Ozil added: “At the time, it seemed fine to me, because after the conflict between my father and Mr Perez, I was worried I wouldn't get any playing time again if I didn't leave. So it's hard to say. But, of course, I wish we could have handled the situation differently back then.”

Ozil was an instant hit at Arsenal, clocking up seven goals and 14 assists at the end of his debut season. During his seven-and-a-half years at the club, he made 254 appearances and won three FA Cups.

‌



View 3 Images Ozil scored 44 goals in 254 games for Arsenal (Image: GLYN KIRK / AFP via Getty Images)

He is not the most recent Real Madrid player to make an impact at Arsenal, as shown by Premier League-winning captain Martin Odegaard. The Gunners will hope that Vinicius Junior can help build on last season’s success if they can get a deal over the line. However, Ozil also reflected on the circumstances surrounding his Real Madrid exit during his Arsenal heyday.

"The only and also self-critical truth [about my Real Madrid exit] is the following," Ozil wrote in his 2017 book The Magic of the Game. "My father Mustafa represented me at this time as an adviser. He was convinced that by now he would understand enough about the profession and no longer depend on the help of other agents.

‌



"I did not intend to leave Real Madrid at all. My father and I both had the goal of extending prematurely for a further year. My father then took over the negotiations. He contacted Florentino Perez and made appointments. It was not about greed. It was just a fair payment. And at first Real did not match us. But the situation was new to my father.

View 3 Images Ozil spent three years at Real Madrid (Image: Angel Martinez/Getty Images)

“He did not know how to be placed under negotiation pressure in this form. He had not done dozens of negotiations with the biggest club managers, and accordingly, he had to be honest, he had to admit that he had to deal with such a provocative offer.

Article continues below

"That is why he did not keep a cool head as it would probably have been important," Ozil continued. "In contrast to a man like Florentino Perez, who expects people to dance to his pipe, stubbornness was not appropriate. And it was not at all right for my father to leave the office and slam the door to Perez's office shut."

Sports.title: 'PSG owner promised me Liverpool transfer before manager changed his mind'
Sports.content:
'PSG owner promised me Liverpool transfer before manager changed his mind'

The former international forward was sorely disappointed that his permanent move to Liverpool failed to materialise

View 3 Images Nicolas Anelka enjoyed his time on Merseyside (Image: Clive Brunskill/ Getty Images)

Former Liverpool frontman Nicolas Anelka previously revealed he was promised a permanent transfer to the Reds from PSG before then-manager Gerard Houllier changed his mind on sanctioning the move. Liverpool are currently embroiled in yet another transfer battle with the French giants over winger Bradley Barcola, with the European champions reportedly demanding £145million for the World Cup star.

‌



While Barcola's future at Liverpool remains unclear, Anelka is adamant that his failed move to Anfield will haunt him forever. The ex-Arsenal forward made an unexpected loan switch from PSG to Anfield back in December 2001, netting five goals in 22 outings.

‌



Yet Liverpool's top brass chose not to make the Frenchman's arrangement permanent the following summer. Instead, they opted for El Hadji Diouf, who had just caught the eye representing Senegal at the 2002 World Cup.

‌



In hindsight, Liverpool's choice of Diouf over Anelka has gone down as one of the most costly mistakes in the club's recent memory.

While Diouf struggled, managing just six goals across two seasons and finding himself mired in a string of controversies, Anelka thrived at Manchester City, netting 45 goals over three seasons.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Liverpool can grant Bradley Barcola’s first demand after PSG transfer READ MORE :

The French forward told the Liverpool ECHO in 2020: "This is my biggest regret as well because I knew it was the perfect match. Everything was perfect! I loved everything about the club. I had an amazing relationship with the fans. I loved them and I think it was reciprocal.

"Looking back, I am proud to have worn the jersey of this legendary club and to have known this stadium and these amazing fans."

The 47-year-old represented 12 different sides throughout his senior career. While his spell at Liverpool was the briefest, his fondness remains evident and he revealed why the transfer fell through.

‌



"It's simple: it didn't happen because Gerard Houllier wanted to pay a lower salary," he said. "It's acceptable but you have to say it. I wanted to sign from the first minute. Of course a permanent move was discussed from the first day I joined the club.

View 3 Images Nicolas Anelka was a hit at Liverpool (Image: Clive Brunskill/ALLSPORT)

"If you look at the first time they introduced me in the press conference, I said if I could sign now, I would, but Gerard Houllier wanted a loan because he was not sure. In the middle of March, we were in negotiations to sign.

‌



"PSG shareholder Alain Cayzac said to me Gerard told him that Liverpool would sign me. Later on, Gerard told me face-to-face he'd sign me permanently.

"In the middle of April we reached an agreement about the salary, which had stalled things a little, but I was expecting to sign my contract when the league was over but there was no news from PSG and no news from Liverpool.

"I heard on the news that Gerard Houllier was after another player so that's how I knew they were not going to sign me!"

‌



Former Liverpool assistant manager Phil Thompson, who was serving as interim manager during Anelka's proposed move to the club while Houllier recovered from a heart operation, claimed the club opted against signing the Frenchman after his representatives allegedly attempted to engineer a return to Arsenal.

"I heard about this Arsenal story," Anelka said. "If it was true, why didn't I sign for Arsenal when Liverpool announced in the press they weren't going to sign me?"

View 3 Images Nicolas Anelka of Liverpool and Assistant Manager Phil Thompson look on (Image: Stu Forster/Getty Images)

‌



"And even if it was true, it's a normal situation. It's like I'm saying I don't wanna sign for a club because they are speaking with another striker. It makes no sense. The reality is at the time it was very easy to point the finger at me with my reputation."

Anelka added: "I loved my time with Phil Thompson, more so than Gerard Houllier. Phil Thompson was a typical Scouser. Direct and straight. He'll tell you what he likes and when he doesn't like it, you would know. This is exactly what I want and what I like from people.

"I know if Phil was the manager I would have signed and stayed many years but fate chose otherwise and I had to take another path to find a big club."

Article continues below

Anelka went on to represent Chelsea, Bolton and West Brom on home soil, as well as the likes of Fenerbahce and Juventus on the continent. During his spell at Chelsea, he claimed the Premier League, two FA Cups and featured in the Champions League final defeat to Manchester United in 2008.

Sports.title: 'Marcus Rashford should be embarrassed – how can his Man Utd team-mates trust him'
Sports.content:
'Marcus Rashford should be embarrassed – how can his Man Utd team-mates trust him'

Manchester United forward Marcus Rashford has been told "he should be embarrassed" as transfer talk continues to whirl following his return from a successful loan spell at Barcelona

View 2 Images Marcus Rashford has been told he "should be embarrassed" at the manner of his Barcelona exit after returning to Manchester United (Image: Getty)

Marcus Rashford has been told he "should be embarrassed" returning to Manchester United this summer. The England forward has reunited with Michael Carrick's squad following his successful spell on loan at Barcelona last season.

‌



Rashford, 28, looked all but guaranteed to join Barca on permanent terms once his temporary spell in Catalonia concluded. However, Los Cules opted to not trigger his £26million clause and signed England team-mate Anthony Gordon from Newcastle instead.

‌



Paul Parker, who won two Premier League titles at Old Trafford, has said Rashford is now on "absolutely his last chance" as he potentially looks set to stay at United this season. However, the retired full-back said Rashford must show humility and "prove a point" as he aims to win over fans (and possibly some team-mates).

‌



Parker told PariuriX: "The biggest thing is, how can he ever be trusted by his teammates again? He wasn't doing his job properly but everyone allowed him to do it [and] now they have figured him out.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

"Back in my time you would have been grabbed by one of the senior players and they would do something to you which you wouldn't find very funny.

‌



7 transfers Man Utd need to complete for Michael Carrick to win silverware this season READ MORE :

Man Utd learn Iliman Ndiaye asking price in transfer battle for Everton star READ MORE :

"He has been given this small chance to come back again and honestly he has only been given this chance because of the fact that Barcelona didn't want him. They decided to spend more money on Anthony Gordon, which Rashford should be feeling embarrassed about. The moment they spent that much money on Gordon, he should be embarrassed."

Gordon's £69.3m move to Barcelona took many by surprise, especially given previous reports suggesting Barca's lack of available finances was a major factor in why they didn't sign Rashford. Not to mention the fact Hansi Flick's side could have had Rashford for nearly a third of that amount.

Alternative transfers are still being explored for Rashford, whose last appearance for United was way back in December 2024. Roma are reportedly interested in the player, while Tottenham have also been linked with his signature.

‌



View 2 Images Rashford finds himself in a difficult position after returning from his loan at Barcelona (Image: Josep LAGO / AFP via Getty Images)

However, the forward's wages are likely to present a significant hurdle for just about any team likely to make a move. Rashford is the highest earner at Old Trafford on wages of £325,000 a week.

"If he is serious about wanting to prove himself again, it will be a serious challenge for him," added Parker. "Because the fans won't accept him just after one game or one goal, he needs to work hard consistently.

‌



"How does he conduct himself when he is sitting at the bench watching the matches? How is he conducting himself in the training and socially? That is one of the big issues and a big reason that he is where he is.

"There is a lot for him to do and to prove to be perfectly honest and this is his last chance. Absolutely his last chance."

Sports.title: Arsenal’s dream final month of transfer window as Vinicius Jr and Julian Alvarez moves sealed
Sports.content:
Arsenal’s dream final month of transfer window as Vinicius Jr and Julian Alvarez moves sealed

Mikel Arteta and Arsenal must secure several world class signings ahead of the new season

View 4 Images Arsenal must sign Bruno Guimaraes (Image: Getty )

Speaking in the wake of Arsenal's agonising Champions League final penalty shootout defeat to PSG in May, Gunners manager Mikel Arteta made no attempt to hide what he expects from the club in the transfer market.

‌



"If you want to reach another level, we're going to have to show that ambition because we are more than capable of doing it, but it demands to be very, very ambitious, very fast and very smart," Arteta said.

‌



So far, however, the Premier League champions have not lived up to those words. With sporting director Andrea Berta at the helm of transfer business, their cautious start to the window has already come at a cost, with Jeremy Monga and Morgan Rogers both moving to rival Premier League clubs in a somewhat damning turn of events.

‌



To put it into context, the Gunners completed six signings during July alone last summer — yet only two new arrivals have been announced so far this time around. The quality of those deals has not been hugely impressive, either.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Vinicius Jr has already promised to join club as Arsenal handed transfer timeline READ MORE :

Vinicius Jr snubs Real Madrid return to cast fresh doubt on future amid Arsenal interest READ MORE :

Piero Hincapie's loan was made permanent, Illan Meslier arrived on a free transfer as a third-choice goalkeeper option, and Greek winger Christos Tzolis — largely unproven at this level — was signed from Club Brugge for £34m.

‌



That said, Berta and Arteta are understood to be pushing hard behind the scenes on a number of fronts, and there are signs that progress is being made. Now, Mirror Football takes a look at the deals Arsenal need to get over the line before the window closes to put themselves in the best possible position to challenge for honours this season.

£80m Bruno Guimaraes deal

Arsenal have, understandably, shown reluctance to splash the same extravagant sums that rivals Tottenham spent on Sandro Tonali and Mateus Fernandes on a central midfielder this summer. They are currently engaged in third-party negotiations with Newcastle over a deal for their primary summer target Bruno Guimaraes.

Arsenal have been informed they must produce a transfer fee in the region of £80m for the Magpies captain, or the deal will collapse. Despite reports suggesting the Gunners had submitted a £70m bid, there have been no direct club-to-club negotiations between the two sides as it stands.

‌



Intermediaries - namely super agent Kia Joorabchian - have reportedly been heavily involved in the potential deal. The two clubs are yet to reach an agreement over the 28-year-old, however.

£80m in today's market for a Premier League-proven talent of Guimaraes' quality is far from an outrageous figure. Arsenal should pay whatever is necessary, and swiftly, to reinforce their midfield before the campaign kicks off, particularly given Declan Rice's recent injury concerns.

Vinicius Junior and Julian Alvarez

View 4 Images Julian Alvarez is Mikel Arteta's dream signing (Image: Getty)

‌



There are very few players in today's market who truly fire the imagination of fans. Julian Alvarez and Vinicius Junior are among those rare footballers who seem to carry a certain world-class aura in the modern game.

Atletico Madrid's Alvarez has been a long-standing target for Arsenal, with Arteta widely understood to be an admirer. The Argentine's preference is plainly to join Barcelona this summer, yet Atletico's firm stance against allowing him to move to a La Liga rival hands the Gunners a genuine opportunity to land his signature.

The striker represents a clear step up from both Kai Havertz and Viktor Gyokeres, with the latter potentially featuring in a player-plus-£51.7million package to secure Alvarez, given Atletico's reported interest in the Swede. The crucial question, therefore, is whether Alvarez would rather remain in Madrid or make a return to England.

‌



Arteta and Berta must pull out all the stops to persuade him to choose Arsenal, as he would undoubtedly represent a transformative acquisition. Much the same applies to Vinicius, whose ongoing contract uncertainty at Real Madrid has fuelled reports of a potential Arsenal approach.

football.london reports that senior figures at the Emirates Stadium are prepared to bring the Brazilian to N5, despite the enormous expense involved. However, no formal discussions have yet taken place between Arsenal and Los Blancos.

Consequently, no transfer fee has been put forward regarding Vinicius, whose deal runs out next summer, although reports emerging from Spain indicate that Madrid have slapped a £137m valuation on the Brazilian.

‌



For Arsenal, Alvarez and Vinicius represent two world-class talents capable of striking fear into any defence in Europe. The financial challenge of securing both players is considerable.

However, should they succeed, the two deals would transform Arsenal's standing on the global stage, firmly establishing them amongst the true elite.

View 4 Images Arsenal's pursuit of Vinicius Jr is ambitious but not impossible (Image: Getty Images Europe)

‌



£26m defender signed

The Gunners are heading into the new season fully aware that they are lacking in defensive cover. Several key components of their backline, including Jurrien Timber, Riccardo Calafiori and Ben White have demonstrated a susceptibility to injury, which proved problematic last season.

Exacerbating the situation is news that William Saliba could reportedly be sidelined for as long as five months with a back injury. Therefore, a right-sided defensive addition is vital.

Ezri Konsa has been identified as a potential target, though the Gunners are reluctant to match Aston Villa's current asking price, understood to be around £60m. Should Villa refuse to lower their demands, long-term target Ivan Fresneda of Sporting CP is the ideal signing.

‌



Fresneda, 21, is a talented prospect understood to be obtainable for around £26m. Such a modest fee would enable Arsenal to preserve resources and focus their spending further forward. The Spaniard would slot in at right-back, allowing Timber, White and Cristhian Mosquera to fill Saliba's role until the Frenchman's return.

That would bring Arsenal's combined expenditure on Alvarez, Vinicius, Guimaraes and Fresneda to roughly £295m – while providing the squad with the sufficient quality to progress further this campaign.

Player departures sanctioned

View 4 Images Fabio Vieira is no longer needed at Arsenal (Image: Getty )

‌



Arsenal need to shake off the perception that they are a poor selling club. Neither Berta nor predecessor Edu Gaspar have managed to get rid of the deadwood at London Colney, let alone secure impressive fees for departing players.

That has to change, starting with Fabio Vieira, Gabriel Jesus, Reiss Nelson and Christian Norgaard being sold. None of these four are expected to feature prominently next season and sanctioning their departures will help alleviate the wage bill, even if minimal funds can be recovered through transfer fees.

Meslier's arrival also suggests Tommy Setford, aged 20, could be loaned out to further his development. Given the congested midfield, Ethan Nwaneri would likewise benefit from consistent game time on loan, with the caveat that his destination club provides a settled environment - unlike the disastrous Marseille loan stint he suffered last season.

Sports.title: Liverpool news: Bradley Barcola negotiations opened as target hands in transfer request
Sports.content:
Liverpool news: Bradley Barcola negotiations opened as target hands in transfer request

Liverpool's push to sign Paris Saint-Germain winger Bradley Barcola has moved up a gear after reports the Reds are entering discussions with the French giants to reach an agreement

View 2 Images Liverpool have reportedly opened talks with Paris Saint-Germain over a move for Bradley Barcola (Image: Dan Mullan - UEFA/UEFA via Getty Images)

Andoni Iraola could be closing in on a transfer signing that has the potential to transform Liverpool's summer window. The Reds' major priority remains a replacement for Mohamed Salah and Bradley Barcola has taken huge steps towards landing that role.

‌



Liverpool already secured the £60million signature of Jeremy Jacquet before Victor Munoz's surprise acquisition. However, Barcola could become Iraola's first superstar capture in a deal that has the potential to set a new British transfer record.

‌



He's not the only forward signing being tipped for a move to Anfield as major developments unfold elsewhere. Mirror Football has all that and more as we break down the latest Liverpool transfer headlines.

‌



FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Liverpool open Barcola talks

Sky Sports News has reported Liverpool could be on track to land their dream Salah replacement after opening talks to sign Bradley Barcola. The player has reportedly verbally agreed to the move, with PSG the only party left that needs convincing.

Luis Diaz hands Liverpool Bradley Barcola transfer boost as final decision made READ MORE :

That won't be an insignificant hurdle to climb, however, with Les Parisiens reportedly demanding £145million for their man. To put that figure into context, it would easily eclipse the British transfer record £125m Liverpool paid for Alexander Isak last summer.

‌



Barcola, 23, has entered the final two years of his contract at the Parc des Princes. He's also reported to have turned down the offer of fresh talks over an extension, further evidence the winger is open to joining the Reds this summer.

Iraola has received further encouragement following reports in France that Barcola turned down Chelsea earlier this summer. Given his club have managed to advance in negotiations, it suggests a move to Anfield holds special significance to the forward.

Atletico Madrid and Aston Villa are among the other major teams said to be interested in the player. He reportedly holds a transfer valuation of around £50m and would come considerably cheaper than some of Liverpool's other attacking targets.

Belgium international Fernandez-Pardo can play across the front line but has operated largely as a centre forward for Lille. The youngster netted eight goals and recorded five assists in 29 Ligue 1 appearances last season.

Sports.title: Man Utd news: Marcus Rashford swap deal proposed as Michael Carrick set to axe four players
Sports.content:
Man Utd news: Marcus Rashford swap deal proposed as Michael Carrick set to axe four players

Michael Carrick's first full Premier League season in charge of Manchester United will soon get underway

View 3 Images Michael Carrick is guiding Manchester United through pre-season (Image: Getty)

Michael Carrick has welcomed three new senior players to Manchester United so far this summer. But with pre-season now in full flow, there could also be a handful of exits.

‌



Champions League football will return to Old Trafford in the upcoming season after newly installed permanent boss Carrick turned the previous campaign from a disaster to a success.

‌



He has been backed in the transfer window to the tune of three new senior arrivals: Andrey Santos, Youri Tielemans and Karl Darlow. Youngsters Tynan Thompson and Kit Margetson have also joined.

‌



But one player whose future remains undetermined is Marcus Rashford. After spending last season on loan at Barcelona, the 28-year-old is stuck in limbo and a swap deal involving him has been mooted. Mirror Football takes a look at all the latest transfer speculation surrounding United.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Man Utd enter advanced talks for striker transfer with £30m clause proposed READ MORE :

7 transfers Man Utd need to complete for Michael Carrick to win silverware this season READ MORE :

Marcus Rashford swap deal

Despite impressing on loan in Catalonia last season, Barcelona did not exercise the £26m purchase option included in Rashford's deal and he therefore remains a United player.

‌



View 3 Images Rashford's future is uncertain (Image: Getty)

A route back to the Camp Nou has been sealed off with Anthony Gordon and Karim Adeyemi signed and so it is currently unknown whether Rashford will return to fight for a place at Old Trafford or leave for pastures new.

Reports suggest neither side would ideally like Rashford to stay and Italian publication Gazzetta dello Sport states the Englishman could help get a deal for United target Manu Kone over the line.

‌



Kone, who currently plays for Roma, impressed at the World Cup for France and is reportedly available for £51m this summer. To help finance the move and offset his wage demands, it has been claimed that Rashford might head in the opposite direction.

Roma reportedly need a left-sided forward but are constrained by Financial Fair Play regulations. Rashford, whose £350,000-per-week wages have proved difficult to shift, could therefore be the makeweight in a deal for midfielder Kone.

Michael Carrick axes four players

Elsewhere, four of Rashford's team-mates appear set for the axe. The Daily Mail reports that goalkeeper Radek Vitek, defender Harry Amass and midfielders Dan Gore and Toby Collyer are all set to leave this summer.

‌



View 3 Images Gore and Collyer are likely to leave United (Image: Getty)

Young goalkeeper Vitek, as well as Amass, may initially be sent out on loan with an option to buy included. Vitek has become a target for multiple Championship teams and Amass is valued at about £6million.

Collyer spent last season on loan with Hull City and the newly promoted Tigers are reportedly interested in signing him permanently. Gore is on the chopping block following a loan with Rotherham United.

Sports.title: Today on Sky Sports Racing: Pyramid and Bintward headline Wolverhampton feature
Sports.content:
Wolverhampton is the centre of attention on Thursday night, with eight races scheduled on the all-weather, all live on Sky Sports Racing.

5.47 Wolverhampton - Exciting newcomers Pyramid and Bintward headline

Exciting newcomers Pyramid and Bintward headline a classy field of eight for the attheraces.com/marketmovers Maiden Stakes.

The Juddmonte-owned Kingman colt Pyramid has a fine pedigree, being related to the likes of Fingerpoint and Set Piece. With his trainers John and Thady Gosden arriving in red-hot form, he ought to go close under Rab Havlin.

Bintward cost a whopping €780,000 at the Deauville Arqana yearling sale and has been given plenty of time by his trainer Roger Varian. A daughter of Night Of Thunder, she is sure to be popular with Sean Dylan Bowen in the saddle.

Chimes Of Thunder rates the best of those with racecourse experience and William Haggas' 76-rated filly will hope to put that to good use as she switches to the all-weather. Sea The Stars filly Walking On Stars made little impression on debut

6.22 Wolverhampton - Angel Sense and Supreme Star seek first success

Angel Sense and Supreme Star feature among 12 runners for an open-looking Free Bets On attheraces.com EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes.

The Marco Botti-trained Angel Sense had finished in the first three on his opening three starts before suffering a heavy defeat when favourite at Newbury and he could be involved if able to bounce back.

Stablemate Supreme Star improved on his debut to finish an excellent second at Nottingham last month and that form entitles him to hit the frame.

Fresh from his Group Two win earlier this week, Kaiya Fraser will be looking for further successes and rides Location Location - who kept on when second at Thirsk on his last start and must be feared. Archie Watson's Ouragan is another for the shortlist, having ran well at Newbury the last day. If she adapts to the tapeta, she could trouble the judge.

10.14 Saratoga - Survie and Gezora seek Grade Two honours

A fantastic renewal of the Grade Two Glens Falls Stakes sees ex-European runners Gezora and Survie clash at Saratoga.

Gezora enjoyed a fruitful campaign last season, winning the Prix de Diane and Breeders' Cup Filly & Mare Turf when trained by Francis-Henri Graffard. However, she is yet to score since heading to the United States. Second in the Modesty Stakes at Churchill Downs on her first start of the campaign, she failed to fire when well beaten in the New York Stakes and has a point to prove on debut for Bill Mott.

Survie has been a fine servant for her connections picking up over £700,000 in prize money in her eighteen starts. George Boughey's five-year-old has run with credit on her last couple of runs at Newmarket and Royal Ascot and could be suited by this sharp 12-furlong test.

Last-time winners Massarat and Dona Clota make each-way appeal in a superb heat.

Sports.title: 'All to play for!' - Why Norris can still retain his F1 title
Sports.content:
Reigning world champion Lando Norris is capable of pulling off a stunning fightback to retain his Formula 1 drivers' title, according to Sky Sports F1's David Croft.

Norris claimed his and McLaren's first victory of the season in Sunday's Hungarian Grand Prix to reduce his deficit to championship leader Kimi Antonelli to 91 points as the sport enters its summer break with 11 of 23 currently scheduled rounds complete.

The emphatic nature of Norris' victory after McLaren brought a significant upgrade package to the Hungaroring has created hope that the Woking squad may have permanently joined the battle for victories, and that the Brit can surge back into title contention.

Speaking on the latest episode of Sky Sports' The F1 Show podcast, Croft suggested that the crucial factor will be whether McLaren can continue to outperform Antonelli's Mercedes team.

Croft said: "One of the big things coming out of the summer break, can McLaren carry this on? Are they going to put their eggs in a Lando Norris basket? And is it going to come up trumps once again?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the 2026 Hungarian Grand Prix

The Constructors' Championship, I think, is still very much up for grabs. The Drivers' Championship, I don't think Lando is that far behind that he can't make up a deficit.

"And seriously, I haven't even gone on holiday yet. I can't wait to get back to business at the Dutch Grand Prix in Zandvoort. I don't want a three-week break; I want the racing thick and fast!"

Can McLaren maintain form?

One of McLaren's weaknesses so far this season has been their inability to get full productivity out of the power unit supplied to them by Mercedes, which the Silver Arrows have better exploited.

The fact that Hungary is one of the least demanding circuits on the calendar from a power-unit perspective leaves some doubt as to whether McLaren can replicate the performance elsewhere.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Craig Slater runs through the biggest talking points from the Hungarian GP as Norris finally wins in 2026, Hamilton gets another penalty, Piastri fumes at McLaren's strategy and Antonelli tops the Drivers' Standings heading into the summer break

However, Croft pointed out that the Hungaroring has similarities to Monaco, where Mercedes were still able to win in early June.

"We're 11 races into the season now, and I think McLaren are understanding the power unit way better than they were at the start of the year," Croft said.

"Is it a surprise they did so well in Hungary? Well, on past form, no, they were one-two for the last two years in Budapest.

"But it is a little surprise given how strong Mercedes were in Monaco. I mean, that might be driver-specific in that respect. It might just be that Kimi was exceptional that weekend. But I don't think the Mercedes are necessarily weak at a track like Budapest.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Norris reacts to his first win of 2026, saying he always believed he could win and calling it one of his best personal performances

"What delighted me in terms of stronger competition to the championship leaders, and we want to see this championship go right to the wire because that's way more fun, was that McLaren's upgrade worked.

"They've taken their time this year to play catch-up, but they are now catching up, I think. And I think the signs were there right from the start as Lando built up the pace into the weekend that this was a good upgrade, they had the pace, and they were ready to challenge Mercedes."

Bernie: All to play for after summer break

There remains some doubt over whether all 12 of the remaining scheduled rounds will be able to go ahead due to ongoing conflict in the Middle East, but Sky Sports F1's Bernie Collins thinks there is time for Norris to turn things around regardless.

"I think this year is going to be about upgrades," Collins said on The F1 Show podcast. "It's going to be about who can get on top of these cars, who can get the best out of the cars, the best out of the engines.

"At the moment as the calendar sets, we've done 11 rounds; we've got 12 still to go. So there's still lots and lots of points on the board."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Norris snatches pole off Lewis Hamilton as Max Verstappen and George Russell struggle in Q3 at Hungaroring

Max Verstappen trailed then championship leader Oscar Piastri by 104 points with nine rounds remaining last season, before fighting back to ultimately finish just two points behind title winner Norris in the final standings.

Collins added: "We've seen McLaren this weekend at least have a little bit of the upper hand. And maybe Mercedes have been a bit distracted with each other in some of the earlier races as well.

"So, I think that it's still all to play for. I think you've pretty much got three cars, maybe Verstappen as well in that fight, that I think who knows as we go through later races who will be at the front week in, week out. And that's really interesting to watch."

Sports.title: Draper given wild card for National Bank Open in Montreal
Sports.content:
Jack Draper has been given a wild card for the National Bank Open in Montreal, which is live on Sky Sports from Monday August 3.

Draper got one of the final wild cards alongside Canadians Alexis Galarneau and Liam Draxl as he continues his attempt to try and return from a left arm injury.

The former world No 4 has endured an injury-strewn 2026 which saw him miss all three Grand Slam tournaments, but he enters the National Bank Open after a late withdrawal from this week's DC Open in Washington.

The Brit, who is coached by Sir Andy Murray, has slipped to world No 147 in the ATP rankings, leaving him likely to face qualifying if he is to compete at September's US Open after missing out on direct entry into the main draw.

Ahead of his withdrawal from Washington, Draper said: "I've had an incredibly challenging 12 months, a lot of adversity, a lot of problem solving, a lot of pain, and trying to understand that and come through it.

"I've never had a long-term injury before so I feel much better than I ever have in the last year. I feel physically really good."

Sports.title: Is Littler most dominant sportsperson in the world?
Sports.content:
Teenage dart sensation Luke Littler has left the darts world questioning if anyone will ever get near him again after winning the World Matchplay Darts on Sunday.

'The Nuke' stormed to victory in Blackpool, winning the competition for the second year in a row and seeing off final opponent Gerwyn Price 18-9.

Littler being in total control at a darts competition is nothing new. He's won every PDC major title in 2026 so far, and his World Matchplay performance has made it very difficult to argue he's not head and shoulders above his competitors.

His mind-blowing performances have sparked debate over where he ranks in the sporting world, leading Sky Sports' Love The Darts podcast pundits, former darts player Laura Turner and darts commentator Chris Murphy, to debate whether he is indeed the most dominant sportsperson in the world right now.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Chris Murphy and Laura Turner debate whether Luke Littler has already surpassed Phil Taylor as the greatest ever darts player.

"It's a very difficult question, how do you measure dominance?" Murphy said. "Darts seems to have more majors than any other sport, if you're doing it on major titles, but then again if you just took the top four and made it fair, he wins what you might call the Grand Slam titles.

"He holds them all and he's on course to have a clean sweep of every title so of course he does. I think yes [he is the most dominant]."

Murphy then named two other sporting stars that come close to giving Littler a run for his money - tennis world No 1 Jannik Sinner and his golf equivalent, Scottie Scheffler - but concluded neither can touch him.

"Looking at other sports, we've mentioned tennis, Sinner maybe he's in the conversation," he said. "Scheffler in golf has been No 1 for a long time, but I don't think any of them get near Littler."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the World Matchplay final between Luke Littler and Gerwyn Price.

Turner agreed, pointing out how rare it is to have two English people dominating a sport in both the men's and women's editions at the same time.

"It's very hard to say no [he isn't the most dominant] isn't it," Turner said. "From a women's darts point of view actually I think [Women's World Matchplay winner] Beau Greaves is unbelievably dominant, she's just picked up the Matchplay in Blackpool. She won 17 out of the 24 titles available in that qualification process as well.

"She's been on a run of 114 consecutive wins, it took Fallon [Sherrock] at a 102 average just to stop that run. Beau is very dominant.

"In darts at the moment I personally think we're very lucky, I know Beau is on the Pro Tour as well. I can't think of another sport where at this moment in time, anyone that is dominating in the way they are."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Women's World Matchplay final between Beau Greaves and Fallon Sherrock in Blackpool.

Does Littler edge Taylor as darts' greatest?

While Turner and Murphy have been wowed by Littler this month, they believe the teenager still has a while to go until he can call himself darts' greatest ever.

Asked if he is the best darts player to ever do it, Murphy replied: "No, and this is where I think we need to zoom out a little bit. Potential to best the greatest? Possibly, but I don't think it's especially close yet to be honest.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Following his World Matchplay final victory against Gerwyn Price, Luke Littler says he'd love to be the greatest darts player of all time and admits he is chasing the feat of winning every major darts title in a calendar year.

"It's not criticism of his abilities and talents, it's just simple arithmetic I suppose. Phil Taylor's title tally, 16 world titles, spanning across four different generations of darts players, and he's had to reinvent himself for different games in different eras."

Taylor, who retired in 2018, holds the record for the most darts world titles. Littler, meanwhile, has two, winning the PDC World Darts Championship in 2025 and 2026 after bursting on the scene in 2024.

Laura agreed that Littler has a way to go yet to edge Taylor, adding: "All of us suffer from recency bias. There's a lot of people don't forget that never engaged in darts to the level they are before Luke Littler came onto the scene.

Image: Darts icon Phil Taylor was Luke Littler's idol growing up

"Ultimately, Phil has played through different generations, I don't want to say mind games but you know you can get under people's skin a bit more.

"Ability wise, and all the accolades he has won over all those years, you have to say Phil is the greatest ever darts player we've had.

"Luke Littler perhaps one of the most dominant sports people at this time."

Sports.title: Bialecki clinches Players Championship 26 title
Sports.content:
Sebastian Bialecki secured his second PDC ranking title with a hard-fought 8-6 victory against Mario Vandenbogaerde in Wednesday's Players Championship 26 final.

Exactly a year to the day since he claimed his maiden ranking title in Hildesheim, Bialecki repeated the feat on German soil, overturning a 5-3 deficit to cap off another memorable triumph.

The 22-year-old has celebrated an astonishing six Development Tour titles in 2026, and he reaffirmed his credentials by returning to the winner's circle at Halle 39.

Bialecki began his title challenge with successive ton-plus averages in deciding-leg wins over Dennie Olde Kalter and Cor Dekker, recovering from 5-3 down in his opener against Olde Kalter.

Sports.title: Liverpool beat Wrexham in New York to maintain perfect pre-season under Iraola
Sports.content:
Liverpool continued their winning start to life under Andoni Iraola by beating Wrexham 1-0 in their second pre-season contest ahead of the 2026/27 campaign.

The Reds had already beaten Sunderland in Nashville before making the trip to Yankee Stadium in New York to face a stern test, with their opposition having already bested both Manchester United and Leeds in recent weeks.

Image: Szoboszlai leads Liverpool out ahead of their 1-0 win over Wrexham

Stand-in captain Dominik Szoboszlai was forced to play centre-back following the injury to Joe Gomez against the Black Cats. He was still involved in Liverpool's best chance in the first half, picking out Harvey Elliott, who would then set up Josh Abe for a shot kept out by former Reds goalkeeper Danny Ward.

Iraola made four changes at the break, one of those being the introduction of Rio Ngumoha. The teenage sensation proved the difference-maker, driving at the heart of the Wrexham defence before his deflected effort looped into the back of the net for the sole goal of the game 15 minutes from time.

Kieffer Moore did waste a good chance for Wrexham in the latter stages, fluffing his lines from close range, but Liverpool held on to make it two wins from two in the United States.

The squad will travel to Chicago ahead of their next game against Leeds on Sunday, when the likes of Florian Wirtz, Ryan Gravenberch and Alexander Isak are expected to get their first minutes of pre-season.

Iraola: Liverpool still not showing my identity

Speaking with the club's media post-match, Iraola said his side still had some way to go to adapt to his style ahead of the new season.

"I think overall we were more solid than the other day," he said. "It was a different kind of game. The pitch is quite narrow and there are not a lot of spaces. But, I think we had good spells. And even if the other day we scored more goals and it looked nicer, I think today we were more a team and more collective.

Image: Andoni Iraola believes Liverpool still have work to do to showcase his footballing identity

"I think we're still not there [showing his identity]. We sometimes arrive too late, but I think it's a step forward, since especially the first half against Sunderland.

"That is more of a reference than the second half. Slowly, I hope every game we are closer and closer. We start to add new bodies, because now we are playing with a lot of the young players. We have to add the senior players that are starting to train with us, so we can arrive to the beginning of the season in a good place."

Wirtz, Gravenberch and Isak set to feature vs Leeds

Iraola also confirmed plans to use some of his biggest players when the Reds face Leeds in their final game of the American tour on Sunday.

The trio of Wirtz, Gravenberch and Isak have already begun their pre-season training in Chicago following early exits from the World Cup, and will be joined by the rest of their team-mates.

When asked if there was a chance Reds fans could see them in action - as well as new signing Jeremy Jacquet - Iraola responded: "Yes, my idea is for Ryan [Gravenberch], for Florian [Wirtz], for Alex [Isak], for even Jacquet to have their first minutes against Leeds.

"We'll see how many minutes they can play, but we have to start slowly integrating more of the senior players that have had less training sessions. I think they should be ready on the weekend to have their first minutes."

Sports.title: England dominate Tonga in must-win clash at Commonwealth Games
Sports.content:
England dominated Tonga 94-32 in their must-win Pool A game at the Commonwealth Games at the Hydro in Glasgow.

It means England's hunt for a semi-final place continues and they did it in some style, scoring a record 94 goals for the team at the Games.

It surpasses their previous record of 89 goals at the Commonwealth Games, which came 24 years ago against Sri Lanka in 2002.

The match was, throughout, in England's hands after they cantered into a 27-8 lead at the end of the first quarter.

Eleanor Cardwell then took real control, scoring 54 goals from 60 shots. Sasha Glasgow added 18, Ella Clark added 12, then Olivia Tchine added 10 for a statement win.

England are attempting to cement a top-two spot as they try to go for glory for the first time in eight years after their 2018 triumph.

They currently sit in third but are level on points with Australia and South Africa.

England's goal average is 1.74 and goal difference is 127. South Africa's goal average is 2.06 and their goal difference is 123. Australia's goal average is 1.99 and their goal difference is 116.

In their final match of the pool stages, England will take on South Africa at 9pm on Thursday.

Sports.title: Rockets hand Fire first defat in The Hundred as Pretorius stars for Spirit
Sports.content:
Trent Rockets handed Welsh Fire a first defeat of the season in The Hundred in a one-sided affair at Sophia Gardens.

The visitors chased down a below-par target of 123 with 28 balls to spare, Ben Duckett seeing the Rockets to victory with an unbeaten 52.

The start of the Rockets' chase was not fluent by any means but the Fire bowlers were sloppy, giving away four free-hits in the powerplay and seven in total.

Duckett faced the first four, only finding the boundary once, but he and Finn Allen (33) still managed to move the visitors onto 42-0 after 25 balls with little cause for concern.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Welsh Fire's Joe Root was bowled by Matt Henry after a failed attempt at a scoop shot in the match against Trent Rockets

The explosive Allen began to accelerate, taking 17 runs off Sam Cook's first five. He and Duckett cruised along against an uninspired Fire attack, taking the score to 75 before Allen fell lbw to fellow Kiwi Rachin Ravindra for 33.

Duckett, joined by Tom Banton (31), continued on his merry way, bringing up a second half-century in as many games, this time from 42 balls, as the Rockets made it two wins from three.

Sports.title: Uefa calls emergency meeting as opposition to Fifa plan hardens
Sports.content:
Uefa has called an emergency ­meeting of its 55 members for Thursday afternoon to discuss a coordinated response to Gianni Infantino’s plan to sell off stakes in the World Cup to private investors. A European boycott of Fifa tournaments is among the options under consideration.

As the next major event in the Fifa calendar, a boycott of next year’s Women’s World Cup has been ­mentioned in preliminary ­discussions, although there would be a reluctance in some quarters to make the women’s game suffer as a consequence of a protest against Fifa proposals that primarily revolve around ­monetising the men’s World Cup and Club World Cup.

Uefa’s initial condemnation of Fifa’s plan to “sell the soul” of ­football has received strong backing from Concacaf – the North, Central ­American and Caribbean ­confederation – and the Asian Football Confederation (AFC). If their members follow their leads there should be sufficient votes to block the proposal.

Those three confederations make up 143 of the 211 Fifa members, but unanimity is not guaranteed, as was made clear when Czechia’s ­football association became the first in Europe to back the plan.

Having received more than 200 ­letters of endorsement backing his re-election next year, Infantino is confident he has enough votes – although it is unclear whether the proposal requires a simple ­majority to be passed. Several sources have said that creating a new commercial entity – Fifa Forward Enterprise [FFE] – and selling a 20% stake to investors would necessitate a change of Fifa statutes, which requires a 75% majority that would be much harder to obtain.

View image in fullscreen Fifa’s branding was impossible to miss during the World Cup. Photograph: Mike Segar/Reuters

On Wednesday evening, Infantino released a video to address the ­backlash. “FFE is actually a ­proposal, an offer,” he said. “It’s part of a democratic process – a ­consultation process – and, above all, it is an opportunity but not an ­obligation. It is a golden opportunity to turbocharge the development of the game globally.”

Earlier, Uefa redoubled its attack on Fifa by accusing the world ­governing body of “using our sport to enrich themselves and their friends” after it emerged that ­Infantino had ­presented members with a deadline of 19 September to decide whether to apply for an ­initial payment of $20m (£15m) from the proposed sell-off.

A further $20m for each ­association would also be made available at a later date, although it is unclear whether accepting the money would equate to a formal ­endorsement and therefore remove the need for a vote.

“Today we have learned of Fifa’s deadline to associations to support their proposals or have the one-off payout offer withdrawn,” Uefa said. “This says everything you need to know about this plan. But having held discussions with many stakeholders across the game, Uefa knows there is significant and growing opposition to Fifa’s scheme. Fifa cannot continue to use our sport to enrich themselves and their friends. We can grow the game correctly. It’s time to prioritise associations, clubs, leagues, players and fans.”

Uefa’s second statement of condemnation followed a similarly strong intervention from ­Concacaf, which is particularly ­significant given the confederation has just hosted the most ­lucrative World Cup and covers the region that has brought the proposed new investment from the New York-based Thrive Eternal.

The Concacaf president, Victor Montagliani, was instrumental in the success of the US, Mexican and Canadian bid for the tournament, but along with the seven other Fifa vice‑presidents and Fifa council members he was kept in the dark over the plans.

“Concacaf was only made aware of this matter through media reports and, subsequently, via a media release,” Concacaf said. “We are deeply concerned by the lack of due process.

“We share the ­disappointment of many within our region and the game that this level of detail has been designed and shared publicly before any discussion with the ­relevant governance bodies and stakeholders has taken place.

“As leaders within football, we are the custodians of the game. Collectively, Fifa, the confederations and every member association have a responsibility to always act in the best interests of the sport. Every decision we make must be guided by good governance, robust processes and long-term stewardship.

View image in fullscreen Gianni Infantino announces Saudi Arabia as the 2034 World Cup hosts. The AFC’s statement is understood to have the backing of the Saudi Arabian federation. Photograph: Fifa

“This is the framework within which Concacaf operates. We trust that all within the Fifa family will act in the same manner.”

The AFC issued a similar statement of disapproval, which significantly is understood to have the backing of the Saudi Arabian football federation, a close ally of Infantino and the host of the 2034 World Cup.

“The AFC was not consulted on the proposal and is disappointed that a matter of such significance entered the public domain before the AFC family had been afforded the opportunity to examine and discuss it through the appropriate and established governance channels,” it said.

“While the AFC recognises the importance of exploring innovative approaches that can strengthen the future of global football, initiatives of this scale and consequence must be founded upon the principles of good governance, transparency and meaningful consultation.

“Decisions that may reshape the commercial and financial future of the game require comprehensive prior engagement with confederations, member associations and other relevant stakeholders before any proposal is made to the appropriate decision-making bodies.”

Elite clubs also expressed their unhappiness, with the European Football Clubs organisation pointing out that Fifa had not consulted it despite the two bodies having signed a memorandum of understanding.

“As an institution that represents over 850 football clubs – whose member clubs, their players and communities are fundamental participants in football worldwide, not least in Fifa’s competitions including all the international club competitions – it would be wholly appropriate for EFC to be fully consulted on a proposal of such magnitude,” it said.

“EFC learned about this proposal in the same way as most global football stakeholders – without warning and through the media.”

Sports.title: Experimental Liverpool down Wrexham thanks to Rio Ngumoha’s deflected strike
Sports.content:
Liverpool turned the Empire State Building red when launching a new away kit on Tuesday but neither they nor Wrexham could illuminate Yankee Stadium 24 hours later. It was rough in the diamond, although Rio Ngumoha’s deflected goal made it two wins out of two for Andoni Iraola on his first pre-season tour as Liverpool head coach.

Ngumoha, a second half substitute who Iraola deployed on the right, satisfied the majority of a 42,204 crowd with a 75th-minute shot that looped in off Wrexham defender Lewis Brunt. Wrexham’s Hollywood co-owners Ryan Reynolds and Rob McElhenney (now simply Rob Mac) were in attendance for what the former had labelled a “punch-me moment” but in truth few blows were traded at the iconic baseball stadium.

Liverpool’s preparations for the second game of pre-season were not exactly smooth, in fairness to Iraola’s team. Their flight from Chicago was cancelled on Tuesday night with players and staff on the tarmac ready to take off. Poor weather conditions in the New York area delayed their arrival until the day of the game, and Liverpool only checked into their Midtown hotel around midday. They were flying back to Chicago straight after the match too.

Florian Wirtz, Alexander Isak and Ryan Gravenberch did not make the trip from Liverpool’s training base despite joining up with the squad following their post-World Cup holidays. The game came too early in their pre-season preparations to be considered. With Joe Gomez injured and Federico Chiesa also absent through illness, Iraola had little choice but to select another young and experimental side. Six of Liverpool’s starting line-up had no Premier League experience whatsoever but at least the emphasis on youth offered the crowd a glimpse of the highly-rated Joshua Abe.

View image in fullscreen Joshua Abe reacts after failing to score at Yankee Stadium. Photograph: Angela Weiss/AFP/Getty Images

Abe, a pacy and prolific right winger, is regarded as one of the brightest prospects in the country and was inundated with offers before committing his future to Liverpool when turning 16 earlier this month. Manchester City, Manchester United and Chelsea were all interested in the Warrington-born England youth international, with deals worth £40,000-a-week reportedly on his table. There was understandable relief inside Anfield when he agreed scholarship terms in June with a three-year professional contract to follow on his 17th birthday next July.

Abe could have marked his first senior Liverpool start with an early goal when released clear of the Wrexham defence by Harvey Elliott. A heavy first touch gave the Wrexham and former Liverpool goalkeeper Danny Ward opportunity to save at the feet of the teenager. Iraola started with a front line of Calum Scanlon, Lewis Koumas and Abe. Koumas went close from distance and had a penalty shout waved away but, aside from a few surging midfield runs by Dominik Szoboszlai, it was a quiet friendly.

Wrexham are further along in their pre-season work – their first competitive game is a week on Friday against Middlesbrough in the Carabao Cup – and it showed as the first half progressed and Phil Parkinson’s team gained a physical edge. Sam Smith and Callum Doyle were unable to trouble Giorgi Mamardashvili with the chances that fell their way.
