Sports.title: Paul Mullin signs for EFL club after Wrexham contract terminated this summer
Sports.content:
Paul Mullin has signed for Rotherham United after seeing his Wrexham deal terminated.

The striker became a cult hero for the Welsh club, helping them win promotion from the National League and League Two in back-to-back years.

2 Mullin's later years at Wrexham haven't been what he was hoping for Credit: Getty

He even found a role in Deadpool with Ryan Reynolds as 'Welshpool', and the striker gained a large number of fans.

However, his contract was mutually terminated in June, and the Championship side elected not to keep him around.

Still, his record for Wrexham was very good, scoring over 100 goals in just over 160 appearances.

And now he's back in League Two to try and help the Millers. Mullin has signed a two-year deal with south Yorkshire-based side.

Speaking to the club's website, he said: "It's been a long summer for me. Just, obviously, after the last couple of years, it was just about taking my time and making sure something was right for me, my family to the next part of the chapter of my career and Rotherham was an opportunity I couldn't pass up.

"I spoke to the manager beforehand, who obviously highlighted the plans he has for the club and that the people above him have for the club going forward, and although it hasn't been a great time the last couple of years, we've all seen what can happen at this place once it takes off and, hopefully, this year we can get back going that way."

Mullin on Wrexham

Mullin spent five years with Wrexham and became one of their most important players of recent times.

He still had one year left on his deal, but it was agreed by mutual consent to terminate it.

And it was an emotional goodbye for the striker, who said: "From the bottom of my heart, thank you very much to all the fans, near and far. What we create together is something I'll always be proud of.

"This club is special and has been to me and my family from the very start. I want nothing more than to see this club continue to progress - for all those people who came together to keep it alive and for Ryan Reynolds and Rob Mac who are a special pair of people.

2 Mullin is a legend for Wrexham, and now he has the chance to carry on his career Credit: Getty

"This might be the end for me as a player, but there's not a chance it's the end of my love and affection for the club."

Manager Phil Parkinson also paid tribute, saying: "This settlement enables him to take his time and find the right club for him, going forward.

"It can't be underestimated the role Mulls (Mulliin) has played in the story of Wrexham Football Club over the last five years, with so many memorable goals and moments. He'll be a player always remembered and revered by our supporters."

Bagsman

Rotherham are hoping that Mullin's excellent League Two record can continue.

In 274 appearances in that division, he has 93 goals and 26 assists.

At the fourth tier of English football, he is a proven goalscorer.

Sports.title: Rio Ferdinand’s son, Tate, signs first pro deal with Premier League club
Sports.content:
Rio Ferdinand's son, Tate, has signed his first professional contract with Premier League side Brighton and Hove Albion.

It follows his oldest son, Lorenz, doing the exact same thing a year ago.



2 Two of Ferdinand's sons are now following in his footsteps Credit: Getty

Tate, who is 17 years old, is a centre-back, just like his dad.

His other son is a goalkeeper, so they'll likely be playing together at some point in the near future for one of Brighton's youth sides.

In a post on Instagram, Ferdinand revealed the news and just how proud he was.

He said: "Proud moment with the family, my boy @tateferdinand5 signed his first pro contract @officialbhafc.



"Keep up the hard work."

Tate became an official part of the Brighton Under-18s squad in 2024.

They are the only club that he has played for in his career so far, though, he is yet to appear for the club's Under-21s and make his Premier League 2 debut.

In the replies, loads of Manchester United legends and Ferdinand's former teammates sent their congratulations.



Edwin van der Saar said: "All the best, Tate."

Joleon Lescott, who was an England international with Ferdinand, said: "Sick."

Tate's career and play style

Unlike his older brother, Tate is very much in the mould of his dad. He is a centre-back and also wears the number five jersey.



Rio was a leader when he was at Manchester United, and Tate has been described as being the same.

But he was also excellent on the ball, and after a game late in October last year, people at the match believe he was just like his father.

However, his manager, Bjorn Hamberg believes the attention is water off a duck's back.

He said: “I am sure he doesn’t care about that (attention).

“Tate Ferdinand is Tate Ferdinand and he needs to be play his game and have his pathway and career.



2 Tate is following exactly in his father's footsteps Credit: Getty - Contributor

“For us as a team, for the under-18s as a captain, he is a big voice in our dressing room.

“He is obviously a leader in the back line and playing very well for the moment. I am really pleased for him as well.”

Brothers in arms

Tate and Lorenz are now both professionals with Brighton, and Rio will be hoping the future is very bright for both of them.



There are only two years separating the siblings as well, so it's possible we'll see double Ferdinand in the Brighton first team one day.

But as Rio said in his post, this is actually where the hard work starts.

Sports.title: Marcus Rashford could make shock move to Premier League rival of Man United in £30m deal
Sports.content:
Marcus Rashford could make shock move to Premier League rival of Man United in £30m deal

Marcus Rashford could join Tottenham this summer, despite continuing to be linked with north London rivals Arsenal.

The England forward has long been tipped for a move to the Gunners, although no attempt to sign him has been made this summer as his future remains in limbo.

6 Rashford is weighing up his future after featuring six times for England at the World Cup Credit: Getty

After spending last season on loan at Barcelona, Rashford saw his hopes of joining them permanently fall apart when England teammate Anthony Gordon completed a £70million move from Newcastle to the Camp Nou.

This means that, as things stand, the 28-year-old will report back to Manchester United for pre-season training in the coming days.

Rashford hasn't played for the Red Devils since the back end of 2024, spending time on loan at Aston Villa and then Barcelona.

However, United are still expected to try and offload the academy graduate before the end of the summer, with the club keen to get his wages of more than £325,000-a-week off the payroll.

And Rashford is also keen to leave Old Trafford, having fallen out with the club's hierarchy, as well as previous boss Ruben Amorim.

Rash decision

As speculation continues over Rashford's future, Arsenal have once again been linked with the winger, after long being touted to sign him in previous transfer windows.

The Gunners are keen to strengthen in the left-wing area following Leandro Trossard's departure, and were recently dealt a blow in their pursuit of Real Madrid superstar Vinicius Junior, who is set for new contract talks with the Spanish giants.

And while Rashford is expected to be available for a cut-price £30million, talkSPORT's Chief Football Correspondent believes Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta could be put off signing him.

Crook said talkSPORT's Hawskbee and Jacobs show: “I'm just not sure Marcus Rashford is a Mikel Arteta-type player.

“If you look at what he's done, and why Arsenal have been so successful in his tenure, he weeded out the sort of problematic characters from the dressing room, so I'm not sure that he would necessarily welcome Marcus Rashford with open arms."

6 Arteta has made ruthless decisions on big-name players in his Arsenal tenure, including Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang and Mesut Ozil Credit: Getty

6 Rashford scored 14 goals and provided 14 assists for Barcelona last season, but the Spanish giants opted not to sign him permanently Credit: Getty

Gunner go across town?

Moving on to where Rashford could go instead of Arsenal, Crook then surprisingly pointed to bitter rivals Tottenham.

He insisted that head coach Roberto De Zerbi could be drawn to the prospect of turning the Englishman's career around, while Spurs haven't been afraid to splash the cash this summer.

After narrowly avoiding relegation last season, the north London outfit have spent heavily as they look to strengthen, spending £237m on new players which includes record signing Sandro Tonali.

On Rashford, Crook continued: “I think if he goes anywhere in London, I'm keeping an eye on Tottenham.

“I could see that deal happening. Roberto De Zerbi believing that he can get the best out of Marcus Rashford.”

Outlining the finances of a potential deal, Crook explained that while Rashford is set to be available for an appealing transfer fee, he admitted his wage demands could be a stumbling block.

6 Roberto De Zerbi has been ambitious with his player recruitment at Tottenham so far this summer Credit: AFP

Crook added: “When you say a cheap deal, I think probably an offer of £30million will be accepted by Manchester United, but you have to factor in he's on £325,000 a week at Old Trafford, and doesn't seem too willing to take a pay cut.”

'Every top-six team' would want Rashford

While Rashford's time as a United player looks to be up, talkSPORT's Rory Jennings believes he will still be holding out hope to be given a second chance by newly-appointed permanent boss Michael Carrick.

The local lad graduated from United‘s academy and has scored 138 goals in 426 games for the senior side – but has not played for his boyhood club since December 2024.

Rashford joined Aston Villa on loan in January 2025 after falling out of favour under ex-United head coach Ruben Amorim, and has previously drawn attention for off-the-field issues, including a controversial trip to a Belfast nightclub in January 2024.

Jennings told talkSPORT Drive: "Carrick's done an excellent job at that club.

"If he now looks at Marcus Rashford and thinks that there is a world where Rashford could come back into the fold, maybe get him playing again, maybe get the Stretford End singing his song again to the Stone Roses, that would be I think the dream for Rashford.

6 Rashford has spent almost 18 months away from Old Trafford across two loan spells Credit: Getty

"It feels optimistic but that's as good as it can get for Rashford now."

Jennings insisted that if it weren't for previous disciplinary issues, Rashford would be of interest to all top Premier League clubs.

He continued: "If you remove all of the baggage, all of the compensation. Just as a footballer, on form. I think he's excellent.

"I think he's an excellent footballer and if he didn't have the baggage and didn't have the wage expectation, I think basically every team in the top six… [would be interested].

"I think there is reputational damage, I think there is professionalism. I remember when he was meant to be playing for Manchester United, he missed training, he was in Belfast, he was boozing. I think there is reputational damage to Rashford."

He added: "There is also the financial demands of having Rashford in your camp. If we forget everything and we just talk about the footballer on his best day, I think every team in the top six would want him.

6 There is no question about Marcus Rashford's ability on his day Credit: Getty

"The reason they don't want him is the reputational damage and the wage demand."

Sports.title: Argentina charged by FIFA over Falklands sign as players and coach face possible ban for ‘assault’
Sports.content:
Argentina charged by FIFA over Falklands sign as players and coach face possible ban for ‘assault’

Argentina have been charged by FIFA over the Falklands signs displayed after the World Cup semi-final against England.

The South American nation have been found to have breached four different FIFA conduct codes.

5 Argentina's flag after the win over England claimed the Falklands as their own Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

They are also being investigated for racism and discrimination.

And after the scenes at the World Cup final, Leandro Paredes, Nahuel Molina and coach Roberto Ayala are facing 'assault' charges and a potential ban.

Last week, FIFA hired a special disciplinary and ethics prosecutor to asses the scenes at the final whistle.

Paredes and Molina started launching themselves at Spain's players, who were attempting to celebrate the victory.

And on recommendations by the prosecutor, Molina, Paredes and Ayala are all set to be investigated for their conduct.

All are for alleged assault, and Molina has an extra for unsporting behaviour.

Thiago Almada and Gavi are under investigation for unsporting behaviour as well.

Under FIFA's disciplinary rules, if found guilty, it is at least a one match for unsporting behaviour and three for assault.

The national team itself has been charged with a few breaches as well.

The first is for using a sporting event to demonstrate a non-sporting political cause.

5 Ugly scenes marred the end of Spain's World Cup win Credit: Getty

This relates to the Falklands banner that the Argentinian players claimed from their fans and danced around with after beating England in the semi-final in Atlanta.

The banner read: “Las Malvinas son Argentinas”, which translates as 'The Falklands are Argentine'.

They have also been charged with team misconduct, racist and discriminatory abuse and breaching order of security.

That last charge is related to late kick-offs, while the other charges are in relation to the fans.

American streamer IShowSpeed was the subject of alleged racial abuse during one Argentina game.

5 Argentina now face several very serious charges Credit: AFP

Action

At the time of the Falklands banner and the World Cup final, FIFA said they wouldn't be looking into it. They now have, and there are some very serious charges.

Regarding the post-match brawl, Spain's manager Luis de la Fuente called for action once he saw what actually happened.

Speaking after the World Cup final, he said: “At the time, I didn’t realise it. I was celebrating, hugging teammates.

“But in any case, it is intolerable, unacceptable, it cannot be allowed.

"Players of that stature, whom I praised in the days leading up to the match and continue to praise, who are great players with a tremendous coach, surely they must have felt just as bad as we did seeing those reactions.”

An online petition quickly surfaced demanding that Argentina be banned from all future World Cups.

5 Spain managed to overcome the Argentines in New Jersey Credit: Getty

Over 23 million people signed it before being closed after FIFA launched their investigation.

And talkSPORT's Gabby Agbonlahor believes the punishment for the Argentinian players throwing punches should be severe.

He said: "If you watch it back, Paredes on Garcia, he grabs his neck. And the way Garcia's neck jolts, that's assault, it's as simple as that.

"You want to feel safe on the pitch, the punishment has to be that big that no one ever does that again.

"No matter what happens in football, you can be angry you lost, but be classy in defeat. If you want to fight Paredes, there are places to fight - not on the pitch against Garcia.

"And the way he was manhandling Gavi, a 21-year-old kid, and you were throwing him around on the pitch, that's someone's son, brother. Disgraceful. I would ban him from the whole next tournament if I had my way. Coward."

5 Paredes became public enemy number one after the World Cup final Credit: Getty

Bizarre

Following the Falklands banner being widely slammed by media all over the world, the White House came to Argentina's defence.

They claimed that the South American giants had every right to display the banner.

The executive director of the White House's World Cup team, Andrew Giuliani told reporters: "We believe in our First Amendment rights here in the United States of America.

"And in terms of the ability, the opportunity to be able to make statements, (Argentina) has the ability to do that in the United States of America."

Meanwhile, the Falklands government themselves called for sanctions against Argentina, saying: “The Falklands government is disappointed – though regrettably not surprised – that the Argentine football team decided to tarnish the result of last night’s World Cup football semi-final – a game that did not in any case involve the Falkland Islands.

“That said, it is hardly news to anyone that the people of the Islands were victims of an aggressive invasion in 1982, which left many traumatised.

“The banner displayed by Argentina last night, therefore, was particularly insensitive for many people in the Falklands.”

They continued: “It is the avowed policy of the Falkland Islands Government that we do not wish to see politics being brought into sport.

“Nor do we wish the Islands and their people to be used as a political football in every conversation about England and Argentina.”

Sports.title: Abbi Summers: Jury is out on Savinho but one transfer is a no-brainer for me
Sports.content:
Abbi Summers: Jury is out on Savinho but one transfer is a no-brainer for me

Tottenham have been urged to consider signing England star Marcus Rashford instead of pursuing a move for Savinho.

Roberto De Zerbi's side remain interested in a deal for the Manchester City winger.



5 Abbi Summers doubts Savinho's Premier League pedigree amid Spurs' interest in the winger Credit: Getty

Savinho has told Manchester City he wants to join Spurs, talkSPORT understands.

The 22-year-old was also keen on the move last summer amid previous interest, but remained at the Etihad Stadium.

He remains a leading target for Spurs, but any potential deal is dependant on the City board changing their stance.



The arrival of another winger could allow Savinho to leave the club before the transfer window closes, though.

Talks between City and Spurs have been ongoing since the early part of the summer.



However, Tottenham broadcaster Abbi Summers remains on the fence over Savinho's potential arrival in north London.

She assessed Spurs' interest on the latest episode of talkSPORT's Inside Spurs alongside Majestic and Sonny Snelling.



Savinho signed for City two summers ago, before penning a new six-year deal last October through to 2031.

Savinho is not 'Prem proven'

Asked if the Brazil international is still unproven, Summers admitted: "Yes, I was actually having that conversation yesterday with a City fan about him because I was like, we are so hellbent on getting Savinho and I just need to know why.

"I’m not disputing it. Obviously, there’s data there that will back it up. Everything is done by data now. So, they obviously think he’s the best option and fit for Spurs."

5 Spurs remain in talks with City for Savinho, who wants to join the club this summer Credit: AFP



Since joining City, Savinho has scored seven goals and added 16 assists in 84 appearances.

However, he was limited to just 14 starts in all competitions under Pep Guardiola last season.

Summers added: "I would say that first season, decent enough return, but look, he’s still young. He’s not always been first-choice and featured loads for City.

"I think I’m kind of with Sonny on ‘proof will be in the pudding’ with it. I think him coming to Spurs, having a fresh start, obviously he’ll get more game time.



"Maybe there’s a player in there that just hasn’t really developed yet. My fear with that is that we tend to always have players that haven’t quite developed yet.

"Can’t always cross a ball, can’t always beat a man. Ball retention is not always the strongest point.

5 Summers believes pursuing a deal for Rashford is a 'no-brainer' for Spurs Credit: Getty

"So my thing is I would have liked someone that is proven. Yes, he’s ‘Prem proven’ to an extent, but he’s not ‘Prem proven’ enough for me."



Rashford deal a 'no-brainer'

Summers remains keen for Spurs to strengthen in the left-wing position ahead of the new season, though.

Wilson Odobert is not expected to return from injury until at least November, whilst fellow wingers Mikey Moore and Manor Solomon were both out on loan last season.

As a result, Summers has hailed a move for Rashford as a 'no-brainer' amid his uncertain future at Manchester United.

When asked if she would go for the England forward over Savinho, she replied: "Yes, yes I would. That’s a no-brainer to me, but I think maybe the wages is where that would be an issue.



"I mean, Rashford might not want to come, first and foremost, and want to fight for his place under (Michael) Carrick, but to me I would."

5 Rashford's future at United is uncertain following his loan spell with Barca Credit: AFP

Summers continued: "I would much rather go for Marcus Rashford. I think in terms of what he’s done over the course of his career, I think he’s been brilliant for the most part.

"I think it’s easy for us to get wrapped up in maybe the last couple seasons or where it hasn’t always been going so great at United.



"But I think he is much better as an option. Plus the output and what he can bring, especially when he’s got the freedom and the confidence.

"I just would have preferred to go for a player of that profile, but maybe the wages would be a stumbling block on that."

Rashford won the LaLiga title on loan at Barcelona last season, scoring 14 goals and providing 14 assists in 49 outings across all competitions.

The 28-year-old was subsequently part of the Three Lions' World Cup squad, scoring once as they finished third in North America.



He is set to return to United training this summer, with two years remaining on his current deal at Old Trafford.

Where should Spurs strengthen?

The left-wing position is one of three in which Summers still wants De Zerbi to strengthen before the end of the summer.

Spurs' midfield has already been bolstered by the additions of Sandro Tonali and Mateus Fernandes.

Meanwhile, Jan Paul van Hecke has arrived from Brighton along with free transfers for fellow defender Marcos Senesi and Andrew Robertson.



Revealing where else Spurs need to strengthen, Summers explained: "I’m looking for that next area, that key area for me to be happy as someone on the left, a striker and I think we need a No.10 as well.

"I appreciate we’ve got Xavi Simons, but Xavi Simons is going to miss a huge chunk of the season.

5 Xavi Simons will be sidelined until at least February with a ruptured ACL Credit: PA

"Obviously James Maddison is super injury prone and, please God, he stays fit this year, but I don’t think we can take that chance.



"(Dejan) Kulusevski, who can also play in the 10, we don’t even know what’s going on with Kulusevski, let’s be honest.

"So, yes, I think those three are very important, but the Savinho thing, to be confirmed."

Xavi Simons is set to be sidelined until February after rupturing his ACL at the backend of last season.

He is joined by Dejan Kulusevski, who missed the entirety of the previous campaign with a knee injury of his own.



James Maddison returned to action in April after a torn ACL, but was limited to three substitute appearances totalling 34 minutes.

Sports.title: Man United told to slap down £50m bid for Newcastle star to ‘ruffle some feathers’
Sports.content:
Man United told to slap down £50m bid for Newcastle star to ‘ruffle some feathers’

Manchester United must go all out to sign Newcastle defender Lewis Hall.

That is a view expressed on talkSPORT's Inside Devils amid ongoing links between the Red Devils and the 21-year-old left-back.

3 Hall has established himself as one of the top left-backs in the Premier League Credit: Getty

The former Chelsea player made 46 appearances under Eddie Howe last year, scoring once and registering an assist.

Man United are expected to add a new left-back to their squad, as Michael Carrick plans to build depth ahead of a return to the Champions league.

So far this summer, the Manchester-based outfit have added midfielders Andrey Santos, Youri Tielemans and goalkeeper Karl Darlow to their ranks.

Those three signings aren't enough, according to talkSPORT pundit Flex, who began: "I think we need to do everything we can to get Lewis Hall. Newcastle United is a tough place at the minute.

Rippling the Toon

"There's Bruno Guimaraes who’s probably about to leave for Arsenal, then [Sandro] Tonali and [Anthony] Gordon are already gone.

"People are looking around the place, and players are probably thinking, 'what’s happening here?'

"Harvey Barnes has committed his future, but there were rumours and reports that he [Hall] might have been a bit agitated.

"[Athletic writer] Andy Mitten has been talking, saying he’s someone who Manchester United like.

"We’re not in charge of the purse, but I’m saying you slap £50million down - opening bid - and just ruffle some feathers in there.

"Newcastle could say, 'Listen, we can’t have this because fans are going to turn this place upside down.'

3 Hall was a standout player for the North East side last term, despite not being picked for the World Cup squad Credit: Getty

"You can’t lose Tonali, Guimaraes, Gordon and Hall in one window, plus Isak last season. They will say absolutely not. So for the fans, they might put their foot down and say, 'Sorry Lewis'.

"But then he might put his foot down and say, ‘I’m off, I don’t want to play here.'"

Man United pre-season on MUTV Fans can watch Michael Carrick prepare for the new season and how the squad is shaping up across Finland, Norway, Sweden and Ireland. MUTV is the home of all Manchester United pre-season fixtures. It’s the opportunity to watch new faces, young players, returning names, tactical clues and the first signs of what United might become over the next season. MUTV on Sky: £7 extra a month. Existing Sky TV customers only. 31 day rolling contract. Cancel anytime with 31 days’ notice. Requires compatible Sky Q or Sky Stream boxes.

Newcastle denied any falling out between Hall and Howe following media reports which highlighted the player's frustrations.

However, leading up to the World Cup, the youngster was granted limited minutes towards the conclusion of the campaign.

It is understood he feels the lack of game time was a factor that contributing to his omission from the Three Lions squad that travelled stateside.

Newcastle eventually finished a disappointing 12th in the Premier League, having achieved a fifth-placed finish to secure Champions League qualification the previous year.

3 Shaw has played nearly every minute under Carrick Credit: Getty

Levelling up

Presenter Angelina Kelly added: "If I was Lewis Hall I would feel disrespected that you’ve lost your place to Dan Burn. That cost him his place at the World Cup, essentially because of what Eddie Howe decided to do at Newcastle.

"So, I would be absolutely fuming if I was him, and I would be looking at Newcastle and thinking, ‘you don’t value me, so I’m going to go somewhere that will.’

"I think Man United would value him because, we have to be honest about our full-backs, we’ve been struggling.

"Are Diogo Dalot and Luke Shaw of the calibre we need to challenge for a Premier League title? No."

Newcastle have not sold a player to United since Andy Cole completed a then-British record £7million move in January 1995.

Hall scored twice at Old Trafford during the 2023/24 campaign in what was a 3-0 victory for Newcastle in the Carabao Cup and again in a 3-2 defeat at the end of that season.

Sports.title: Brazilian footballer slapped with unusual punishment for breaking opponent’s leg
Sports.content:
A Brazilian footballer been banned for up to six months after being handed an unusual punishment for breaking another player’s leg.

Internacional defender Victor Gabriel was shown a straight red card for a sickening challenge on Cruzeiro winger Gabriel Pec last week.



5 Gabriel has been handed a serious punishment for his studs-up red card challenge Credit: ge

Pec, who was making his debut for Cruzeiro after joining from LA Galaxy, was left with a fractured left tibia after the studs-up tackle.

And while Gabriel was immediately given his marching orders on the pitch, he has now been dealt an even harsher sanction.

Eye for an eye

Brazil’s Superior Court of Sports Justice - the country’s highest independent body for discipline - has dished out a never-before-seen punishment.



Gabriel has now been suspended until Pec returns to training following his recovery from the leg break.

With such injuries having no clear timeline for recovery, the ban has been capped at a maximum of six months.



Brazil’s Superior Court of Sports Justice said: “The offender may remain suspended until the injured party is able to return to training, respecting a maximum period of 180 days.”

While Gabriel is now staring at a lengthy spell out of action, he can still launch an appeal on the decision.



The 25-year-old told the court that his horror challenge was 'a completely unfortunate incident'.

Gabriel had only been on the pitch for 14 minutes when he flew into Pec as he looked to stop a Cruzeiro counter attack.

The referee initially played the advantage before pulling play back to send off the Internacional man, while Pec was stretchered off after blood could be seen pouring from his leg.

5 Gabriel sent Pec flying into the air with his horror challenge Credit: ge



5 Gabriel put his head in his hands after being given his marching orders Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

At his hearing, Gabriel told the court: "I apologised to him [Pec] and offered my help.

"I asked him ‌to forgive me for not having had any ill intent, and all I could do at that moment was pray for him.

"Since that night, it's been incredibly difficult for me. My whole life I've prepared for moments of happiness, and instead, it's been sleepless nights."



Punishments for a red card vary according to country, with Premier League and EFL players getting a one-match ban, which can be extended to three for serious foul play or violent conduct.

UEFA and FIFA also both ban players for one match but can add extra sanctions, such as a fine, for an especially serious offence.

US player Folarin Balogun was fined $40,000 (£30,000) for 'serious foul play' during the World Cup, but controversially saw his one-game ban suspended after President Donald Trump's intervention with FIFA President Gianni Infantino.

5 Gabriel had been making his 16th league appearance of the season, which ended in dismissal Credit: Getty



Road to recovery

As both players prepare for a lengthy spell away from the pitch, Pec has since undergone successful surgery following the career-threatening tackle.

In a statement shared on Instagram, the seven-cap Brazil Under-23s star wrote: “The surgery was successfully completed.

“To the honour and glory of God. Without Him, none of this would have been possible.

“I thank and praise the Lord for the lives of the doctors – Sergio, Rodrigo and Gustavo.



“I also want to thank all the supporters, family members, friends and staff. Thank you for so many messages of love and affection.

“In the midst of this challenge, I have chosen to keep my eyes fixed on Christ.

5 Pec joined Cruzeiro earlier in July after two years at MLS side LA Galaxy

“He is my strength, my refuge, my fortress, where I find peace and joy. And I have been learning to find contentment even in the midst of trials.



“I am doing my best to recover as well as possible and as quickly as I can so I can continue doing what I love. My dreams and goals remain intact.”

After both players' saw their involvement end with the horror tackle, Pec's Cruzeiro teammates went on to claim a 2-1 win in the Brazilian top-flight clash with Internacional.

Sports.title: Saudi boxing chief Turki Alalshikh on verge of breaking into English football with EFL club
Sports.content:
Saudi boxing chief Turki Alalshikh on verge of breaking into English football with EFL club

Saudi boxing supremo Turki Alalshikh is on the verge of breaking into English football with Derby County.

According to reports, the independent football regulator is set to make a decision on Alalshikh's investment into the Championship club next week.

3 Alalshikh has transformed boxing since his involvement in the sport Credit: Getty

The Daily Telegraph's John Percy states that the EFL have completed all the necessary background checks on the Saudi Arabian businessman.

And sources suggest that the Rams are confident that the major investment will be approved after the interest first emerged in May.

Derby have been out of the Premier League since 2008 when they recorded the worst season in Premier League history.

They managed to accumulate just 11 points and have been into League One since then as well.

But Alalshikh is prepared to invest heavily and try to return the Rams to England's top flight.

This wouldn't be the first time that Alalshikh has involved himself in football, though.

He has owned Spanish club Almeria and Egyptian side Pyramids FC in the past but has been looking to invest in EFL clubs.

Alalshikh's wealth

The latest reports suggest that Alalshikh is worth $2.8billion, and he has accumulated that wealth from various means.

He is the chairman of the Saudi GEA and is heavily involved in boxing.

Alalshikh is one of the leading figureheads in Riyadh Season, which has transformed boxing and put on some of the biggest fights in history.

3 Alalshikh doesn't lack ambition or money Credit: Getty

He is widely seen as the mastermind behind the 'Battle of Britain' between Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua.

A new boxing venture between he and Dana White and Frank Warren known as Zuffa Boxing has been brought into existence with big plans.

Alalashikh is also a close advisor to the Crown Prince of Saudi Arabia, Mohammed bin Salman.

Advice

talkSPORT's Simon Jordan revealed last year that he advised Alalshikh on which English club to buy.

So, his interest in English football has been around for over a year now.

He actually told the Saudi supremo to buy Sheffield Wednesday.

3 Derby could be set for a very bright future Credit: Shutterstock

Speaking about that conversation in 2025, Jordan said: “If I was buying a football club and I was really motivated and had your kind of dough, I would buy Sheffield Wednesday."

Expanding on that, Jordan said: “I told him that. We’ll see what they do; they are captains of their own ship, aren’t they?

“Be careful what you wish for. We’ve already got enough foreign investment in our football clubs, but if this is the direction of travel, that’s the way I’d go.

"It’s a big football club.

“There’s a reason why Hillsborough got used up to a point, for FA Cup semi-finals.

“But I’ve been to that club, I’ve watched it, I’ve seen the fan base. I know the Saudis can look across the city at Sheffield United and think their mate who owns that football club hasn’t had the greatest of times over there, but I think it’s a powerhouse."

“You buy a powerhouse like Sheffield Wednesday that’s in Yorkshire, not just Sheffield, that could be garnered and pushed forward, no disrespect to [current owner, Dejphon] Chansiri, but somehow or another he’s managed to steal defeat from the jaws of victory."

In the end, Alalshikh chose not to take Jordan's advice but his interest in English football never went away.

He is now one step away from adding Derby to a growing portfolio of sporting acquisitions.

Sports.title: Idi Amin's grandson accuses boxing officials of bias after being disqualified for headbutting English opponent at Commonwealth Games: 'It's bulls***!'
Sports.content:
Idi Amin’s grandson accused officials of conspiring against him after he was disqualified for headbutting England’s Damar Thomas.

Ugandan super heavyweight Aziz Abdul is a descendant of the country’s brutal despot who murdered hundreds of thousands during his regime.

Before he became president in 1971, Amin was also an accomplished boxer.

He is alleged to have fathered 50 children and Abdul, 25, who goes by the nickname Ringo, claimed he was on a mission to be crowned ‘the new King of Scotland’ before his fight was terminated by judges in the third round.

The Last King of Scotland is a 2006 historical drama that depicts the Amin dictatorship through the perspective of Nicholas Garrigan, a fictional Scottish doctor.

‘All I can say about this is the referee’s decision is not right and I am not happy,’ said Abdul. ‘This n***** next time, I will get him. Anytime in the future. Two years, five years, 10 years. I will show him that Aziz Ringo is a real warrior.

Idi Amin’s grandson Aziz Abdul (left) accused officials of racism after he was disqualified for headbutting England’s Damar Thomas (right) in their Commonwealth Games bout

‘When you watch the previous fights of England, their boxers create a lot of fouls and they play a lot of bull****. They cannot judge them wrong. I took a light punch and they counted. I landed a heavy punch on him and they deduct my points and warn me.

'Of course it’s unfair. I’m a black African, I know. It’s God’s plan. I don’t know why the officials are scared about this fight. Why can’t they let this fight continue.’

Abdul claimed the officials wanted to see a British representative in the final.

‘How can I headbutt someone?’ he said. ‘I would not headbutt someone. He is the real person they wanted to win. He was the winner before. I knew if I could not get a knockout then I would not win the fight because he’s at home. It’s an away match for me here. All I say is it’s God’s plan and I wish him good luck for his next fight.’

Sports.title: Rio Ngumoha steps up amid Bradley Barcola speculation, the classy 18-year-old at the back and the star of the show shines again: Liverpool 1-0 Wrexham TAKEAWAYS
Sports.content:
The Andoni Iraola era continued to gather pace in New York as Liverpool beat Wrexham thanks to Rio Ngumoha’s second-half goal.

At the iconic home of the New York Yankees baseball team, Ngumoha cut in from the right wing – pretty much second base on this slapdash, bumpy football pitch – and scored via a deflection.

It is Liverpool’s second win of this pre-season tour of the United States having beaten Sunderland in Nashville last week and they now fly back to their training base in Chicago to take on Leeds on Sunday.

Like in the first friendly, there were plenty of minutes for youngsters given the long list of absentees from Iraola’s first fortnight.

Florian Wirtz, Ryan Gravenberch and Alexander Isak remained at base in Chicago while Federico Chiesa was ruled out through illness, according to boss Iraola.

Daily Mail Sport's Reds expert LEWIS STEELE was in situ in The Bronx to bring you the top talking points from leg two of Liverpool’s tour.

Liverpool narrowly beat Wrexham 1-0 in a pre-season friendly at Yankee Stadium in New York

It means that Andoni Iraola has now won his first two games in charge of the Reds

Rio’s right in the thick of it

Liverpool are stepping up their pursuit of Bradley Barcola and hope to strike an agreement with Paris Saint-Germain over the £145million-rated winger.

When Sky Sports posted on X asking readers whether it would be a good signing, former Liverpool defender Jamie Carragher replied: ‘No he plays on the opposite flank!

‘LFC currently have three players who could play from the left in Rio (Ngumoha), (Cody) Gakpo and (Florian) Wirtz and no one who plays from the right.’

It is a salient point – their attack is and will be more lopsided if and when Barcola arrives. Victor Munoz, the early-summer signing from Osasuna, also prefers playing on the left though is said to be more versatile.

Ngumoha, therefore, was trialled on the right wing here in New York.

Was it a perfect performance? No, he was quiet at times – just as he was in Nashville on the left, by the way – but it was Ngumoha who stepped up with the decisive moment to open the scoring in the 75th minute.

It was a slightly lucky finish given the significant deflection off the Wrexham defender but it counts the same and probably a product of players backing off him to his frightening speed and trickery.

Anyone for Barcola and Ngumoha on either side of Isak on the opening day?

Rio Ngumoha scored the only goal of the game and showed why he can be an asset on the right wing

Can Nyoni save Reds millions on midfield upgrade?

There are plenty of calls from the fanbase for Liverpool to sign a new midfielder but Trey Nyoni might be the answer they are all craving.

Nyoni, 19, signed from Leicester in 2023 and has made 20 appearances for the first team, largely off the substitutes bench in the cups.

He played 21 minutes in the Premier League last term but given Alexis Mac Allister and Ryan Gravenberch both saw their form dip, the teenager could probably feel aggrieved that he did not get on the pitch more.

Nyoni can play as a No6, as he did here, or further forward and has even played at centre-half and in the front three over his career. Mr Versatile.

But the deep-lying position is where he truly thrives. Having watched him extensively for the youth teams, Nyoni is best when showing for the ball and making the game tick, dictating possession with a simple pass-and-move, Spanish-like style.

Could this be his year? If so, it could save the Reds millions.

Shame about Ndukwe

Ifeanyi Ndukwe has looked a classy defender in his two pre-season appearances – but do not get excited just yet.

The 18-year-old, who signed from Austria Wien this summer, cannot play for Liverpool this season as he does not yet have the required points total to obtain a work visa. That’s Brexit for you, folks.

There will be a long list of clubs queuing up to take him on loan, then, given his calm performances against Wrexham and Sunderland in pre-season. He is composed in possession and sniffs out danger defensively.

Dominik Szoboszlai was head and shoulders above the rest at the Yankee Stadium

Noting Liverpool’s defensive crisis – Joe Gomez, Jeremy Jacquet and Giovanni Leoni are unfit, while Virgil van Dijk is now 35 and not on this tour – Ndukwe could have got some minutes this year so it is a crying shame that red tape will prevent that.

Alongside him, Luke Chambers looked equally as assured. Now 22, Chambers has had loans at Kilmarnock, Wigan and Charlton but is a classy footballer whose journey has been halted somewhat by injuries.

Chambers can play at left back and left centre-back so could be a handy squad player to keep around.

Szoboszlai Hungary for more as Elliott steps up

Dominik Szoboszlai was head and shoulders above the rest at the Yankee Stadium – fitter, stronger, faster. Wrexham could not get near him.

The Hungary captain was also wearing the armband for Liverpool with Virgil van Dijk absent from this pre-season tour.

Szoboszlai, who signed a new long-term contract earlier this month, has eyes on taking on the captaincy long-term and might get the nod for vice-captain this season, with Alisson also in the running for said vacancy after Andy Robertson’s departure.

Whether or not he takes on that mantle, it is clear he is growing as a leader on and off the pitch. Time and again here, the midfielder stormed through the Wrexham midfield like a hot knife through butter.

Harvey Elliott also dazzled and should have had an early assist, though young Joshua Abe fluffed his lines after a clever run off the ball. Elliott could have had a goal for himself later on but was denied by former Liverpool goalkeeper Danny Ward.

Sports.title: Stephen Fleming in line to become England's new Test coach after Brendon McCullum sacking - as New Zealander is chosen by ECB to lead post-Bazball project
Sports.content:
Stephen Fleming in line to become England's new Test coach after Brendon McCullum sacking - as New Zealander is chosen by ECB to lead post-Bazball project

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

England are closing in on Stephen Fleming as their new Test coach following the axing of his fellow New Zealander Brendon McCullum.

Fleming, 53, is viewed as one of cricket’s great strategists, having played 111 Tests for his country, becoming their most successful captain with 28 wins.

Since quitting international cricket in 2008, he has enjoyed a successful coaching career, predominantly with Chennai Super Kings, claiming five Indian Premier League titles before quitting days after McCullum was removed from his position.

Defeat to New Zealand at Trent Bridge in what was Ben Stokes’ final international appearance meant England had not won a series for more than 12 months, forcing a re-think within an ECB hierarchy that resisted change following the deflating 4-1 Ashes defeat last winter.

The ECB declined to comment when contacted on Wednesday, but Daily Mail Sport understands he edged out Englishmen Richard Dawson and Jonathan Trott in the selection process.

One of Fleming’s first tasks will be to determine who succeeds Stokes as England captain.

New Zealander Stephen Fleming is in line to become the new England Men's Test head coach

Fleming has worked as a coach since 2009, but his only roles have come in franchise cricket, including 14 years over two spells at Chennai Super Kings

England are still looking for a new captain after Ben Stokes' retirement earlier this summer

Joe Root stepped in when Stokes was suspended for The Oval Test last month and was being lined up to work alongside McCullum until the end of next year’s Ashes.

That particular succession plan was put into place in order not to over-burden Root’s fellow Yorkshireman Harry Brook.

However, Brook revealed it would be a ‘privilege’ to lead England in all three formats, having made a success of turning around results in his 15-month captaincy of the limited-overs teams.

Appointing Brook, who at 27 is Root’s junior by eight years, now would maintain some continuity as England return to split coaching roles and avoid another captaincy switch within the next 18 months.

Fleming indicated his interest in the post immediately after mutually severing ties with the CSK organisation a fortnight ago. The franchise said it was ‘bringing to a close one of the most successful and enduring partnerships in IPL history.’

Adding: ‘The decision was reached with respect and gratitude, following a series of open and honest discussions between Fleming and the Super Kings management.’

Fleming also ended ties with Super Kings' other franchises - Joburg Super Kings in the SA20 and Texas Super Kings in the United States - where he was head coach.

His appointment would reunite him in a working capacity with McCullum, who viewed his fellow Kiwi as a mentor during their playing days.

It would also take the numbers of New Zealanders across England’s coaching set-up to four: Jeetan Patel and Tim Southee are currently spin and fast bowling coaches respectively.

Some will feel that a lack of homegrown presence is a concern, particularly after managing director Rob Key turned to Australian Marcus North as national selector.

Indeed, only two Englishmen featured on a nine-strong list of potential candidates. Not all received calls, however, suggesting that Fleming became their preferred choice after Andy Flower, the original No 1 target, turned down the chance to interview.

Fleming is well known to the English game, however, having captained Nottinghamshire to the County Championship title and also represented Yorkshire.

As a coach, he also took Southern Brave to the knockout stages of the 2023 and 2024 editions of the Hundred.

Sports.title: UEFA accuse FIFA president of BRIBING nations to back Gianni Infantino's plans to sell stakes in the World Cup - as they step up criticism of controversial proposal
Sports.content:
UEFA accuse FIFA president of BRIBING nations to back Gianni Infantino's plans to sell stakes in the World Cup - as they step up criticism of controversial proposal

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

UEFA have seemingly accused FIFA of bribing associations as they continue to scold Gianni Infantino's plans to sell stakes in the World Cup - criticising FIFA’s self-interest as they pressure associations with a £30million incentive.

FIFA wrote to national associations on Wednesday morning to explain their leaked plans, detailing that a £30m funding package will become available to associations should they sign off on the World Cup private investment plan.

In a letter to the associations, Infantino says associations must decide on the proposal - which would see private investors procure a £3bn interest in the World Cup - by September 19 and explains the financial benefits of approving the project.

In response to the letter, UEFA said: 'Today we have learned of FIFA’s deadline to associations to support their proposals or have the one-off payout offer withdrawn. This says everything you need to know about this plan.

'But having held discussions with many stakeholders across the game, UEFA knows there is significant and growing opposition to FIFA’s scheme. FIFA cannot continue to use our sport to enrich themselves and their friends. We can grow the game correctly. It’s time to prioritise associations, clubs, leagues, players and fans.'

Sources have told Daily Mail Sport that UEFA have scheduled crisis talks with all 55 member nations on Thursday as they rally the troops against FIFA.

Tensions have long been growing between FIFA President Gianni Infantino and UEFA President Aleksander Ceferin, who boycotted the World Cup final

FIFA hope to set up a company responsible for the commercial activity and 'operational delivery of FIFA tournaments', called FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE).

Investment bank J.P. Morgan is FIFA's financial advisor on the project while Joshua Kushner's Thrive Capital is expected to lead the proposed investor group. Kushner is the brother of Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared.

FIFA hope to raise more than £3bn for the venture from a diversified, global investor group which is thought to include sovereign wealth funds.

There are major concerns over what the proposals could mean for the game, including whether FIFA could increase the frequency of tournaments to create more opportunities for financial backers to see a return on their investment.

The European Leagues Association, of which the Premier League is a founding member, said: 'The World Cup should not be for sale. It is not the FIFA President’s private equity asset. Its value is created day in and day out by leagues, clubs, players and supporters who are being left without a voice or a vote on this matter. European Leagues firmly reject this proposal.'

Philippe Diallo, the president of the French Football Federation, called it a 'worrying project that raises many questions'. He added: 'This is worrying because there are no details, yet it touches on one of football’s fundamental assets, the World Cup, which is the world’s greatest sporting event.'

The Confederation of African Football offered a more conciliatory tone, saying in a statement: 'CAF is committed to continue consulting and working together with its Member Associations, FIFA, other Football Confederations and stakeholders in support of increasing financial and other resources for the development and growth of football in Africa and worldwide.'

Infantino and FIFA conducted their own in-house 'interview' on Wednesday without taking any questions from the media.

Sports.title: Man City push for World Cup wonderkid amid doubts over Rodri's future - as Juventus swoop to steal Kerim Alajbegovic from Chelsea's grasp: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
Man City push for World Cup wonderkid amid doubts over Rodri's future - as Juventus swoop to steal Kerim Alajbegovic from Chelsea's grasp: WINDOW WATCH

It's that time of the year again - the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period with clubs looking to make big signings ahead of next season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Juventus swoop to gazump Blues

Juventus have made a £26million bid plus add-ons and a sell-on clause for Chelsea target Kerim Alajbegovic.

The Bayer Leverkusen teenager was leaning towards a move to Chelsea but is now closing on agreement with Juve as they would put him in the first team squad.

Hull City eye Augsburg's Komur

Hull City have asked about Germany U21 midfielder Mert Komur from Augsburg. Hull have also enquired about Rayo Vallecano defender Nobel Mendy.

Reds ramp up Barcola talks

Liverpool have been speaking with Bradley Barcola’s representatives about the France international joining this summer.

A bid is being prepared with Barcola intimating he is keen on moving to Anfield and it is now a question of how negotiations go with his club Paris St Germain.

Bradley Barcola is keen on a move to Anfield this summer

There is a belief a compromise could be reached for less than the £140million that PSG sources initially quoted.

The 23-year-old still has two years left on contract but has indicated he will not be signing a new one amid frustrations at a lack of starting time.

Andoni Iraola wants another goalscoring winger with Victor Munoz already signed.

Man City push for World Cup wonderkid

Manchester City and Lille are holding further negotiations over the proposed £80million transfer of midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi.

The teenage Morocco international is ready to make the move now though Lille would prefer him to stay for another season.

City would want Bouaddi for this season with Real Madrid ready to push for Rodri who is keen to return to Spain for family reasons.

Though they have added Elliot Anderson, they have lost Bernardo Silva and could also sell Nico Gonzalez and Tijjani Reijnders who has interest from Galatasaray and earlier in the summer Atletico Madrid.

The 18-year-old Bouaddi has plenty of admirers but City are ready to meet the terms required to prise him away.

Elsewhere, Marseille goalkeeper Geronimo Rulli is among the names being considered by City.

The 34-year-old Argentina international has been discussed as a candidate to fill the void that will be left by James Trafford's move to Leeds United.

Rulli has one year left on contract and was signed by City ten years ago only to be loaned out to Real Sociedad and eventually sold.

City have been assessing a number of candidates.

Manchester City and Lille are holding further negotiations over the proposed £80million transfer of midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi, who impressed for Morocco at the World Cup

Henderson exit paves way for Chelsea move

Brentford have announced that Jordan Henderson has left the club by mutual consent.

The 36-year-old has held talks with Xabi Alonso ahead of joining Chelsea.

As Daily Mail Sport reported, Brentford are working to sign Mamadou Sangare from Lens and have interest in Pape Sarr from Spurs.

Potters star attracting attention

Stoke City winger Sorba Thomas is attracting interest from Coventry City, West Ham, Stuttgart and Genoa.

The Wales international impressed against Everton in Stoke’s 1-0 friendly win on Tuesday evening and interest has been building in the 27-year-old following his last campaign where he scored ten goals in the Championship.

Stoke are understood to value him around £9million.

Stoke star Sorba Thomas is attracting interest from Coventry, West Ham, Stuttgart and Genoa

Black Cats bound

Toulouse have confirmed they are in talks with Sunderland to sell £25m-rated defender Dayann Methalie.

Olivier Cloarec, the Toulouse president, said: 'Dayann Methalie is one of the most sought-after players,' he said. 'There is no agreement with Sunderland. We were counting on him but the market is such that when there is a certain amount, not selling him would be a management error.'

Boro ask about in-demand Travers

Middlesbrough have made enquiries for Everton goalkeeper Mark Travers over a permanent transfer.

The Republic of Ireland keeper, who started in Everton's friendly defeat to Stoke on Tuesday night, has been the subject of a number of enquiries this summer including from Coventry who finally agreed a £22.5million fee plus add ons with Brighton for Carl Rushworth on Tuesday.

Iliman Ndiaye is subject to interest from Saudi side Al Hilal this summer

Boro have also asked about Manchester United's Radek Vitek but 27-year-old Travers has been at the club before on loan and could prove cheaper. He joined Everton from Bournemouth last year in a four-year deal.

Meanwhile, Everton have still to receive an offer from Al Hilal for Iliman Ndiaye. They are aware of interest but have no desire to sell, though the 26-year-old has turned down offers of a new contract.

Koleosho heads to Paris

Burnley winger Luca Koleosho has completed a permanent move to Ligue 1 side Paris FC for an undisclosed fee.

County in the money

Derby County are close to finalising a major cash injection from Saudi Arabian sports promoter Turki Alalshikh to boost their spending power.

Alalshikh has been looking to invest in Derby having been in talks with owner David Clowes over a proposed deal since May.

The deal has had to go through the Football League and the Independent Football Regulator but there is optimism the deal will be given the go-ahead by next week.

Alalshikh, who has previously owned football clubs in Spain and Egypt and is now among the most powerful figures in world boxing, is looking to buy a stake in the Championship side.As chairman of Saudi Arabia's General Entertainment Authority - and someone who is a prominent figure in the close circle of the country's de facto ruler Mohammed bin Salman - 44-year-old Alalshikh has been criticised by human rights groups for his role in alleged 'sportswashing' by Saudi Arabia.

Clyne flies the Eagles nest again

Crystal Palace have confirmed that Nathaniel Clyne has left the club following the expiration of his contract.

The full back, who made 252 appearances across two stints at Selhurst Park, told Palace TV: 'The last few seasons have given me some of the best days of my life.

'When I started at Crystal Palace we were in the Championship. Now the club is playing European football, having nights like we did in Leipzig.'

Palace remain in talks over a possible permanent deal for Takehiro Tomiyasu, who is training with the club in Como. Discussions are also continuing over defensive targets Chrislain Matsima and Raphael Le Guen.

Takehiro Tomiyasu is currently training with Crystal Palace as he seeks to find a new club

Bees looking to seal £41m Sangare deal

Brentford are closing in on an agreement with Lens for Mamadou Sangare worth around £41million.

As Daily Mail Sport reported yesterday, Brentford moved quickly to fend off competition for the 24-year-old from Crystal Palace.

Brentford are long-term admirers of the player and signing a new central midfielder was a priority even before Chelsea moved for Jordan Henderson. They also like Spurs' Pape Matar Sarr.

Palace man moves to Wrexham

Wrexham have confirmed the signing of Danny Imray from Crystal Palace.

Daily Mail Sport revealed Wrexham's interest on Sunday and they have moved quickly to secure a £4.5million deal plus bonuses should they gain promotion.

The full-back has joined on a four-year contract and linked up with his new teammates on their USA pre-season tour in New York.

The 23-year-old spent last season on loan at Blackpool and West Brom.

City teen heads to Leicester

Manchester City left back Christian McFarlane has joined Leicester on loan.

McFarlane, 19, becomes the third signing through the door at the King Power Stadium this summer. He joins Conor Chaplin and Alex McCarthy in bolstering Russell Martin's squad.

New Leicester boss Russell Martin has bolstered his team's promotion bid with the signing of Man City left back Christian McFarlane

McFarlane said: 'As a player, I’m intense and aggressive at both ends – attacking and defending. I like to make runs in behind and can be a bit of a nuisance for the opposition.

'The way [the manager] wants to play suits me perfectly, so I’m excited to get started.'

Blues close to landing Lund

Birmingham are closing on a deal for Palermo left back Kristoffer Lund.

The 24-year-old Dane spent last season on loan at Cologne but the German side did not take up their £2.5m option to buy.

Solomon set on permanent switch

Manor Solomon wants to leave Tottenham on a permanent transfer amid interest from West Ham.

The Israeli winger’s agent has made it clear he does not wish for another loan move, after spells with Leeds, Villarreal and Fiorentina, and that’s expected to suit Spurs as they look to recoup funds and upgrade their wide options.

Meanwhile, Spurs are closing on agreement with Wolves for Kwasi Senyah. The 16-year-old defensive midfielder and England youth international was wanted by several clubs but will join Spurs once terms are agreed and it is cleared by the FA.

Benfica are showing interest in Spurs left wing-back Souza while Leicester remain hopeful of taking 18-year-old centre back prospect Malachi Hardy.

Manor Solomon's Tottenham career has struggled to take-off since his move from Shakhtar Donetsk

A goalkeeper for Magpies

Newcastle United are proceeding in talks for SPORTING BRAGA goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek who has a £29million release clause.

Daily Mail Sport revealed Newcastle’s interest at the weekend. The 6ft 6in Czech international was pulled out of Braga's squad to face Zeleznicar Pancevo in the Europa Conference League amid talks over his exit.

Rovers return for Vaulks

Wales international Will Vaulks is in talks over a move to Tranmere.

The 32-year-old started his career with the Wirral club but never made a senior appearance.

Vaulks has gone on to play nearly 600 games at Sheffield Wednesday, Cardiff and Rotherham before arriving at Oxford United. He made 38 appearances in the Championship for them last season but is now looking to return home.

Tranmere have also snapped up goalkeeper Harrison Male on a one-year contract. The 25-year-old was a free transfer after he was released by York City earlier this summer.

He played 46 games as the Minstermen pipped Rochdale to the National League title and won Golden Glove after keeping 19 clean sheets.

Elsewhere...

BRIGHTON have handed a first professional contract to defender Tate Ferdinand, 17, son of former Manchester United and England defender Rio.

EVERTON are showing interest in CELTIC right-back Alistair Johnson. The 27-year-old has 63 caps for Canada.

NOTTINGHAM FOREST are closing on the £35m signing of Sporting Lisbon defender Ousmane Diomande.

IPSWICH TOWN are trying to sign Florentino Luis from BURNLEY. The Portuguese midfielder has been talking to HULL CITY.

Click below for all the transfer developments over the last few days...

Tuesday: Man United open to offer for four academy graduates

MONDAY: Leeds close in on deal for James Trafford

SUNDAY: Liverpool seek compromise on Bradley Barcola

SATURDAY: Tottenham continue push for Man City winger Savinho

FRIDAY: Real open talks for Yan Diomande, Chelsea go back to Villa to poach set-piece coach Austin MacPhee... and Brentford bid for West Ham wing back

THURSDAY: Arsenal sign Christos Tzolis in £34million move from Club Brugge as Leeds ramp up talks with Man City's James Trafford

WEDNESDAY: West Ham star Crysencio Summerville set for £60m Saudi Arabia move despite Roma's late attempt to hijack deal

Sports.title: Jamie Carragher warns Liverpool against pursuing Bradley Barcola as he insists £145m PSG star would NOT be the right signing as club continue search for Mo Salah replacement
Sports.content:
Jamie Carragher warns Liverpool against pursuing Bradley Barcola as he insists £145m PSG star would NOT be the right signing as club continue search for Mo Salah replacement

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Jamie Carragher has warned Bradley Barcola should not be viewed as a successor for Mohamed Salah as Liverpool prepare to launch their first offer for the £145million-valued PSG star.

Barcola is understood to be keen to join Liverpool after the club held talks with his representatives in the last week.

The 23-year-old France international has indicated he does not wish to sign a new contract with the European champions and is open to joining Liverpool, who have a long-held interest.

PSG are considering his sale but he still has two years left on his contract and they believe, based on his age, potential and current market prices, that £145m is a fair price.

Former Liverpool star Carragher responded to a post from Sky Sports asking whether Barcola is the right player to replace legendary Reds winger Salah, who left the club on a free transfer this summer.

'No he plays on the opposite flank!' Carragher wrote.

Liverpool are set to make their first offer to PSG for £145m-rated Bradley Barcola

Former Liverpool star Jamie Carragher has warned Barcola is not a suitable replacement for Mohamed Salah

Carragher stressed that Barcola plays on the left, while Liverpool 'desperately' need a right winger after Salah's departure this summer

'LFC currently have three players who could play from the left in Rio/Gakpo/Wirtz & no one who plays from the right.'

Carragher's comments had been backed up by a graphic accompanying the question, which showed that Barcola has had vastly more time playing on the left wing than the right for PSG in the Champions League.

He expanded on his comments further after a Liverpool fan suggested Rio Ngumoha should be shifted from his favoured role on the left to play on the right.

Carragher stressed that Liverpool need to 'desperately' sign a right winger ahead of the season, with Salah's departure having created a need for a high class option in the position.

'Well Rio has always played from the left so that’s obviously his best position, Gakpo should move really but who knows, I’m interested to see where Wirtz plays, if he’s 10 Dom plays CM,' Carragher added.

'I’m not sure about that.

'Need a right winger desperately!'

Daily Mail Sport reported that Liverpool will seek a compromise on the £145m figure demanded by PSG, with Barcola's price reputed to have been closer to £75million last summer when they first sounded out his representatives.

Barcola is not a regular starter for Luis Enrique's side and they have been pursuing RB Leipzig's Yan Diomande, which would have pushed him further down the pecking order, only for Real Madrid to declare their intent to sign the Ivory Coast international on Friday – which is now close to completion.

Liverpool also had an £85million proposal rejected for Diomande, but Barcola has always been in their thinking.

Liverpool are seeking to strengthen new boss Andoni Iraola's attacking options

He has the skillset to suit Andoni Iraola's style and can provide a serious goal threat following the void left by Mohamed Salah's departure.

Across the past two seasons at PSG, Barcola scored 34 goals and assisted a further 28.

He played in all eight of France's World Cup matches this year, scoring three goals, including one against England in the third-place play-off.

Arsenal and Bayern Munich also retain interest in Barcola while Chelsea made enquiries earlier in the summer.

Sports.title: 'I used to hate the water and cried before swimming lessons!': Meet 18-year-old sensation Filip Nowacki, the Jersey A-level student who beat his idol Adam Ramsay-Peaty
Sports.content:
During Filip Nowacki’s childhood, which was not all that long ago, his parents gave him an ultimatum.

‘Me and my friends would go out to Greve de Lecq, which is a popular beach where you can go cliff jumping,’ explains the 18-year-old from Jersey.

‘It’s a five-minute swim across to the rocks where you jump in. It’s maybe 15 metres high. It’s a bit hairy for a responsible adult but it’s a good adrenaline kick.

‘It’s very important you know how to swim so my parents wanted me to be able to keep myself afloat when I went out with my mates.’

When they doubled down on his swimming lessons, little did they know that Nowacki would be winning gold and silver medals at the 2026 Commonwealth Games.

The teenager, who is still waiting for his A-level results, has been Glasgow’s breakthrough star. He beat his idol, Adam Ramsay-Peaty, on Saturday night and has become one of swimming’s overnight sensations.

Teenager Filip Nowacki, who is still waiting for his A-level results, has been Glasgow’s breakthrough star after beating his idol, Adam Ramsay-Peaty, on Saturday night

Last year, after finishing his lower-sixth exams, he won the 200m breaststroke at the Junior European Championships with a time that would have medalled at the 2024 Olympics in Paris

Sitting in the team room in Glasgow, beaming ear to ear after his victory, Nowacki takes Daily Mail Sport through his journey to the podium.

His surname has Polish roots. In 2002, his mum and dad boarded a one-way flight to Jersey and landed jobs in accounting and construction.

‘They took me to swimming lessons when I was five or six and I hated it,’ he recalls. ‘I hated the water, I hated getting wet and I cried before I got in. When I was seven or eight, I started to enjoy it. I went for a trial taster session at Jersey swimming club and thought, “This is a bit of me”.

‘You’re never far from the sea in Jersey. You can go for open-water swims but I’ve never been the biggest, so I had to get my elbows out because of all the waves. I definitely preferred sticking to the black line of the pool.’

At secondary school, students were pushed to take part in all sports. One look at Nowacki’s slight 5ft 10in frame, however, will tell you that he was not destined for contact sports.

‘I played a bit of house rugby but I tended to run away from the ball!’ he laughs.

‘I did a lot of sports growing up, but mainly swimming, cycling and running. When I was 14, I went to the swimming nationals. It was at Ponds Forge in Sheffield and that really sparked my journey. I was between 10th and 20th in all events when I arrived and I walked away with four golds. That was my first experience of what it feels like to win.’

Nowacki has never looked back. His swimming coach at the Jersey Tigers convinced him to move to Millfield boarding school for his sixth form studies, where he could spend more time perfecting his technique.

Last year, after finishing his lower-sixth exams, he won the 200m breaststroke at the Junior European Championships with a time that would have medalled at the 2024 Olympics in Paris.

People talk about these games as a launchpad for greatness and his name is worth remembering for LA 2028

‘This is the first competition where I haven’t had maths or physics to worry about in the background,’ he explains. ‘I had all my A levels leading up to these Games, which was quite intense. I was spending a lot of time on my iPad reading over notes and making flash cards. Knowing I don’t have any schoolwork to do whilst I’ve been here has been quite nice!’

Nowacki has been staying in the same hotel as Ramsay-Peaty, overlooking the River Clyde. He is not blessed with his senior’s upper body strength – joking that maybe one day he will ‘get hench’.

While Ramsay-Peaty changed the game with his bulldog-like power, Nowacki is more like a skimming stone. ‘I saw Adam in the lift after my race on Tuesday night and he congratulated me. I’ve looked up to him for most of my life. I was eight years old when he won his first Olympic gold so to be racing in the lane next to him is pretty special.

‘We went for a coffee before the Commonwealth Games and I peppered him with questions for an hour and a half. I’m trying to draw as much experience from him as possible. Going up against some of those lads in the 100 breast can be a challenge because they’re so much bigger than me. I’m not the tallest of men and I’d love to put on muscle but there’s no point, given the momentum I’m carrying in the 200. If I get too big, I’m going to end up fighting the water, rather than gliding through it.’

Nowacki has been gliding through the Glaswegian waters with an effortless cadence. People talk about these games as a launchpad for greatness and his name is worth remembering for LA 2028.

‘Every athlete dreams of the Olympic Games,’ he says. ‘They are staging the swimming in a 40-thousand capacity arena which will be unreal. Coming here and winning medals is a big step in the right direction.’

'He's swimming times that have never been seen from an 18-year-old'

By Michael Jamieson, Olympic silver medallist and TNT Sports expert

Watching Filip Nowacki in the pool brings back memories of seeing Kosuke Kitajima win double gold for Japan at the 2004 and 2008 Olympics.

They’re both relatively small but they possess so much natural speed. Filip is swimming times that have never been seen from an 18-year-old so he’s a real trailblazer.

You don’t want to pile expectation onto his shoulders but he’s already right at the sharp end of the global rankings. There are Japanese and Chinese athletes who are swimming slightly faster times but Filip has just come out of juniors and he’s already right behind them.

He lined up against Adam Ramsay-Peaty in the 50 and 100m breaststroke this week and everyone has been comparing their physical appearance. They’re very different.

For me, Filip naturally set up as a 200m swimmer. Technically, he is absolutely perfect. He’s got a bit of a longer stroke, with a lower stroke rate. You can see the leg drive come in as his hands shoot forward. His streamline position is great and the timing is perfect. It’s a flawless cascade of movement patterns.

With some of the heavier guys, like Adam, you see their hips drop in the last 50m over four lengths. That’s when it becomes harder and harder for those heavier, muscly guys. Filip’s hips are high when he drives his legs and his body sits right on top of the water. He seems to have the perfect blend between speed, technique and timing. That’s married up with the fitness and endurance he has for the 200m.

'Watching Filip Nowacki in the pool brings back memories of seeing Kosuke Kitajima win double gold for Japan at the 2004 and 2008 Olympics,' says TNT Sports expert Jamieson

'He lined up against Adam Ramsay-Peaty in the 50 and 100m breaststroke and everyone has been comparing their physical appearance. They’re very different,' says Jamieson

He’s burst onto the scene over the last 12 months. He’s won junior titles and swam the 2.07 benchmark that sets apart the world class. Because he speaks so eloquently, I don’t think there was any doubt that he would be affected by the occasion of these Games.

The exciting thing is he has still got areas where he can improve. His muscle mass will increase as he develops towards the 2028 Olympics, where he should be in firm medal contention.

It’s a monumental step to win your first senior title immediately after your junior career. He’s going to emerge as the face of the men’s breaststroke scene and his support team need to manage that. He’s made it look so easy and that’s fantastic news for both Jersey and Great Britain.
