Sports.title: Fans “don’t understand” clipping and think F1’s racing is great – Domenicali | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Formula 1 CEO Stefano Domenicali believes fans can’t tell the difference between genuine racing and position changes caused by differences in energy deployment.

The new power units introduced this year have caused an increase in passes which arise when drivers deploy energy at different points on the track, creating what some termed “yo-yo racing”

Domenicali has previously rejected criticisms of F1’s racing in 2026 but has conceded the sport must make changes to its deeply unpopular engine regulations. However he claimed fans have had an extremely positive reaction to the racing this year.

“There is a lot of action on the track,” Domenicali told the BBC. “People are loving it. They are focused on what is happening on the track.

“They don’t understand our technology, division [definition] of ‘clipping’, or whatever it is, because it’s too technical for the wider base that we have. Therefore, the effect on the track has been widely super-positive about [among] the fans.”

F1 drivers have reiterated their unhappiness with the current power units following recent races. McLaren’s Oscar Piastri described them as “a crap way of going racing” and Hungarian Grand Prix winner Lando Norris said F1 had ruined its regulations because it was desperate to attract new engine manufacturers such as Audi.

Max Verstappen described how he “started laughing” during his first experience of driving Spa-Francorchamps under F1’s 2026 rules in Red Bull’s simulator. Fernando Alonso said the current F1 cars have less energy than F2 machines over a lap of Spa.

Domenicali said he has told drivers to offer “constructive” comments and denied he was trying to censor them. “I prefer to discuss things in that respect in four walls to find solutions.”

Despite Domenicali’s repeated defence of F1’s engine regulations, the series has reacted quickly to introduce changes, some of which came into effect after the fifth round. It intends to abandon the ’50-50′ power split between combustion and electrical energy – a key feature of the current power units which F1 promoted heavily in the years before the new engines arrived – moving to a 60-40 split by 2028.

Sports.title: “Don’t waste time racing him”: Mercedes told Antonelli not to defend lead from Norris | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Mercedes looked unstoppable after they won the first six rounds of 2026 in a row.

Only Ferrari had managed to beat them to victory prior to the Hungarian Grand Prix. But in a sign of the change in the competitive situation at the front of the field, Mercedes recognised they couldn’t contain the threat from another of their rivals: McLaren.

As Lando Norris closed on race leader Andrea Kimi Antonelli in the second half of the Hungarian Grand Prix, Mercedes were convinced their driver, on older tyres, would not be able to keep the world champion behind.

On lap 44, two laps before Norris caught the Mercedes, race engineer Peter Bonnington told Antonelli: “Norris at 1.8 [seconds behind], we don’t want to waste time racing him.”

Two laps later, Norris cruised up to the back of Antonelli’s car. He made a bid to pass on the inside at turn one but ran wide, allowing Antonelli to accelerate back ahead as they approached turn two.

“Let’s not waste time here, Kimi,” Bonnington reminded him.

Norris’s fresher tyres appeared to make it inevitable he would pass the Mercedes. Antonelli later made another pit stop, dropping him even further behind the McLaren.

However in the cool-down room after the race Norris suggested to Antonelli he only had a limited window of opportunity to pass him.

“I honestly thought if I didn’t pass you the lap I passed I would have been stuck behind you,” said Norris. “The last few corners you were very strong, we were just terrible in the last few corners.”

Sports.title: IndyCar reveals new, lighter IR-28 chassis for 2028 season | IndyCar
Sports.content:
IndyCar has revealed the first images of the new Dallara IR-28 chassis which the series will introduce in 2028.

As with the series’ current car, the new model will appear in two guises: one for road and street courses and another for oval speedways such as Indianapolis.

The IR-28 will be the series’ first all-new chassis since the current DW12 debuted in 2012. The cars have undergone various alterations since then, including the addition of the ‘Aeroscreen’ in 2020.

IndyCar will also replace its current 2.2-litre V6 turbo engines with new 2.4-litre versions. It predicts the upgraded power units will produce up to 760bhp.

With the IR-28 chassis projected to weigh around 45 kilograms less than the current version, IndyCar expects its 2028 cars to offer a greater power-to-weight ratio.

IndyCar President J Douglas Boles said the new car “will take our sport into an exciting new era.”

“As you can imagine, a project of this magnitude takes an incredible amount of planning, collaboration and execution. I would like to thank all of our partners including Dallara, Chevrolet, Honda, Firestone and Shell, who have worked tirelessly to create a package that will enhance IndyCar’s already incredible competition and industry-leading growth.”

Reigning IndyCar champion Alex Palou said: “Seeing the car for the first time made me even more excited about where IndyCar is going. The design is super cool and feels like a proper next step for the series while still looking like an IndyCar series car.

“I think the fans are going to love it, and as a driver I cannot wait to get behind the wheel. The most important thing is that we keep the close, fun racing that makes IndyCar special, and from what I’ve seen, we’re heading in a really good direction.”

Sports.title: WEC definitively cancels its 2026 Qatar race due to war in Middle East | WEC
Sports.content:
The World Endurance Championship has confirmed its race in Qatar will not go ahead this year.

Its race at the Losail International Circuit , which Formula 1 is due to visit in November, was originally due to open the season in March. It was cancelled following America and Israel’s bombing of Iran, which prompted retaliatory strikes against Qatar and other countries in the region.

WEC originally rescheduled its Qatar round for October. However following the resumption of bombing in the region in recent weeks, and despite another recent pause, WEC has finally abandoned its efforts to hold the race.

“I would like to warmly thank Losail International Circuit and their team in Qatar for their understanding in these times,” said FIA WEC CEO Frederic Lequien. “We have been in constant dialogue with LIC and QMMF [Qatar Motor and Motorcycle Federation] and are proud of the close, long-standing relationships we have built.” He said the series “will return in the future.”

The series has also called off its planned season finale in Bahrain.

The Circuit de Catalunya has will hold a WEC event on October 16th to 18th, in what it called an “exceptional round.” It will be the series’ first visit to the Spanish circuit.

F1 cancelled two of its planned races in the Middle East, the Bahrain and Saudi Arabian grands prix, which were scheduled for April. The Bahrain Grand Prix has been reinstated to the calendar in name, but it will take place 6,000 kilometres away in Malaysia.

The final two rounds of the F1 season are due to take place in Qatar and Abu Dhabi on November 29th and December 6th respectively. F1 CEO Stefano Domenicali has previously said the series has a contingency plan in case those rounds cannot take place.

Sports.title: “It was the throttle pedal”: What Mercedes told Russell about his terrible start | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Mercedes gave George Russell further feedback on what caused the problem with his car which ruined his start to the Hungarian Grand Prix.

Russell’s slow getaway from sixth on the grid dropped him to the rear of the field and dealt a further blow to his world championship hopes. When he asked his team what had gone wrong his race engineer Marcus Dudley immediately replied: “Anti-stall.”

The anti-stall system activates to prevent an engine from stopping when the revs dip too low. Russell would obviously be aware his anti-stall had activated, so as he continued around the opening lap he replied: “Yeah, I know anti-stall,” then a few corners later added: “Was I on target or not?”

“Clutch [was] two percent shallow,” Dudley replied. “It was the throttle pedal, you backed off at high RPM.”

Russell’s revs dipped around the time the fourth red light illuminated prior to the start. After finishing the race seventh he told Dudley: “Not sure what happened at the start. The revs were just running away from me.”

Afterwards Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff said the poor start was due to the car, not the driver. Mercedes changed Russell’s power unit overnight after he suffered a water leak during qualifying.

“His problem at the start was fully on us as a team and it isn’t good enough,” said Wolff. “He has suffered too many of these problems. We are doing everything we can to get on top of them, but it is unfortunately another issue that has cost him again today.”

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Deputy team principal Bradley Lord said Russell’s engine revs had risen beyond what he had requested. “As the drivers wait for the start, they hold what are called their ‘wait revs’ which is holding the engine’s rpm at a specific level,” he explained in a video released by the team. “As George was doing that, the revs actually rose out of proportion to what he was asking for from the throttle.

“The revs hit the rev limiter at the maximum rpm that the engine allows at that point, and then George tried to get it back under control to optimise and control his start. He wasn’t able to do so and as he was lifting right off the throttle to under 10% of throttle demand.

“The lights went out and so he made a start with effectively much too little throttle through no fault of his own. That meant the anti-stall kicked in so he dropped to the back of the field.”

Russell revealed his power unit problem in qualifying had an unusual side effect. Although his power delivery was unaffected, the lost water sprayed onto his rear tyres during his flying lap, causing a drop in temperature.

Sports.title: How Piastri’s quick thinking avoided a slow pit stop early in the race | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Oscar Piastri demonstrated a keen eye and quick thinking as he avoided a setback which could have cost him the lead of the Hungarian Grand Prix early on.

The McLaren driver was doomed not to finish the race for reasons beyond his control. But he was fully on top of the situation after snatching the lead from team mate Lando Norris at the start.

While Piastri led a queue comprising Norris, Max Verstappen and the Ferrari drivers, his McLaren team was alert to the threat from Lewis Hamilton behind. They summoned Piastri into the pits soon after Hamilton pitted and Verstappen responded.

However as he exited the penultimate corner on lap 15, Piastri spotted the ailing Cadillac of Valtteri Bottas ahead, smoke pouring from its front-left wheel. McLaren did not have time to tell him to stay out but Piastri made the call for himself.

“I was going to get blocked by the Cadillac,” Piastri told his race engineer Tom Stallard after choosing to pass by the pit entrance. Had he come in, he could well have been delayed behind the Cadillac, which Bottas brought to a stop after rounding the long final corner.

Piastri came in the next time by and made his pit stop while retaining the net lead of the race.

Sports.title: Carlos Monzon Ends Legendary Career Against Rodrigo Valdez
Sports.content:
Valdez, 31, entered the ring determined to avenge the unanimous decision defeat he suffered against Monzon in the same venue the previous year. The Colombian made an immediate statement by dropping Monzon in the second round, the first time the champion had visited the canvas in approximately 13 years. The knockdown briefly suggested the aging champion might finally be vulnerable.

Instead, Monzon settled into the disciplined style that frustrated challengers throughout his reign. Using his height, reach and accurate jab, he gradually took control while forcing Valdez to absorb clean punches from long range. The fight changed once Monzon opened a deep cut over Valdez’s left eye. Damage soon developed around the right eye as well, leaving blood streaming down the challenger’s face through the championship rounds.

Valdez refused to retreat, continuing to press the action despite the punishment. Monzon landed the cleaner punches down the stretch as fatigue gradually slowed the challenger.

The judges awarded Monzon a unanimous decision by scores of 147-144, 145-143 and 144-141 after 15 demanding rounds. Valdez required hospital treatment for stitches following the bout after absorbing severe facial damage.

Moments after the victory, Monzon announced his retirement.

“I think I showed everyone I’m one of the great ones. But it’s over now. I’m going to start living like a human being tonight.”

The victory closed one of boxing’s greatest middleweight careers. Monzon never fought again, retiring as the undisputed champion after seven years atop the division. Valdez returned four months later to defeat Bennie Briscoe for the vacant middleweight championship, ensuring that the final challenger of Monzon’s reign also became the man who succeeded him.

Sports.title: Shane Mosley Backs Keyshawn Davis as WBO Purse Bid Looms
Sports.content:
WBO Championship Committee chairman Gustavo Olivieri confirmed the bidding is set for July 30 at 11:00 a.m. AST from the organization’s headquarters in San Juan, Puerto Rico. The minimum bid is $200,000, with Haney entitled to 75 percent of the winning bid as champion and Davis receiving the remaining 25 percent.

Dan Rafael also reported Haney’s side has agreed to terms, leaving the multi-million-dollar gap between Top Rank’s offer and Keyshawn’s asking price as the final obstacle.

Mosley offered his opinion on the matchup after previously training Haney.

“It’s going to be a very difficult fight for both guys. Haney has good fast feet and Keyshawn has to be able to nullify those fast feet that Devin has. Once he does that, I think Keyshawn has the more power,” said Mosley to Fighthype. “He has the better punch. I lean toward Keyshawn Davis because he’s a fighter like me. I love the way he fights, but it could be a hard fight for him if he doesn’t do the right thing.”

Mosley also praised Haney’s unanimous decision over Brian Norman Jr., saying he recognized techniques from their earlier work together.

“I liked that. He did a good job. It seemed like he used some of the things I showed him, the punches, the rope rides and similar techniques. He does have power, so we’ll see what happens.”

Thursday’s bidding is the next hurdle unless the camps bridge the financial divide before the deadline. If no agreement is reached, promoters will compete for the promotional rights through the WBO process.

Sports.title: Lamont Roach Questions William Zepeda’s Chin Before WBC Title Fight
Sports.content:
The confidence is understandable. Roach has shared the ring with Gervonta Davis and Isaac Cruz without being stopped. Yet his breakdown of Zepeda overlooks one of the Mexican’s greatest strengths.

“I think his punch resistance is moderate, but I don’t think he’ll be able to withstand what I got for 12 rounds,” Roach said to Sean Zittel. “We’re training for it, but I really don’t think he can take a lot of clean punches. I’m throwing fastballs with some heat on them.”

Roach later expanded on what he views as Zepeda’s biggest weakness.

“Defense, it’s a little shaky, but that’s what we’re going to exploit.”

The flaw in that analysis is assuming Zepeda fights like the opponents Roach has already faced.

Isaac Cruz, Gervonta Davis and Hector Luis Garcia all relied far more on head shots than sustained body attacks. Zepeda works differently. He chips away at the midsection from the opening bell, slowing opponents before the opportunities upstairs begin to multiply. His offense is built less around one damaging punch than a constant stream of combinations that gradually wears opponents down.

That approach changes the equation for Roach. Sharp counterpunching from the outside can expose Zepeda’s defensive lapses early, but maintaining that rhythm becomes much more difficult once the body attack begins taking effect.

Roach’s durability has never been a major concern. The more significant question is how his movement holds up after several rounds of absorbing body shots from one of boxing’s busiest pressure fighters.

Roach’s prediction will depend on consistently landing the cleaner punches before Zepeda’s body attack begins slowing him down. If Zepeda succeeds in dragging the fight into his preferred pace, punch resistance may become a secondary issue. The outcome could instead hinge on whether Roach can keep his movement, work rate, and defensive discipline intact after absorbing the sustained body attack that has become Zepeda’s trademark.

Sports.title: Simon Jordan Retracts Anthony Joshua Fight Suspicion After Review
Sports.content:
Reviewing the fight again, listening to Prenga’s corner instructions, and discussing the bout with trainers led Jordan to reconsider his initial reaction.

The dispute began after Jordan questioned why Prenga abandoned the aggressive approach that dropped Joshua twice in the opening round. Barry Hearn mocked that view, suggesting Jordan was implying the bout had been fixed and joking that his longtime rival always finds a way to say something foolish.

Jordan responded in kind.

“Obviously Barry is getting a bit decrepit so I allow him to have a senior moment and make his observations that way. But I also think that they are right,” said Jordan to talkSPORT Boxing. “When I first watched the bout. I saw Prenga come out and do the polar opposite of what he had done in the first round. My initial thought was, ‘I don’t like how this appears.’ But the more I rewatch it, and the more I listen to the corner work. It kind of takes me down the path that maybe I jumped to conclusions about something being amiss.”

Jordan ultimately settled on a boxing explanation rather than a conspiracy theory. Spencer Oliver argued that Prenga’s team made a critical tactical error by instructing their fighter to take their time instead of pressing a still-recovering Joshua. Richard Riakporhe agreed, saying Prenga followed poor instructions in the biggest opportunity of his career.

Jordan maintained that Joshua remains vulnerable while praising his finishing ability. He also reiterated that Joshua should avoid the division’s younger elite, identifying Moses Itauma and Daniel Dubois as dangerous opponents while viewing Tyson Fury as the logical next fight.

The second round completely changed the fight. When a heavyweight has an opponent hurt, especially one with Joshua’s history of struggling after being shaken, the standard approach is to press the attack immediately.

Prenga’s cautious start gave Joshua the one thing a recovering heavyweight desperately needs: time. Those extra seconds allowed him to regain his composure and steady his legs. Had Prenga attacked with the same urgency he displayed in the opening round, Joshua would have faced a far more dangerous situation. Instead, his corner’s strategy handed Joshua an opportunity, and he took full advantage with a decisive finish.

Sports.title: Duane Bobick Stops Chuck Wepner After Brutal Six-Round Battle
Sports.content:
Bobick entered the contest as one of boxing’s fastest rising heavyweights. The Minnesota native brought a 36-0 record and a No. 3 ranking into the bout after victories over Scott LeDoux and Bunny Johnson. Those performances moved him within reach of a world title opportunity. Across the ring stood Wepner, ranked No. 9 after his memorable challenge of Muhammad Ali the previous year. “The Bayonne Bleeder” remained one of boxing’s best-known heavyweights because of his toughness, willingness to absorb punishment, and habit of turning fights into rough affairs.

Wepner quickly dragged the bout into the kind of physical contest he preferred.

Bobick boxed behind a steady jab before unloading combinations whenever Wepner moved inside. Wepner answered with clinching, rabbit punches, and constant wrestling inside. His face soon showed the effects. Cuts opened as Bobick’s punches repeatedly found the target, leaving blood streaming down Wepner’s face.

The breakthrough arrived in the fifth round when Bobick landed a crushing body shot that dropped Wepner to the canvas. The veteran beat the count, though the punishment had clearly accumulated.

Only 1:12 into the sixth round, referee Harold Valen halted the bout after Wepner’s cuts became too severe to continue. Bobick earned a technical knockout that moved him to 37-0.

Bobick remained on course for a championship opportunity and added another victory later that month. The momentum ended in May 1977 when Ken Norton stopped him in one round at Madison Square Garden.

The loss came late in Wepner’s memorable career. He fought only a handful more times before retiring in 1978, leaving behind a legacy defined far more by his courageous effort against Ali than by the punishment he absorbed against Bobick.

Sports.title: Shane Mosley Reveals Adrien Broner’s Biggest Comeback Obstacle
Sports.content:
“I think that if he doesn’t lose focus on his goal and his dreams, then he’ll be all right,” Mosley said to Fighthype. “Sometimes he really, really want it and sometimes like he don’t give up, but he’s still working, but he loses focus on what he’s trying to do.”

Mosley left no doubt that he still believes Broner has the talent to compete. His concern is whether the former champion will stay committed long enough to prepare for another meaningful fight.

“He has the skills. He has the talent to be able to do some stuff,” Mosley said. “But I think that his worth, he’s got to show that. He’s not showing that he wants to fight. He can talk like that all day long. But he has to really be consistent, really be dedicated like he says he is and he can do it.”

Mosley’s comments come after a recent video showed Broner carrying noticeable extra weight around his midsection, raising fresh questions about whether he has begun preparing seriously for another fight.

Broner has not fought since 2024. Three years away from the ring leaves plenty of room for skepticism. Until he begins serious training and signs for a meaningful opponent, Mosley’s comments suggest the biggest question is not Broner’s talent but his commitment.

Adrien’s career has never matched the expectations that surrounded him. Many fans once viewed him as Floyd Mayweather Jr.’s successor, yet he has fought only four times in the seven years since 2019.

Sports.title: Andy Cruz’s Next Promoter Must Resist One Costly Mistake
Sports.content:
Following his third-round knockout of Abraham Montoya on July 18 in Carson, reports surfaced that Cruz’s contract with Matchroom Boxing has expired, leaving several promotional offers on the table. If accurate, every interested company faces the same question.

Does Cruz belong at lightweight?

The easy answer is no because Raymond Muratalla defeated him in an IBF title fight. That overlooks the circumstances.

Muratalla is one of the division’s biggest fighters. He’s not the standard for every lightweight. Cruz also fought a style that played into Muratalla’s strengths, relying on movement and single shots instead of sitting down on his punches and forcing the champion to respect his power.

The Montoya fight suggested Cruz (7-1, 4 KOs) had already begun making adjustments.

Against Montoya, he planted his feet more often, committed to combinations and sat down on his punches. The third-round stoppage showed a more assertive version of the Cuban Olympian than the one who challenged Muratalla.

The performance did not prove Cruz suddenly became a devastating puncher. It did suggest his team recognized the tactical mistake against Muratalla and corrected it.

Any promoter that signs Cruz should resist sending him to 130 simply because he lost one championship fight. He deserves another opportunity against a quality lightweight using the more aggressive style displayed against Montoya.

At 30, Cruz doesn’t have time for a lengthy rebuilding process after an accomplished amateur career. His next promoter should focus on securing meaningful fights instead of assuming one defeat settled the question of his best weight class.

If Cruz is truly a free agent, the promoter that benefits most may be the one that trusts his ability at lightweight instead of rushing him into another division after a single defeat.

Sports.title: Oleksandr Usyk Defends Deontay Wilder Before Potential Heavyweight Fight
Sports.content:
Usyk praised Wilder while discussing the former WBC champion, making it clear he still considers the American a legitimate threat.

“This is a man who in the last 10 years has been a top fighter. He’s a dangerous guy,” said Usyk to All Out Boxing about Deontay.

The timing of those comments is difficult to overlook. Wilder has emerged as a leading candidate to face Usyk, though the reaction remains mixed. While Wilder remains one of the sport’s biggest punchers, recent results have left many questioning whether he still belongs alongside the elite.

Usyk is making the opposite case. Instead of focusing on Wilder’s defeats, he highlighted the body of work that established him among the longest-reigning heavyweight champions. That argument also helps justify the matchup if negotiations move forward.

The undisputed champion may need that rationale because choosing Wilder is unlikely to satisfy fans who want to see him share the ring with younger contenders. A fight against Moses Itauma would generate far more excitement because of the unbeaten Briton’s rapid rise, while Frank Sanchez has strengthened his own claim with victories over established heavyweights. Those names present fresher challenges than a 40-year-old Wilder whose best years appear to be behind him.

Usyk has never shown much interest in those alternatives. Instead, his public comments suggest Wilder is among the opponents he believes still carries enough credibility to justify a championship fight. That helps explain why he chose to emphasize Wilder’s accomplishments instead of the setbacks that have created doubts about where the former WBC champion belongs in today’s heavyweight picture.

None of that erases Wilder’s accomplishments. He ruled as WBC champion for five years, defending the belt 10 times before losing it to Tyson Fury. He also remains capable of ending any fight with one right hand.

The bigger issue is timing. Usyk’s comments suggest he knows what fans will say if Wilder becomes his opponent. By defending Wilder’s credentials before contracts are signed, Usyk appears to be making the case that his next fight deserves more respect than many fans are prepared to give it.

Ghana News.title: Daily Insight for CEOs: Leading with Focus and Discipline
Ghana News.content:
Insight.

Leadership effectiveness is often determined not by how many priorities are pursued, but by how well the most important priorities are executed.

As year-end approaches, CEOs should help their organisations distinguish between activities that are urgent and those that are truly strategic. Maintaining focus requires disciplined decision-making, effective resource allocation, and the courage to say no to distractions.

Focused organisations consistently outperform those pursuing too many competing priorities.

Key Strategies:

1. Clarify the organisation’s top strategic priorities.

2. Eliminate low-value activities.

3. Align resources with business objectives.

4. Strengthen leadership accountability.

5. Review priorities regularly.

CEO Leadership Actions.

✅ Reconfirm organisational priorities with the executive team.

✅ Eliminate initiatives that no longer create strategic value.

✅ Encourage disciplined decision-making.

Actionable Tip.

* Ask your leadership team to identify one activity that should stop to create more capacity for strategic execution.

Why This Matters?

Focused leadership improves productivity, execution quality, and organisational performance.

About the Author.

Ernest De-Graft Egyir, CEO advisor, Thought Leader and Founding CEO of Chief Executives Network Ghana, convenes the Ghana CEO Summit and served on Ghana’s Economic Dialogue Planning Committee.

Ghana News.title: HACSA Foundation’s Tech4Girls Programme graduates 4th cohort, advancing Ghana’s digital skills agenda
Ghana News.content:
The fourth cohort of the HACSA Foundation’s Tech4Girls Programme will graduate today, Thursday, at the HACSA campus in Kanda, Accra, as the initiative continues its drive to equip young women with coding and job readiness skills.

The graduation ceremony, scheduled for 3:00 pm, marks another milestone for the programme, which was developed to empower girls and women with critical digital skills needed for employment and future careers.

The Tech4Girls initiative aligns with President John Dramani Mahama’s One Million Coders initiative, launched in 2025, and supports HACSA’s mission to develop leadership and skills among young people.

Since its inception in late 2023, the programme has focused on providing participants with practical coding knowledge, soft skills training and career development opportunities.

The first cohort introduced participants to foundational computer coding concepts and equipped them with essential soft skills.

The second cohort expanded the programme’s reach by introducing different learning levels. Participants were divided into a foundation class focused on frontend development and an intermediate class specialising in backend development.

That structure continued into the third cohort, which recorded increased participation while maintaining the programme’s focus on coding, soft skills training and masterclasses designed to promote collaboration and peer learning.

A key addition to the initiative has been the establishment of an Innovation Lab, which provides work experience opportunities for selected alumni who do not immediately transition into further education or internships with external organisations.

According to HACSA Foundation, the programme has continued to grow by creating pathways for young women to develop digital competencies and improve their employability.

The foundation says the initiative remains committed to preparing participants for meaningful jobs and careers while contributing to Ghana’s broader digital transformation agenda.

The graduation of the fourth cohort adds to the growing number of young women trained through the programme since its launch and reinforces efforts to increase female participation in technology and innovation.

Ghana News.title: Court remands two suspects in Immigration Officer murder case as prosecution awaits DNA report
Ghana News.content:
The Adabraka District Court has remanded Bright Aweh and Thomas Zigah, the two suspects standing trial in connection with the murder of an Immigration Officer, into prison custody for an additional two weeks.

The decision follows the delay in delivering a final determination in the case, which had earlier been adjourned to July 29, 2026, for judgment.

However, proceedings have been further stalled as the prosecution awaits the outcome of a DNA examination report and advice from the Attorney-General’s Office to guide the next steps in the matter.

The two suspects are facing charges in relation to the killing of an Immigration Officer, Stephen King Amoah whose death sparked public concern and intensified calls for justice.

Stephen King Amoah was reported missing after he failed to return home from duty, triggering a search and investigation by security agencies.

His disappearance later turned into a murder investigation after his partially charred body was discovered, leading to widespread concern and calls for justice.

Following investigations, Bright Aweh and Thomas Zigah were arrested and put before court in connection with the case. The prosecution has since relied on evidence gathered during investigations, including forensic materials, as it builds its case.

The two accused persons will remain in custody until they reappear before the court after the two-week remand period.

Ghana News.title: Tamale court jails ex-police officer, accomplice 25 years for armed robbery
Ghana News.content:
A former police officer and his accomplice have been sentenced to 25 years’ imprisonment with hard labour each for conspiracy to commit robbery by the Tamale High Court in a case linked to a high-profile armed robbery in the city.

The court convicted G/Cpl Suleman Ayuba Gbana, formerly of the Tamale District Police Station, and Adam Siba on July 20, 2026, after concluding the trial.

The case dates back to April 15, 2020, when armed assailants attacked two foreign exchange dealers, Issahaku Sumaila and Baba Fuseini, at the entrance of the then Mum Hotel on the Tamale-Bolgatanga Highway. The robbers shot both men and fled with GH¢530,000 in cash and other foreign currencies.

Investigations by the Northern Regional Police Command linked Gbana to the robbery syndicate after an arrested suspect named him as a member of the group.

A search of his residence led to the recovery of a Ghana Police Service pistol, 10 rounds of ammunition, three pairs of handcuffs, and a brown handbag.

Police say the pistol had been issued to Gbana during an earlier posting as a police bodyguard, and he unlawfully held onto it after his reassignment.

Officers arrested Gbana on April 23, 2020, and the Police Service interdicted him pending the outcome of the trial.

The court acquitted and discharged a third suspect, Mohammed Iddrisu, on all charges.

It also ordered that the pistol and ammunition tendered as exhibits be returned to the Ghana Police.

Ghana News.title: ‘It’s feasible’: NDC says it is ready to implement Supreme Court ruling on internal party elections
Ghana News.content:
Dr. Sofo Tanko Rashid Computer, Deputy National Director of Elections and IT for NDC

The National Democratic Congress (NDC) has expressed confidence that it can comply with the Supreme Court's directive requiring political parties to replace the delegate system with a more inclusive process that allows all eligible members to participate in the selection of parliamentary and presidential candidates.

The party believes the transition is achievable, arguing that the success of such a system depends largely on maintaining a credible and comprehensive membership database.

It maintains that with accurate records, political parties can efficiently organise nationwide internal elections involving all eligible members.

The Supreme Court recently declared the delegate system unconstitutional and ordered political parties to adopt a new electoral arrangement that gives every member in good standing the opportunity to vote in presidential and parliamentary primaries within one year of the ruling.

Speaking on Citi FM on Wednesday, July 29, the NDC's Deputy Director of IT and Elections, Rashid Tanko Computer, said the party already possesses the data management systems and organisational structures needed to implement the new arrangement.

He pointed to the party's recent branch elections, where members across more than 40,000 branches voted directly to elect their representatives, as evidence of its preparedness.

"It's feasible. Very feasible. I mean, why not? It's just about data. If you have the data, why can't you do it?" he said, adding that the NDC could implement the directive even if it were required to do so this year.

Mr Tanko said the successful conduct of the branch elections demonstrated the party's capacity to organise large-scale internal polls involving thousands of members.

He insisted the NDC is well-positioned to comply with the Supreme Court's decision within the stipulated timeframe and remains committed to strengthening internal party democracy.

Ghana News.title: CDD-Ghana’s Kojo Asante hails Supreme Court ruling on delegate system
Ghana News.content:
The Director of Policy Engagement and Partnerships at CDD-Ghana, Dr Kojo Asante, has welcomed the Supreme Court's decision declaring the delegate system unconstitutional, describing it as a bold judgment that could reshape internal party democracy in Ghana.

He said the ruling comes at a crucial moment when the country is reviewing its constitutional framework, arguing that it could accelerate long-standing reforms aimed at making political parties more democratic and reducing the influence of money in internal elections.

Dr Asante noted that concerns over the delegate system and the monetisation of party politics have featured prominently in discussions by the Constitutional Review Committee.

He expressed optimism that the judgment would serve as a catalyst for implementing reforms even before the broader constitutional review process is concluded.

Speaking in an interview on Channel One TV on Wednesday, July 29, Dr Asante said he was impressed by the Supreme Court's 5–2 majority decision and the reasoning of Chief Justice Paul Baffoe-Bonnie. "I think this is a landmark decision," he said.

"The timing is impeccable because, as you know, we are in the constitutional review process where this matter, in terms of the internal democracy of parties and the monetisation of party politics, has been a huge issue that the Constitutional Review Committee has proposed some reforms around."

He added: "I walked away from the court today feeling elated by the bravery of the courts. They think the time is now for us to reform and basically trigger the process."

The Supreme Court ruled that the delegate system used by political parties to elect their presidential and parliamentary candidates is unconstitutional and ordered all political parties to adopt a system that allows every member in good standing to vote in internal primaries.

The Court further directed the parties to implement the necessary changes within one year of the judgment.

Ghana News.title: UK High Commissioner alleges scholarship funds were mismanaged under previous government
Ghana News.content:
Ghana’s High Commissioner to the United Kingdom, Sabah Zita Benson

Ghana's High Commissioner to the United Kingdom, Sabah Zita Benson, has alleged widespread mismanagement in the administration of government scholarship funds under the previous administration.

She is claiming that excessive spending on dependants of scholarship beneficiaries contributed to the accumulation of millions of pounds in unpaid tuition and stipends owed to Ghanaian students in the UK.

In a series of Facebook posts, Ms Benson cited what she described as several instances of "reckless" expenditure, including the payment of allowances, airfares and other benefits for spouses and children accompanying scholarship beneficiaries abroad.

According to her, in one case, the spouse and three children of a beneficiary each received £8,160 in addition to the scholarship awarded to the student, while the family's airfare alone reportedly cost GH¢90,000.

"The spouse and children were paid £8,160 each to accompany the wife and mother to go study. That is different from the scholarship amount to the beneficiary. Why?... We have hundreds of such cases," she wrote.

The High Commissioner further claimed that money spent on dependants could have been used to settle outstanding tuition fees and living allowances for scholarship beneficiaries.

She alleged that more than £37 million in tuition fees and stipends accumulated between 2020 and 2025, while also questioning the award of a government scholarship to a 16-year-old to attend a private secondary school in the UK at a reported cost exceeding £56,000.

She cited another case in which the government allegedly spent GH¢90,420 on visa fees, tuberculosis screening and airfare for two students and the spouse of one beneficiary.

Responding to a planned protest by some Ghanaian scholarship students in the UK over delayed payments, Ms Benson argued that the current administration inherited substantial financial obligations from the previous government.

"Those who want to come and protest tomorrow because Government hasn't paid your fees, you now know where your money went. You should have protested from 2020–2025 when they were not paying," she stated.

She added that the government paid £3 million towards the arrears last year, has settled first-quarter payments this year and is processing second-quarter payments, insisting that the current administration is committed to clearing the outstanding debts while ensuring accountability.

Ghana News.title: Supreme Court ruling will keep OSP in check – Martin Kpebu
Ghana News.content:
Private legal practitioner Martin Kpebu has described the Supreme Court's ruling affirming the Attorney-General's authority to discontinue prosecutions initiated by the Office of the Special Prosecutor (OSP) as a significant constitutional safeguard that will keep the anti-corruption agency in check.

Reacting to the judgment in an interview on Citi FM on Wednesday, July 29, Mr Kpebu said the decision provides much-needed clarity on the constitutional relationship between the Attorney-General and the OSP.

"It's a welcome relief, very timely. It will help to at least keep Kissi Agyebeng in check for a bit," he said.

According to Mr Kpebu, the ruling confirms that although the OSP has prosecutorial powers under the Office of the Special Prosecutor Act, those powers are exercised on behalf of the Attorney-General.

He explained that the Constitution vests the power to prosecute criminal cases in the Attorney-General, who also retains the authority to discontinue any prosecution at any stage.

"The Supreme Court has been very clear that the Office of the Special Prosecutor is under the Attorney-General's office. The decision is that it's only the Attorney-General who has power to prosecute. Any other person prosecuting a criminal case is doing it on behalf of the Attorney-General," he stated.

Mr Kpebu argued that the judgment creates an important constitutional check against any potential abuse of prosecutorial authority by the OSP.

He said individuals who believe they have been unfairly targeted by the anti-graft agency can now seek redress from the Attorney-General, who has the power to review the case and discontinue proceedings where appropriate.

"The Attorney-General will call for the file and look at it and see if your case has merit. The Attorney-General will stop what the OSP is doing. So that's very key. It's a key check," he added.

The Supreme Court's ruling followed a constitutional challenge filed by private legal practitioner Noah Adamtey, who argued that Parliament could not confer independent prosecutorial powers on the OSP because Article 88 of the 1992 Constitution vests that authority in the Attorney-General.

While the apex court upheld the constitutionality of the Office of the Special Prosecutor Act, 2017 (Act 959), it ruled that the Attorney-General's constitutional power to discontinue prosecutions remains intact, including in cases initiated by the Special Prosecutor.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”
