World.title: The final innings
World.content:
People observe a minute’s silence for West Indian cricket legend Sir Garfield Sobers ahead of the third one-day international cricket match between England and India at Lord’s Cricket Ground in London on July 19, 2026. (Photo: AFP)

BRIDGETOWN, Barbados (CMC) — Garfield St Auburn Sobers played his final innings at the Kensington Oval here on Wednesday under bright sunshine for nearly three hours, still able to mesmerise local, regional and international spectators, most of whom, including Britain’s King Phillip, acknowledging that there have been few, “whose name alone brings a smile to people’s faces across Barbados, the Caribbean and the entire Commonwealth”.

Barbados Prime Minister Mia Mottley, in her “grateful from the nation” tribute at the State Service of Thanksgiving, said the visit to the Kensington Oval, “this most iconic of cricket grounds where Sir Garry’s casket was draped with the national flag of Barbados”, was to pay tribute, “but also to send a message to the future”.

She said the 89-year-old Sir Garry did not come to be the best or the first or the last, but “came to do his best and to be his best, not for the world, but for goals that he set himself, conscious that if he did that, along with whatever else everyone else did, that glory could come, victory could be assured”.

Sobers was buried one day after he would have celebrated his 90th birthday, and Mottley said that the gods would have conspired to ensure that the West Indies cricket team had defeated the visiting Pakistan test team by 90 runs on Tuesday in Trinidad and Tobago, thereby allowing the seven members of the regional team to attend the ceremony.

“I say today as we say farewell to you, Sir Garry, this is your final walk from Kensington Oval. This will be our country’s last opportunity to give you that which you became so accustomed to, a standing ovation,” Mottley said in blazing sunlight over the picturesque ground on the outskirts of the capital, Bridgetown.

“I ask each and every one of us in this Oval today …to let us stand and give Sir Garry, our Sir Garry, our hero, our beloved man. A man who guided me in my own personal journey with the confidence that I think that each and every one of us as children need to take on this world.

“We thank you for teaching us that greatness could wear humility, that excellence could still belong to ordinary people, that the dreams of a little boy from the Bayland could become the inheritance of an entire nation,” Mottley said of the man, who until July 17, was one of two Barbados living national heroes, the other being the internationally acclaimed singer, Robyn Rihanna Fenty, who was also present at the funeral.

Former West Indies captain, Brian Lara, who in April 1994 broke Sir Garry’s long-standing world record of 365 runs which he made against Pakistan in 1958, in an emotional address, described the gifted batsman as “my mentor, my dad, and my friend”.

Lara added: “First time I met you, you were Sir Sobers. Over the last few days I struggled with what I would say today, but now I am here, I realise something, this is not a sad moment, this is a moment for us to celebrate and I hope you feel the same.”

Lara said he hopes that 10 years from now when there will be a celebration of Sobers’s 100th birthday “we might also be celebrating the rebirth of West Indies cricket”.

Another former West Indies captain Sir Clive Lloyd, who at one time played alongside Sobers, said, “Today I believe we can honour Sir Garfied in ways that extend beyond statues and ceremonies, worthy those are.

“His extraordinary achievement as a fast bowler, as a left-arm spinner, in three distinct styles, as perhaps the greatest close catcher of the game ever seen, and as an incomparable batsman, should become the foundation of institutions dedicated to nurturing future generations.

“Today, we should study not only what Sir Garfield accomplished, but how he accomplished it. What inner drive compelled him to reach such heights? What vision inspired him each time he walked to the crease or began his run to the wicket? What dreams guided him as captain of the West Indies team?”

The Guyanese-born Lloyd said that these are questions worth asking because the answers can inspire generations yet unborn.

Sobers represented West Indies between 1954 and 1974 and played 93 Test matches, scoring 8,032 runs at a spectacular average of 57.78. Sobers also claimed 235 wickets at an average of 34.03 and an economy rate of 2.22. By an act of Parliament in 1998, Sobers was named as one of the 11 National Heroes of Barbados.

Two of Sobers’s children, Mathew and Daniel, recalled the influence their father had on their lives.

“Whether it was cricket, table tennis, golf, or just shooting hoops with the kids, he was blessed with rare talents few people had. But as I grew older, I realised his greatest gifts had very little to do with sport, but everything to do with the way he lived,” Mathew Sobers said.

“The world knew him as the Right, Excellent Sir Garfield St Aurbun Sobers. Many believed he was the greatest cricketer who ever lived,” he said noting, “but remarkable as those achievements were, they tell only part of the story.

“Dad was born into a Barbados still emerging from the long shadow of plantocracy and colonial rule. At a time when opportunity was limited for so many, he became living proof that excellence could come from these shores.

For his part, Daniel Sobers, who together with Matthew flew into Barbados from the United States, and with his younger sister Genevieve cutting short a visit to Australia with her mum, described his father as “the greatest”.

He said while he welcomes the avalanche of thoughts, prayers, and kind words about his father, he would like to thank all those who had been taking care of his father “during the more than 18 months of his steady decline”.

“Growing up, I never really understood the gravity of the mastery of my dad’s achievements. I was born into his life and just took them for granted. For me, it was a thing of normalcy.

“Doesn’t every dad at the age of 21 score 365 not out and hit six sixes in an over whenever he feels like it? What I also remember is that he was always busy and travelled a lot, and that I missed him when he was gone,” Daniel Sobers added.

Following the funeral, Sir Garfield Sobers, considered to have been the greatest all-rounder in cricket’s history, was given a 19-gun salute as his body was buried at the Coral Ridge Memorial Gardens on The Ridge, Christ Church Parish.

World.title: Dream Wknd, partners ready to welcome thousands to MoBay
World.content:
Mobay Mayor Richard Vernon addresses the recent launch of Dream Wknd 2026 held at Pier 1.

MONTEGO BAY, St James — Dream Entertainment Limited, St James Municipal Corporation, and Jamaica Constabulary Force say all systems are in place for Dream Wknd’s inaugural staging in Montego Bay.

With months of planning and cross-agency collaboration will culminate in what is expected to be one of Jamaica’s largest entertainment events of the summer.

More than 30,000 patrons are expected to descend on the tourism capital over the coming days for the festival’s first staging outside its long-time home of Negril, bringing a significant boost to the local economy while showcasing Montego Bay’s growing capacity to host major international events.

Chairman of Dream Entertainment Kamal Bankay said organisers have spent months working alongside government agencies, venue operators, and service providers to ensure every aspect of the festival is ready ahead of Thursday’s opening.

“We have been working very closely with the venues and the planning authorities in St James,” Bankay said. “That includes the municipal corporation, the Jamaica Constabulary Force, the Ministry of Health, the Jamaica Fire Brigade, and the other agencies responsible for issuing the relevant approvals.”

He said the work has extended beyond regulatory requirements to include detailed coordination with venue operators and event partners responsible for delivering the festival experience.

“Based on where we are now, all of those preparations have been completed and the necessary systems are in place, so we’re ready to welcome patrons when the events begin on Thursday,” he said.

Bankay added that while Dream Wknd will deliver its signature entertainment experience, the festival also provides visitors with an opportunity to experience Montego Bay beyond the event venues.

“When you come to Montego Bay, just know that it’s a great city in its own right, and Dream Wknd is really there to elevate what’s already on offer,” he said. “Visitors can enjoy the city’s hotels, restaurants, beaches, and attractions throughout the weekend.”

Mayor Richard Vernon described Dream Wknd’s arrival in Montego Bay as a significant milestone for the city, saying it reinforces its standing as one of the Caribbean’s leading tourism and entertainment destinations.

“Dream Wknd’s expansion to Montego Bay is a landmark moment for Jamaica’s tourism capital,” Vernon said. “It affirms our city’s reputation as a premier entertainment destination in the Caribbean and demonstrates confidence in our ability to continue hosting world-class events, even during our most challenging times.”

Vernon said his team has worked closely with partners to ensure the city is prepared to welcome the influx of visitors. Traffic management plans have been finalised, public health protocols activated, and emergency contingencies established to support the festival weekend.

“Our hospitality sector has mobilised to meet demand, while local businesses are prepared… This readiness ensures that Dream Wknd will be a successful event and drive sustained economic activity across Montego Bay,” said Vernon.

Senior Superintendent Eron Samuels, commander of the St James Police Division, said the police have developed a comprehensive security plan in partnership with other stakeholders.

“Our objective is to create a safe environment where patrons can enjoy the festivities while residents and visitors continue to feel secure,” Samuels said.

He encouraged patrons to celebrate responsibly by planning their transportation in advance, avoiding drinking and driving, securing their personal belongings, remaining aware of their surroundings and following the instructions of police officers, event security personnel and emergency responders.

“Our message is simple: Enjoy the event, make lasting memories, but make safety your priority,” he said.

In addition to extensive logistical preparations, organisers say patrons can also expect an elevated festival experience through the involvement of Dream WKND’s major brand partners, each bringing unique activations designed to complement the music and entertainment.

Red Stripe and its portfolio of brands will deliver vibrant social spaces across four signature events: Guinness at Dream Live, Casamigos at Daydreams, Red Stripe at YUSH, and Smirnoff at Igloo. Meanwhile, the Campari Group will bring premium activations, signature cocktail experiences, and interactive brand engagements to Wet ‘N Wild with Magnum, Foul Play with J Wray & Nephew, and Xodus Remedy presented by Campari.

Festivalgoers can also look forward to high-energy experiences from Boom Energy Drink, whose touchpoints are designed to keep the excitement going throughout the weekend. Mother’s will round out the culinary experience with specially curated dishes prepared throughout the weekend, providing hearty, flavourful meal options to keep patrons fuelled while they enjoy the overall festival atmosphere.

Dream Entertainment says the collective investment by its corporate partners reflects a shared commitment to delivering a world-class entertainment experience, with immersive brand experiences carefully integrated into the festival to ensure patrons enjoy much more than just the performances onstage.

World.title: Safety or red tape?
World.content:
DALRYMPLE-PHILIBERT... said any organisation introducing a programme for children has a duty to satisfy itself that those involved are suitable.

A spirited debate erupted during a sitting of Parliament’s joint select committee reviewing the Child Diversion Act on Wednesday, after Government Senator Sherene Golding-Campbell questioned why licensed psychologists, who are already vetted by their professional regulatory body, must undergo additional background checks before being allowed to work with children in the Child Diversion Programme.

However, committee members, including chairman Delroy Chuck, argued that the additional scrutiny is essential because vulnerable children are involved, insisting that no safeguard should be overlooked when selecting professionals to work in the programme.

The disagreement emerged as the committee examined provisions of the Act dealing with how counsellors and psychologists are approved to provide services under the Child Diversion Programme, which seeks to rehabilitate children who come into conflict with the law rather than exposing them to the formal court system.

Under the existing law, the minister is empowered to approve counsellors and psychologists for use in the programme. The legislation also requires standards and procedures to be set for the operation of diversion services.

Golding-Campbell questioned whether that approval process was necessary for psychologists who are already licensed to practise under Jamaican law.

“If they’re registered under the Act, what is the purpose of a background check on a psychologist? I’m not understanding that,” she asked.

Director of the Child Diversion Branch in the Ministry of Justice and Constitutional Affairs Venisa Clarke explained that the programme uses a range of mental health professionals, including psychologists, counsellors, clinical social workers, and guidance counsellors.

She said the background checks are carried out not because the professionals are unqualified, but because they will be working closely with vulnerable children.

“Every psychologist that touches base with the Child Diversion Office or contacts us, we have a list of things that are required. We have a checklist that they have to meet certain criteria. Once that is done, we indicate to them that we are now going to move to get the approval to engage. The first aspect of that approval is that a background check has to be done as well, and we have to see that they are certified,” Clarke explained.

She said the background check includes more than a criminal record search.

“For the mental health service providers, we engage a private member of society that does that for us. It includes a visit to their community, getting information from NIB [National Intelligence Bureau], as well as a sex offender registry, a whole list of things, and the report includes if they find any adverse traces or anything of that sort,” she added.

Golding-Campbell, however, argued that the process appeared to duplicate checks already carried out by the bodies responsible for licensing professionals. She also questioned whether the programme was making the best use of limited public resources.

“I appreciate that it’s children, but if these professionals are registered, they’re registered. If they have a valid registration under the Act, they’re registered. I’m not understanding why we would commit resources to a private investigator to find out whether or not they have convictions,” she queried further.

The senator also questioned why the minister should have the power to approve individual psychologists and counsellors if they have already met the legal requirements to practice in Jamaica.

Her concerns were met with resistance from several committee members.

Chuck acknowledged that professionally registered psychologists may require less scrutiny than other groups, but said the ministry still has a responsibility to ensure every person working with children can be trusted.

“You don’t know which of these personnel could abuse the child. And therefore, the background check is absolutely important… The last thing we would want is we put the child to interact with a mentor, and the mentor turns out to be a paedophile,” he said.

Member of Parliament for Portland Eastern Isat Buchanan also defended the practice, arguing that professional registration alone cannot guarantee that a person poses no risk to children.

“Background checks for the purpose of child diversion are about adverse findings. There are persons who have come in conflict with the law that have not been brought before the court because other things would have happened…So if we are protecting the child, Minister, respectfully, you sit in the chair right now. It is the approval by you, because if anything should happen I will be the first to say, ‘How could the minister make this happen? Heads should roll!’, and I will be the first to say ‘Resign, resign, resign’,” he expressed.

State minister in the Ministry of Justice Marisa Dalrymple-Philibert similarly backed the existing approach, saying any organisation introducing a programme for children has a duty to satisfy itself that those involved are suitable.

However, Golding-Campbell maintained that her concern was not with protecting children but with making sure the system is logical and consistent. She argued that if the programme believes extra vetting is necessary, then it should not happen only once at the beginning.

“If it is that you want to be satisfied that they are safe people for children separate and apart from their registration under law governed by another body, then it must be something that you’re telling me you’re satisfying yourself of periodically, because to satisfy yourself when they are approved does not hold for the entire time that they participate in the programme. Being good in 2022 doesn’t mean that I haven’t committed some offence that would disturb you in 2025,” she said.

That argument appeared to win some support from Chuck, who agreed that repeat checks should be considered.

Clarke also welcomed the suggestion, confirming that, while background checks are currently mandatory before a professional joins the programme, the ministry would consider introducing periodic reviews.

World.title: LEAPING TO HISTORY
World.content:
Tajay Gayle (Photo: AFP)

TAJAY Gayle created history on Wednesday when he won Jamaica’s first-ever men’s long jump gold medal at the Commonwealth Games (CWG).

Shot putter Lloydricia Cameron claimed a bronze medal at Scotstoun Stadium in Glasgow, Scotland, as Jamaica’s medal tally went up to four — inclusive of three gold and a bronze — at the 23rd edition of the Games.

Romaine Beckford and Demario Prince had opened Jamaica’s medal account on Monday with gold medals in the men’s high jump and 110m hurdles, respectively.

Expectations are high for more medals on Thursday with finals in the women’s triple jump and discus throw competitions.

After placing fourth at the 2018 Commonwealth Games in Australia, Gayle jumped 8.15m (1.5m/s) to become the first Jamaican man to win a long jump competition. He is the first Jamaican man to win a medal at the Games since Wesley Clayton won back-to-back bronze in 1962 and 1966.

India’s Sreeshankar took consecutive silver medals after a best mark of 8.09m (1.3m/s), just ahead of Stephen Mackenzie of Scotland who was third with 8.08m (0.9m/s). Jamaican Jordan Turner was ninth with 7.65m (0.1m/s).

Cameron, who won her first national championships title this year, improved on her fourth-place finish from four years ago in Birmingham, England, taking the bronze with a best of 17.87m in the final round to eclipse Manpreet Kaur of India.

Canada’s two-time World Athletics Indoor champion Sarah Mitton defended her title with an effort of 19.88m. Nigeria’s 19-year-old Jessica Oji took the silver medal with 17.87m, getting the edge over Cameron with a better second throw.

National champion Ackelia Smith and NCAA winner Shantae Foreman are set to take on world leader and Olympic champion Thea Lafond of Dominica in the women’s triple jump on Thursday.

Jamaica’s Samantha Hall is the Commonwealth leader in the women’s discus throw and will start as pre-championships favourite going into the final.

There will also be qualifying in the 100m hurdles in which Kerrica Hill and Megan Simmonds are set to compete. In the men’s triple jump Jordan Scott, who is ranked number one, is also down to feature.

Kelly Ann Beckford qualified for the final of the women’s 800m after placing third in her semi-finals in 1:59.96, beaten to the finish line by Lilian Odira (1:59.39) of Kenya and Shafiqua Maloney (1:59.81) of St Vincent and the Grenadines.

Adelle Tracey was fourth in her heat in 2:01.54 for 10th overall.

Other Jamaicans, including 200m and women’s 400m hurdles runners, progressed past the first round of their respective events on Wednesday.

National champion Sanique Walker and Shiann Salmon, the latter who was second four years ago in Birmingham, topped the qualifying in the women’s 400m hurdles.

Walker won her heat in 54.83 seconds and Salmon topped hers in 55.30 to booked places in Friday’s final.

National champion Assinie Wilson was second in his first round heat in the men’s 400m hurdles in 49.19.

Lavanya Williams and Alana Reid were also the fastest in the women’s 200m first round.

Williams ran 22.91 (0.8m/s) to win heat five and national champion Reid clocked 22.95 (1.7m/s) to claim heat six as they made safe passage through to Thursday’s semi-finals.

All three Jamaican men also advanced in the 200m.

Christopher Taylor was second in his heat in 20.36 (1.6m/s), the same time given to Ghana’s Joseph Paul Amoah, who was declared the winner.

Roshawn Clarke won his heat in 20.56 (1/0m/s) and Jevaughn Powell recorded a wind-aided 20.28 (2.6m/s) to top his heat.

World.title: Chef Colin Brown’s HOMECOMING CHAÎNE FEAST
World.content:
Yellowfin tuna crudo with lime-ginger marinade, Scotch bonnet oil, ripe mango salsa and breadfruit crisp (Photo: Aceion Cunningham)

Sun-kissed afternoon, the hum of conversation, and the clink of glasses set the scene at Uncorked Ochi at Drax Hall on Sunday, July 26 as Chaîne des Rôtisseurs Jamaïque, Select Brands, and Uncorked hosted a celebratory bistro brunch showcasing the return of Chef Colin Brown to Jamaican shores. Brown — back from an international run of kitchens — teamed with Uncorked’s culinary team to present a lively fusion of island flavours and classic French techniques that won praise from members and guests alike.

The cold and seafood station opened the meal with refined island flair: Yellowfin tuna crudo brightened with a lime-ginger marinade, Scotch bonnet oil, ripe mango salsa, and a crisp of breadfruit; and an escoveitch conch paired with calabash lobster, spiced pickled vegetables, allspice, and lime zest that married Caribbean acidities with steely seafood sweetness.

The opening of the smoked and slow-roast station followed. A pimento-smoked salmon with a rustic salsa; golden goat, glazed with Appleton rum and finished with a nutmeg-thyme jus offered deep, caramelised rum notes; and Blue Mountain coffee-crusted pork belly, lacquered in a tamarind-molasses glaze balanced bitter, sweet and savoury. Braised oxtail croquettes, stuffed with a butter-bean purée with chive oil, provided a textural and flavourful nod to Jamaica’s comfort-cook traditions, while a live action station with pimento-smoked roasted leg of lamb, scented with rosemary, orange zest and tarragon, rounded out the roast offerings.

Side dishes and local provisions were treated with equal care: roasted sweet potatoes and breadfruit crowned with coconut butter and toasted pimento, herbed yam croquettes, creamy coconut rice with gungo peas, callaloo-pak choi sautéed with ginger, garlic and island five-spice, and an inventive green banana risotto studded with aged local artisan cheese. These accompaniments anchored the menu in terroir while supporting the international techniques on display.

Dessert showcased Jamaica’s signature ingredients in elegant formats: Wray & Nephew rum and gingerbread pudding bathed in warm coconut custard, a sorrel-hibiscus panna cotta with candied ginger, and a guava tart in flaky coconut pastry. Sweet finishes were complemented by a chilled limoncello cooler pairing that cut through the richness.

Select Brands curated the beverage pours, pairing the menu with a sparkling and wine line-up that included Veuve Clicquot Brut NV, Kettmeir Pinot Grigio 2024, Terra Alpina Chardonnay 2022, Aqua di Venus Rosé, Tassajara Pinot Noir 2022 and Dominio Fournier 2020. The thoughtful beverage selection underscored the brunch’s balance of celebration and culinary craft.

The event was both a welcome-home for Chef Brown and a statement of culinary collaboration — a tasteful fusion that celebrated Jamaica’s pantry while leaning into French technique and presentation, a thrust Brown is quick to emphasise in the Jamaican culinary space.

“We have to cook our own food, add our cultural perspective and use the techniques from France, Italy and we’ll become masters by taking an indigenous cuisine and refining it. For today’s menu we used the Seville orange, rice vinegar, Mirin, sushi ginger, ripe mango, tomato and we boiled the breadfruit in the skin, sliced thinly, fried it to make a nice crisp and this came out really well for the yellow fin tuna. escoveitch conch and lobster, we made a lobster bisque for the base, boil it and season only with Scotch bonnet powder, sear it, keeping it fresh and nice. For the conch we cooked it for hours and sliced it thinly, tossed and fried keeping it crispy,” Brown explained.

“The salmon was done of more a jerk style but with more kick to it. Everyone is more use to curry goat, but we slow-cooked the goat with Appleton rum, nutmeg and thyme, making it a well-balanced dish. The crispy pork belly was cooked in Blue Mountain coffee jerk for two and half hours and glazed with June plum and lime and dusted with Blue Mountain coffee, giving you the sweet, sour, coffee flavour and the jerk. The oxtail was also slow cooked and the lamb leg we marinated for three days,” Brown added.

World.title: Jamaica snatch last minute draw against Panama in U20
World.content:
Jaquan Brown of Jamaica celebrates his equaliser in the young Reggae Boyz' Concacaf Under-20 Championship match against Panama on Wednesday, July 29, 2026. The game ended 2-2. (Photo: Concacaf/Instagram)

KINGSTON, Jamaica — Jamaica rallied from two goals down to earn a courageous draw against Panama in their Concacaf U20 Championships Group C at Estadio Universitario BUAP in Puebla, Mexico on Wednesday.

The result kept Jamaica’s hopes of advancing to the quarterfinals alive as they are on four points, one more than Canada who will play Honduras in the second game, while Panama are on one point from two games.

Jamaica are also third in the overall rankings that include teams from the other groups, only behind the USA and Mexico, both of who have won their first two games.

Desperate to earn a win after losing 3-0 to Canada on Sunday, Panama got off to a fast start and were ahead 2-0 after 22 minutes with goals from Moisés Richards in the 13th minute and Carlos Rodriguez in the 22nd minute.

It could have been worse had VAR not ruled out another goal for Panama in the 36th minute.

Jahmarie Nolan, who had scored the first goal in the 2-1 win over Honduras, pulled a goal back for Jamaica in the 62nd minute before Jaquan Brown headed home a freekick from second half substitute Jamione Lyle in time added.

It was the second time in a row that Jamaica scored on the final play of the game, in time added, after Brandon Bent had scored the winner against Honduras in time added.

The coaches had made one change to the starting team, Che Gardner of Stockport County replacing Sean Leighton.

Starting team:

Joshua Grant, Jaquan Brown, Jahmarie Nolan, Jermaine Young, Jabarie

Howell, Jahmani Bell, Che Gardner, Duwayne Burgher, Santana

Headley, Kimarly Scott, Brandon Bent

—Paul A Reid

World.title: Watch out Brussels and Kyiv, Poland’s conservatives are veering right
World.content:
Allies of pro-EU Prime Minister Donald Tusk read it as good news. When Kaczyński stepped to the microphone to kick out Morawiecki, two lawmakers from Tusk’s governing coalition filmed themselves watching the speech, eating popcorn.

You can see why they might be happy. Before the split, POLITICO’s Poll of Polls put Tusk’s Civic Coalition at 32 percent support and PiS at 26 percent. PiS has now slumped to 22 percent.

But that is hardly the whole story. The combined forces of right-wing parties are still in a strong position if they team up for the 2027 election. And Friday’s split means that PiS is more likely to veer right in its alliances, choosing ideological consolidation over an attempt to win back the center.

The wing of PiS led by Morawiecki had argued the party needed to broaden its appeal and adopt a less combative approach toward Brussels. Kaczyński instead appears determined to recapture voters who have defected further right.

It is far from certain, however, how successfully Poland’s far-right parties can agree on a common agenda with PiS.

Among the potential beneficiaries of Friday’s split are parties that oppose Ukraine joining the European Union — and, in the case of Grzegorz Braun’s Federation of the Polish Crown movement, advocate taking Poland out of the bloc altogether.

World.title: The first election of the Andy Burnham era is already here
World.content:
“Let’s go in and have a look. Let’s open it up,” she said at a food market in Altrincham, a town in the south-west of Greater Manchester. Astley said Labour has had “an absolute stronghold of a vice-like grip” across the region for too long. “This is really the first time this level of political choice has been available to the voters,” she said.

Geraldine Coggins is the Green Party pick. She has stood in seven elections, and been elected as a councilor in Trafford three times.

Having joined the party in 2010, she is now relishing the growth in campaign resources after recent electoral successes, and said at a community garden cafe in Manchester that activists had come from as far away as Aberdeen and Cornwall to help out on the doorsteps.

Coggins’ pitch is that Greater Manchester needs a mayor to stand up to government — rather than a “Labour apologist,” a term she used to describe Craig. She also wants more devolution — including for mayors to be given the power to impose rent caps — and has her own bus pledge: to make them free for anyone under 22.

How will the vote be decided?

The mayoralty will once again be decided using the supplementary vote system — and that’s caused a little disquiet from Labour’s opponents on the right.

Voters will be asked to pick a first and second preference. If no candidate gets 50 percent or more of first preference votes, all but the top two candidates will be eliminated. The second preferences of voters who initially backed those losing candidates are then redistributed.

World.title: Climate change is turning parts of Europe into an insurance nightmare
World.content:
The growing risk has prompted the European Central Bank and EU insurance regulator to call on Brussels to take a more active role by setting up an EU-level reinsurance scheme and a public natural disaster fund.

"What’s happening in Europe this summer isn’t unique," deputy governor of the Bank of France Agnès Bénassy-Quéré said. "These heatwaves and forest fires are part of a marked global increase in extreme weather events that imposes real costs on households, businesses, and governments," she said.

Wildfires are “the fastest-growing weather peril globally,” even if they have “so far contributed only a relatively small share of insured losses in Europe,” said Nikhil da Victoria Lobo, who leads reinsurance giant Swiss Re's Property & Casualty Reinsurance business for western and southern Europe, the Middle East and Africa.

Extreme weather events already cost a fortune in repairs for Europe’s cash-strapped governments. Data from the European Environment Agency shows weather-related extremes cost the EU economy over €200 billion in economic losses between 2021 and 2024.

Insurance firms, meanwhile, are hiking their prices and even pulling out of certain at-risk areas, leaving governments and individuals to bear the cost of uninsured losses.

“In Europe, 75 percent of the damages related to natural disasters are not insured,” said Ariel Le Bourdonnec, a campaigner working on insurance at the NGO Reclaim Finance, citing data from the European Insurance and Occupational Pensions Authority. For insurers, flooding and storms are the most costly natural disasters, followed by extreme heat and wildfires, according to Insurance Europe.

World.title: Europe turns to goats to prevent wildfires
World.content:
“In the same way that we understand the need to finance firefighters, we also need to recognize the work done by shepherds,” said Jordi Vendrell, who leads the Pau Costa Foundation, a nonprofit in Spain that studies wildfire management.

As blazes threaten Bordeaux, French farmers have been helping alongside the firefighters, filling their slurry tanks with water to help where they can. Yet a lack of farmers is part of the problem.

Abandoned farmland grows over with shrubs that dry out or get replaced by vulnerable, homogenous forests that burn easily. The European space program’s satellite observatory, Copernicus, confirmed that the largest fires currently ravaging Europe are indeed happening in areas where forests and shrubland form large, connected landscapes.

A wildfire burns in Colinas del Campo, Spain on Aug. 21, 2025. | Cesar Manso/AFP via Getty Images

Yet while there’s plenty of natural fodder for goats, the market doesn’t offer much incentive for shepherds. José María Castilla of the Spanish farm lobby ASAJA said getting young people into goat herding is “impossible” without making it profitable. The solution, he argued, is creating a dedicated fund, following the same logic as the EU’s coronavirus response in 2020.

“Some people are saying that the farmers that are living next to the borders of Russia need to receive more money, since they are the first line of defense,” he said. The first line of defense offered by shepherds tending to tinderbox land plots, he argued, “is exactly the same thing.”

Grazing for a good cause

Funders are embracing Catalonia’s Fire Flocks project as a potential success story, mixing fire prevention with commercial farming.

World.title: INEM helicopters over Portugal ready to take off in three minutes
World.content:
Before the day has even begun, teams are on standby at Portugal's emergency medical helicopter bases. A call can come in at any moment and, when it does, every second counts.

 

On the ground, there is often no time to spare. In the air, the response gains speed. On average, the reaction time between the alert and take-off is three minutes.

"Response time in medical emergencies is the critical factor for success. We are currently operating at an excellent level, within three minutes. In certain cases we can reduce it even further. Our average is three minutes from activation to response," explains Hugo Chambel, director of Gulf Med Aviation Services for the Iberian Peninsula, speaking to Euronews.

The operation is run by Gulf Med, a company of Malta-based Medilink, in partnership with medical teams from the National Institute of Medical Emergency (INEM). The network is spread across four permanent bases: Loulé, Évora, Viseu and Macedo de Cavaleiros, ensuring coverage of almost the entire country.

Gulf Med began operating in Portugal in July 2025, under a direct award contract signed with INEM worth around four million euros, which remained in force until October last year.

From October onwards, the company has been working under a 77.5 million euro contract, awarded following the international public tender for INEM's Emergency Medical Helicopter Service (SHEM), which provides for four aircraft to be available 24 hours a day.

The five-year contract runs until mid-2030 and has a total value of more than 77 million euros.

In April 2026, the company strengthened the system with the addition of a fifth helicopter, bringing the overall investment in the fleet in Portugal to around 50 million euros. This extra helicopter serves as a backup aircraft, ensuring the operational continuity of the four bases in service during maintenance periods or any temporary withdrawals for technical reasons.

The Airbus H145 D3 can land almost anywhere

From remote inland areas to roads and even coastal zones, the helicopter is often the only means capable of providing rapid assistance. The Airbus H145 D3 aircraft, equipped with skis instead of wheels, can land on virtually any type of terrain.

"We are certain of that, not only because these aircraft are designed for this kind of mission. Their weight and payload capacity are very well balanced, which makes them extremely flexible. That means they are able to land practically anywhere: on a road, an estate or in places where there is very limited space for landing. They are outstanding, well-balanced aircraft for our kind of territory and our operational needs," says the Gulf Med representative.

Inside, the spacious cabin and specialised medical equipment are designed for immediate intervention. On board are doctors and nurses trained to operate in critical situations.

"Each mission is made up of several stages. While we are still en route, and based on the initial information, we discuss possible scenarios and anticipate difficulties so we can save time when we approach the patient," says Leila Duarte, an INEM internal and emergency medicine doctor, speaking to Euronews.

"We then assess, stabilise and decide, in contact with the control centre, where to transport the patient. During the flight, we maintain constant monitoring and inform the destination hospital of any change in the patient's condition," she adds.

Equipped with skis instead of wheels, these helicopters can land almost anywhere Bruno Figueiredo/Euronews

In the cockpit, the priority is to ensure safe operations in all circumstances.

"We always check the weather conditions so we can react quickly when a primary call comes in. At night, it is more demanding because we have to take several factors into account, including the landing site. Even so, we are normally able to respond within five minutes," says Craig Dewar, a pilot with INEM's Emergency Medical Helicopter Service.

The missions fall into two categories: primary, when the team is sent directly to the scene of the incident, and secondary, which are more planned transfers between hospital units. SHEM also carries out organ transport and ECMO transport (Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation), for critically ill patients dependent on advanced mechanical cardiopulmonary support between healthcare facilities.

However, the number of primary missions has been increasing, underlining the importance of this resource in critical situations. "One of our first objectives was to change the mission profile. We now carry out more primary missions than secondary ones," notes Hugo Chambel.

Since the beginning of the year, the Heli Sul base in Évora has already completed around 230 missions, 160 of which were primary incidents, highlighting the growing importance of air transport in the medical emergency response, particularly in inland regions.

Whatever the scenario, the goal remains the same: getting there quickly and saving lives.

World.title: French teenager fined in Singapore for viral straw-licking prank
World.content:
Didier Gaspard Owen Maximilien, 19, was handed a SG$600 (406€) fine after admitting to posting to social media a video of himself putting a straw he had licked back into the dispenser of an orange juice vending machine.

 

Maximilien, who is studying in Singapore, posted a video of himself executing the prank on Instagram with the caption "city is not safe".

The clip went viral on Instagram shortly after the incident on March 12, triggering a backlash that led to his arrest in Singapore, which is known for its strict enforcement of public order and hygiene rules.

Handing down the sentence, Judge Kelly Ho said given Maximilien's "age and nature of the offence", alternatives such as probation or a community-based sentence would not be imposed.

Singapore justice fined French teenager 406€ after he pleaded guilty to a public nuisance charge. Copyright 2026 The Associated Press. All rights reserved.

Prosecutors agreed to the defence's proposal for a fine, saying the offence was at the "lower end" of its seriousness and while hygiene was compromised, no member of the public used the straw, so there "was no evidence of harm".

They added that Maximilien "pleaded guilty at the earliest possible opportunity."

In Singapore, public nuisance offenders face up to SG$2000 (1353€) fine and three months in jail.

"He is fully sorry for having caused all this trouble," Maximilien's defence counsel Kalidass Murugaiyan told the judge.

iJooz vending machines are a common sight in shopping districts, selling freshly-squeezed orange juice for SG$2 (1.35€) a cup. The company said it replaced all 500 straws in the machine dispenser after the teenager's prank.

Singapore is known for its no-nonsense approach to public stunts.

Last year it deported an Australian man at the end of a nine-day jail term for rushing film star Ariana Grande during the Asian premiere of "Wicked: For Good".

World.title: Samsung profit jumps 1,814% as South Korean tech giants benefit from global AI boom
World.content:
South Korean technology giant Samsung Electronics on Thursday reported a record operating profit of ₩89.5 trillion (€54 billion) for the April-to-June period, up 56% quarter on quarter and more than 19 times the level recorded a year earlier.

 

Based on Samsung’s published rounded figures, the semiconductor business’s operating profit rose to ₩89.2 trillion (€53.8 billion), 223 times its year-earlier level of ₩0.4 trillion (€241 million).

Samsung's semiconductor business benefited from rising chip prices driven by demand for AI servers and increased shipments of advanced high-bandwidth memory chips used to power AI applications. That outweighed an operating loss in its mobile, TV and home appliances division, partly due to higher component costs.

Samsung's quarterly revenue rose 28% quarter on quarter and 130% year on year to ₩171.5 trillion (€103.5 billion), an all-time high. The company said it expects demand for its memory products to remain strong in the second half of the year, driven by the continued expansion of AI infrastructure and the broader adoption of agentic AI. Demand for server chips is expected to accelerate further, keeping the market undersupplied, it said in a statement.

Samsung Electronics reported its results a day after rival SK Hynix also posted record quarterly revenue and operating profit, as the world's two largest memory chipmakers continue to ride the global artificial intelligence boom.

Despite their soaring profits, the companies' shares have fallen sharply this week in South Korea's volatile stock market, where retail investors often drive sharp swings in share prices, as concerns grow over their plans to spend heavily on expanding manufacturing capacity and the prospect of intensifying competition from China.

Chip shortages could worsen

Kim Jaejune, an executive vice-president of Samsung's memory chip division, said the company expects the gap between chip supply and demand to widen further in 2027. He said the shortage was expected to persist into 2028.

Samsung said its first semiconductor fabrication plant in Taylor, Texas, was on track to begin operations this year. The company also plans to break ground on a second factory, which could begin mass production in 2030.

Kim said Samsung has secured long-term chip supply contracts with the world's five largest data centre companies and is close to reaching agreements with five other major businesses. He did not identify any of them, but the Associated Press said the five companies could include Amazon Web Services, Google, Meta, Oracle and Microsoft.

"Despite our efforts to increase production, demand growth is outpacing our efforts," Kim said on a conference call.

Samsung and SK Hynix together produce about two-thirds of the world's memory chips. While the companies have embarked on major investments in semiconductor manufacturing facilities and data centres as South Korea expands its AI ambitions, some analysts say there are growing concerns about whether such massive spending will ultimately generate sufficient returns.

The chiefs of Samsung, SK and South Korean carmaker Hyundai joined President Lee Jae Myung on his San Francisco trip last week, where they announced hundreds of billions of dollars in planned cooperation with major US technology companies, including AI firms OpenAI and Anthropic and chip designers Nvidia and Broadcom. The agreements span chip technologies, data centres and other AI infrastructure.

At a roundtable with foreign media last week, Kim Yong-beom, Lee's chief policy adviser, said the initiatives reflect how global technology companies are rushing to secure long-term partnerships with South Korean chipmakers as they seek reliable supplies of memory chips for AI.

However, the volatility of the companies' share prices and those of other global tech firms shows that investors are shifting their focus from short-term earnings to long-term sustainability, Son In-joon, a semiconductor analyst at South Korea's Eugene Investment & Securities, said in a report this week.

World.title: ’Magical material’: How Europe’s drought-struck islands could soon harvest water from dry air
World.content:
When wells on his Ibiza property ran dry, Hashem Arouzi experienced Europe’s water crisis first hand.

 

The British entrepreneur set about to find a solution – not only for himself, but for the thousands of island-dwellers whose water supplies are dwindling due to drought, over-extraction and seawater intrusion.

“In Ibiza alone, there are more than 15,000 properties that are not connected to the water supply, and need to secure their own water,” says Arouzi. “The wells that have previously supplied them are running dry.”

Water deliveries by truck offer temporary reprieve but now even the reservoirs that supply them are running dry.

Desalination plants are increasingly coming to the rescue of mains-connected properties but off-grid homes are being left behind.

“This reflects a global challenge: around the world there are millions of homes that are off-grid and water-stressed – in areas where existing methods of water harvesting would struggle with arid conditions,” says Arouzi.

Machines that harvest drinking water from the air – even in hot and dry climates – could be a life-saving solution.

Making use of Nobel-winning water harvesting tech

As soon as next year, off-grid villas and hotels in the Mediterranean and Balearics could be bolstering their water supplies with tech that achieves just this.

Unveiled today (30 July) in Barcelona, the ARK is a plug-and-play device by Arouzi’s climate tech company Ahbstra that the company claims is capable of harvesting up to 500 litres of water a day from the air.

Its secret weapon? Breakthrough molecular chemistry that was awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 2025.

Metal-Organic Frameworks, or MOFs, feature an innovative molecular structure engineered to have a huge internal surface area – the equivalent of a whole football pitch in one gram of material.

The structures are the result of the decades-long work of three scientists: Susumu Kitagawa from Kyoto University in Japan, Richard Robson from the University of Melbourne in Australia, and Omar M. Yaghi from the University of California, Berkeley, in the United States.

The Ahbstra ARK was unveiled n Barcelona on 30 July. Ahbstra

How does MOF-based water harvesting work?

With large cavities in which molecules can flow in and out, MOFs can be used to separate pollutants from water and extract carbon dioxide or water from the air.

Conventional atmospheric water generators (AWGs) work like dehumidifiers, cooling air down to its dew point to create water condensation. At low humidity, the dew point drops, often making it unviable to cool the air sufficiently.

MOFs on the other hand are adsorbents, not condensers, meaning they can hold molecules of gas or liquid on their surface. This allows them to physically bind water vapour molecules directly out of low-humidity air, without the need for energy-intensive deep cooling.

A modest amount of heat is needed to release the captured water as liquid.

Yaghi's own company, Atoco, unveiled the world's first MOF-based water harvester in February 2026, with orders opening later this year.

Capable of producing up to 1,000 litres a day using only ambient thermal energy, the units – roughly the size of a shipping container – could be a lifeline for disaster hit communities, as well as providing resource-hungry data centres with water generated using waste heat.

How a ‘magic material’ could ease off-grid water stress

“For years, MOFs have been a ‘magic material’ on the cusp of delivering vital results for the environment, from water harvesting to carbon capture,” says Arouzi.

But their high energy requirements previously made their use unviable at scale.

Ahbstra says it addresses this with its patented Suspended Particle Reactor, which cycles air through MOF granules in a fluidised state to maximise their performance.

Priced at £150,000 (around €175,000), the company's units still aren’t cheap – but they could be invaluable for properties that are at risk of being devalued or abandoned due to a lack of water security, the developers say.

Water from the ARK can be used to replenish wells and cisterns, or be sent directly to a property’s mains water system.

Both Ahbstra and Atoco are currently developing systems for smaller water volumes, too.

Part of a whole-system approach to water stress

This summer, successive heatwaves and droughts have subjected many southern European countries to severe water shortages, with around 30 per cent of people facing permanent water stress across the region, according to the European Environment Agency.

“It’s clear that weather and rainfall patterns are changing, leading to more extreme and prolonged drought conditions in many places,” says Richard Perkin, CTO of Ahbstra. “Tackling this requires a whole-system approach, from water efficiency to recycling and better infrastructure.”

But if dams or wells are dry, they can only be refilled when it rains in the right place, no matter how responsibly the water is managed.

“This is why atmospheric water harvesting is a necessary part of the response,” he says.

Independent, peer-reviewed data on the ARK’s real-world performance and durability is not yet available.

World.title: Will the ‘coolcation’ travel trend change the geography of international tourism?
World.content:
This summer, amid scorching heatwaves, travellers are looking beyond the usual Mediterranean destinations in hopes of cooler escapes. But will this only be a one-off summer, or mark a durable shift in the tourism market?

 

With temperatures in the European summer now climbing up towards 40C, the trend of seeking out cool has now become cool.

This year, visitors "have been telling me that they have escaped the heat in southern parts of Europe”, said Terje Viblom Pedersen, a guide who offers tours in southeastern Sweden.

They are “just amazed" by the daytime high temperatures under 30C and sea breezes, as well as the lack of crowds compared to tourist hotspots in southern Europe.

"It's good to have escaped the heatwave," said Daniel and Florence Gastaldi, two French tourists on a tour of Stockholm's Old Town. "We're happy to have found cooler temperatures," added the recently retired couple from the southern French city of Marseille.

The "coolcations" travel trend – holidays in a cooler climate – has been gathering pace in recent years and appears to have exploded in 2026.

Research by Mabrian and Data Appeal found a rising appeal for northern regions such as southern Finland and Vestland in Norway. Travellers are also favouring northern areas of European countries further south, such as Galicia in Spain, Trentino-Alto Adige in Italy and Normandy and Alsace in France.

On the French version of Hotels.com, searches for rooms in the Danish capital of Copenhagen have jumped by 246% since the first heatwave struck France in May. Those for Dublin in Ireland have risen by 151%. The trend is not limited to France.

Jonna Robertson, a trip advisor at New York-based Fora Travel, said she had observed the phenomenon in the United States, which has also seen its share of sweltering weather.

"Oslo has seen booking growth of 154% year-over-year, Helsinki 124%,” said the expert and founder of Coolcation Adventures. “Those numbers tell me that travellers are actively looking beyond the traditional summer hotspots."

In France, industry experts say they have seen the growing popularity of mountain resorts during the summer.

"That's because at higher altitudes there is a clear drop in temperatures in the evening and during the night, which makes the stays much more liveable," said Jean-Pascal Chopard, head of the tourism body for the mountainous Jura region.

Southern Europe’s popularity remains

But will this current enthusiasm actually change the geography of international tourism?

Travellers' choices depend on a whole range of different factors, not least pricing, experts point out.

And southern Europe, which is traditionally cheaper than the north, remains at the top of the most popular destinations.

"All European countries have recorded an increase in tourist arrivals, and there is no discernible trend linked to the heat," Swedish professor Stefan Gossling, a tourism specialist, told AFP.

"Temperature is one aspect people take into account when they go on vacation. But there are many other elements. Italy is not Denmark in terms of culture, environment, prices. All of that means people don't easily change destinations when they have a favourite.”

Norway's tourism promotion agency agreed. "Our recent visitor surveys show that around one in five foreign tourists considers cooler summer temperatures to be one of the reasons for choosing Norway," it said.

However, "climate is only one of many factors that influence travel decisions", it argued.

Security, nature, accessibility, air connections and exchange rates also play a role and Mediterranean countries have very extensive tourism infrastructures.

High footfall continues to showcase the popularity of Europe’s warmer climates.

Greece, for example, had its best year ever in terms of visitor numbers last year, as did Spain.

In Spain, spending by domestic and foreign tourists has already risen by more than 8% in the second quarter of 2026, according to data published recently by Exceltur, an organisation that brings together the main Spanish tourism companies.

Fora's Robertson, for her part, is counting on a seasonal redistribution, with trips to hotter countries taking place in spring or autumn, in order to avoid both overtourism and exhausting temperatures.

World.title: US resumes direct attacks on Iran one day after its foiled strikes on Jordanian bases hosting American troops
World.content:
The US military announced early on Thursday it had completed “a heavy wave of strikes against Iran” conducted in response to earlier Iranian attacks on a US base in Jordan.

 

The latest barrage came after the US partnered with Saudi Arabia to strike Iran-backed militias in neighbouring Iraq, killing at least 20 fighters and six Iranian advisers.

The US Central Command said in a post on social media that over a two hour period, the US struck “dozens” of targets belonging to Iran’s Revolutionary Guard Corps, including military command centres as well as missile and drone facilities, coastal surveillance and defence sites.

The new strikes came hours after US President Donald Trump vowed to hit Iran “very hard” after it targeted a base in Jordan that hosts US troops.

Iranian state media said two people were injured in attacks on the island of Qeshm in the Strait of Hormuz and that explosions were also reported in Khuzestan province, west of the country, neighbouring Iraq and Kuwait.

Elsewhere, drone strikes ignited fires on two natural gas vessels at the Egyptian port of Damietta, according to UK maritime security firm Ambrey.

It was not immediately clear who was responsible for the strikes on a US-owned floating storage facility and a Greek-owned tanker at the port, though no injuries were reported.

The flare-ups on multiple fronts after several days of relative calm raised the risk of a return to all-out war. It also underscored the difficulty of winding down a five-month conflict that has jolted the world economy and is unpopular domestically among Americans.

The fighting was also likely to raise concerns that Washington is further drawing down already diminished stockpiles of sophisticated munitions needed to defend its bases and allies.

A damaged vehicle at the site of an airstrike on a Popular Mobilization Forces base in Mosul, Iraq, Wednesday, July 29, 2026 Farid Abdulwahed/Copyright 2026 The AP. All rights reserved.

Egypt, a close US ally and regional mediator, is one of the only countries in the Middle East to have been spared direct military action during the war. A strike by Iran or its allies, if confirmed, would mark a significant widening of the conflict, which has already spilled over to several states.

Asked during an Oval Office event if Iran was responsible for the strikes on the natural gas vessels, Trump responded: “It's a little more of the same.”

“In the meantime, we’re going to be hitting them very hard because it’s our turn to hit them," he added.

Saudi Arabia had accused the Iraqi militias of firing drones against its oil facilities over the past two days.

This satellite image provided by Planet Labs PBC on July 27, 2026 shows smoke rising from the Saudi Aramco oil processing facility in Abqaiq, Saudi Arabia, 2026 Planet Labs PBC/Planet Labs PBC via AP

An umbrella group of Iraqi militias initially denied the allegations, while another Iran-backed group — the Houthi rebels in Yemen — said they had attacked Saudi energy facilities as part of a separate but related conflict.

Before the latest eruption, mediators had expressed optimism about bringing the US and Iran back to the negotiating table.

An interim agreement, signed in June, collapsed in recent weeks over renewed fighting in the Strait of Hormuz, a crucial waterway for global energy supplies that Iranian attacks have again effectively closed.

A regional official said mediators are “still trying with both sides” to restore calm and get the ceasefire back on track, but gave no details on whether progress was being made in the closed-door diplomatic attempts.

World.title: French student fined over Singapore straw licking prank
World.content:
A social media stunt involving a single straw has left a French student facing a hefty fine — and possible consequences for his right to remain in Singapore.

A French student has been fined 600 Singapore dollars (€400, $458) after licking a drinking straw and returning it to a dispenser in a prank filmed for social media.

The 19-year-old, Didier Gaspard Owen Maximilien, pleaded guilty to a public nuisance charge.

He avoided a possible prison sentence, but it remains unclear whether authorities will revoke his student pass. The French national studies at Singapore's ESSEC Business School.

What did the student do and why?

Maximilien removed a straw from a freshly squeezed orange juice vending machine in March, licked it and placed it back in the dispenser.

He filmed the stunt for an Instagram story, and the video later went viral.

An employee of the company operating the machine saw the footage and contacted police. As a result, all 500 straws in the dispenser had to be replaced.

The direct cost amounted to just 5 Singapore dollars, or around €3.30, according to court documents, but the case attracted nationwide attention.

Maximilien could have faced several months in prison, a fine, or both after being convicted of disturbing public order.

His lawyer told the court that he was remorseful and now understood that an apparently harmless prank could have far-reaching consequences.

Singapore's strict public-order laws

The wealthy city-state is known for its strict laws and rigorous enforcement, with cleanliness and tightly regulated public spaces forming part of its image for decades.

The import of chewing gum, for example, remains largely prohibited as part of efforts to prevent littering and vandalism.

Singapore also retains judicial caning for certain serious offenses, although the punishment was not applicable in the student's case.

World.title: Australia: Telegram faces legal action over failure to remove terrorist content
World.content:
Australia says videos of terrorist executions and mass shootings weren't removed from Telegram after they were reported. The move comes a day after Russia charged founder Pavel Durov with facilitating terrorist activity.

Telegram is facing a possible AU$54.6 million ($38 million, €33 million) fine in Australia as a regulator said on Thursday the messaging platform failed to remove terrorist content despite warnings.

What are the accusations against Telegram in Australia?

Australia's online safety regulator, the eSafety Commissioner, said it had begun action after videos of terrorist executions, mass shootings and other extremist material linked to attacks including the 2019 Christchurch mosque shootings and the 2022 Buffalo supermarket shooting continued to exist on Telegram.

"We allege ​that this content remained accessible on the service long after Telegram ​had been put on notice," eSafety Commissioner Julie Inman Grant said in a statement.

The regulator said Telegram failed to remove pro-terror content between July and October 2025 or suspend the accounts responsible, despite users reporting the content and its disseminators.

"This action comes at a time when Australia is experiencing a heightened security environment against the fresh backdrop of the Bondi tragedy," Grant said, a reference to an antisemitic mass shooting at a Sydney beach that killed 15 people last year.

Telegram denied the allegations and said it would contest the case in court, adding that it had blocked thousands of extremist communities in 2026.

Ukrainians turn to Telegram, social media for news To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Russia charges Telegram founder Durov with aiding terrorism

The court action comes a day after Russia charged Telegram's billionaire founder Pavel Durov with facilitating terrorist activity.

Russia's Federal Security Service issued an international warrant for his arrest, alleging the platform was used by Ukrainian operatives to organize attacks inside Russia.

Soon after the news of the warrant broke, Telegram's account on X posted a picture of Durov giving a middle finger to the camera.

The Russian-born billionaire Durov, now based in Dubai, built the Telegram messaging app with his brother Nikolai and launched it in 2013. The platform currently boasts over a billion monthly active users.

World.title: Spain: Hundreds of migrants attempt to swim toward Ceuta
World.content:
Spain's Civil Guard, maritime Rescue Services and the Red Cross said they rescued migrants from the water. The interior minister acknowledged the country was facing an "extraordinary, exceptional situation."

Spanish authorities said on Wednesday that hundreds of migrants swam from Morocco attempting to reach the territory of Ceuta.

Border security was overwhelmed by the action, as it did not expect the surge.

What do we know about the migrant attempts to reach Ceuta?

"In the last few days, more than 1,500 migrants, including adults and minors, have reached Ceuta by sea,” the leader of Ceuta's government, Juan Jesus Vivas, told journalists.

"The reception centers are collapsed and saturated," he added.

Spain's Civil Guard, maritime Rescue Services and the Red Cross reportedly rescued some 117 migrants from the water.

Moroccan authorities also reportedly grabbed dozens from the water on their way to Spanish waters.

Interior Minister Fernando Grande-Marlaska told Spanish television channel laSexta that authorities were facing "an extraordinary, exceptional situation."

Grande-Marlaska added that "we are dealing with it with the means that we already have deployed there permanently."

He praised Moroccan authorities for their involvement, saying they were cooperating and that the relationship with the kingdom was "close and based on loyalty."

Ceuta: Spain's North African exclave sees migration surge To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Mostly Moroccans seeking to swim across

The Spanish government did not confirm exactly how many migrants had reached the territory by swimming.

It also remains unclear why so many people sought to swim toward Spanish territory.

The swimmers were mostly Moroccans, along with a small number of Algerians who had been living in Morocco while trying to migrate to Europe, according to activists in Morocco and Ceuta.

The incident follows a Spanish Supreme Court ruling earlier this month which established that migrants arriving by sea cannot be immediately pushed back across the border without due process, unlike those crossing by land.

However, activists have discounted the probability that average Moroccans including those swimming toward Ceuta would be aware of such a ruling, dismissing a link between the ruling and the crossings.

Spain offers legal status to migrants To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Migrant arrivals in Spain through the Mediterranean enclaves Ceuta and Melilla, were lower this year compared to the same time last year, as many migrants have sought other routes like the Canary Islands.

World.title: Explosions in Kyiv after Zelenskyy warns of Russian strikes
World.content:
At least one person was killed in a Russian air strike on Ukraine's capital, Kyiv. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy had warned that Russia had "prepared a massive attack," citing air force reports.

At least one person was killed in a Russian airstrike on Kyiv, the capital of Ukraine, the city's military administration said on Thursday.

Explosions were reported over the Ukrainian capital Kyiv in the early hours of Thursday, after Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned that Russia might conduct a "massive attack."

Both the Reuters and AFP news agency cited people on the ground as saying they heard explosions.

"Sadly, one death has been confirmed," the Kyiv city military administration wrote on Telegram in the early hours of Thursday.

Russia has struck Kyiv with ballistic missiles, said the city's mayor, Vitaly Klitschko, urging people to seek shelter. He added that a few non-residential sites in Kyiv caught fire.

"The enemy is attacking the capital with ballistic weapons. The threat of further attack remains present. Stay in shelters!" Klitschko said.

Several people killed in Kryvyi Rih

Russia also attacked other Ukrainian cities overnight. At least six people, including two girls, were killed in a Russian missile strike on the central Ukrainian city of Kryvyi Rih, according to the head of the local military administration.

"In a village on the outskirts of Kryvyi Rih, a direct strike by an Iskander-M ballistic missile, launched from Voronezh, hit a private house where a large family lived, killing girls aged five and 12 and four adults," Oleksandr Vilkul said.

He added that a further eight people were wounded and that the death toll may rise.

Russian missiles also damaged two apartment buildings and injured six people in Lviv, a city in western Ukraine close to the Polish border, according to local officials.

Meanwhile, the Polish Armed Forces announced on X that Poland had scrambled its fighter jets on Thursday to protect its airspace amid Russian air strikes on Ukraine.

"Fighter aircraft and an early warning aircraft have begun operations while ground-based air defense systems and radar reconnaissance systems have reached a state of readiness," the post said, adding that the actions are of a preventive nature.

What did Zelenskyy say ahead of the Kyiv explosions?

The strikes come as Zelenskyy had warned of a "high probability that the strike will be carried out tonight."

"I received a report from Air Force Commander Anatolii Kryvonozhko. The Russians prepared a massive attack several days ago," Zelenskyy said on X.

The Ukrainian president stressed that Ukrainians' safety depended on the willingness of Kyiv's allies to provide anti-missile defenses. His statements came on the heels of a trip to the US where he said President Donald Trump had agreed to give Ukraine licenses for Patriot missiles.

World.title: Report finds 2025 was deadliest year for antisemitic attacks outside Israel
World.content:
Germany had the highest number of antisemitic incidents in 2025, both in absolute and relative terms, a report has found.

A report released on Wednesday by the J7 Large Communities' Task Force Against Antisemitism group found a record rise in antisemitic attacks worldwide.

J7 looked at Jewish communities in Argentina, Australia, Canada, France, Germany, Britain and the United States, which together are home to more than 90% of Jewish people outside of Israel.

The report highlighted that some 20 people were murdered in antisemitic attacks in Australia, the UK and the US in 2025, in what was "the deadliest year for antisemitic attacks in the diaspora... since the AMIA attack in Buenos Aires in 1994," the report said.

The AMIA attack was a bombing that targeted a Jewish community center, leaving 85 people killed.

The deadliest event in 2025 was the mass shooting at a Hanukkah festival near Australia's Bondi Beach, where 15 people were killed.

"Antisemitism in our seven countries is no longer a surge; it is our new normal," the J7 task force said in a statement.

"Governments must stop reacting after Jews are attacked and start acting before, with real security funding, stronger laws and social media platforms that enforce their own rules," the statement said.

J7's report found more than 23,000 antisemitic incidents across the seven countries in 2025, a sharp rise from the 9,800 that were recorded in 2022.

Gaza war remains a factor

The report highlighted that anti-Zionism appeared to be a key motivating factor for the rise in antisemitism, accounting for 48% of incidents in Britain and 45% in the US.

According to the report, incidents increased in the years after the Gaza war, which was triggered after Hamas's deadly October 7 attack in 2023.

The report found a rise of 136% in antisemitic incidents from 2022 to 2025.

Although the total number of incidents fell from 2024 to 2025, the figure remains well above pre-October 7, 2023, levels, the report said.

Germany tops list of antisemitic attacks

While Australia topped the seven countries in terms of the sharp rise in antisemitic incidents, Germany stood out as the one with the highest number of antisemitic incidents, both in absolute and relative terms, the report found, nearly five times Australia's rate.



In 2025, there were nearly 70 incidents per 1,000 Jewish residents, with a total number of 8,725 cases up from 8,713 in 2024 and 2,610 in 2022

Right-wing extremism caused 807 of the total cases, up from 562 in 2024.

Meanwhile, the number of antisemitic attacks attributed to left-wing, anti-imperialist extremism also rose from 349 to 501 cases. Islamist extremist-linked incidents rose from 143 to 166.

The report found that "anti-Israel activism" accounted for 22.6% of all recorded incidents in Germany in 2025.

Josef Schuster, president of the German Central Council of Jews in Germany, said the numbers represented an "ongoing normalization of antisemitism" in Germany.

Schuster called on lawmakers "to close existing loopholes in criminal law and consistently criminalize calls for the destruction of the State of Israel."
